meta.title: TriLand – Transgraniczne Centrum Transformacji

card.solution: Obszar wsparcia, region polsko-saksońskiego pogranicza, przechodzi głęboki proces transformacji. Zmiany klimatyczne i środowiskowe, odnawialne źródła energii i przewidywalne wyjście z wydobycia węgla, starzenie się społeczeństwa i migracja, zwłaszcza dobrze wykształconych grup ludności w wieku produkcyjnym, zmiany społeczne, cyfryzacja i zmieniające się warunki pracy stanowią nakładające się na siebie i złożone wyzwania w obszarze wsparcia. Pomimo że wyzwania po obu stronach granicy różnią się w szczegółach, region jest mocno powiązany. Intensyfikacja współpracy transgranicznej w ramach projektu TriLand przyczyni się do wykorzystania doświadczeń po obu stronach granicy w celu wypracowania dobrych praktyk oraz uniknięcia powtórzenia błędów z przeszłości. Celem ogólnym projektu TriLand jest promowanie zrównoważonego rozwoju oraz zwiększenie konkurencyjności obszaru objętego wsparciem w związku z transformacją energetyczną i wyjściem z wydobycia węgla. Cele szczegółowe projektu obejmują: 1. Budowanie zdolności decyzyjnych u decydentów w celu radzenia sobie z obecnymi i przyszłymi wyzwaniami procesu transformacyjnego w regionie w zakresie demografii, rynku pracy, gospodarki, środowiska naturalnego i zmian klimatycznych oraz dziedzictwa przyrodniczego i kulturowego. 2. Wykorzystanie i połączenie wiedzy po stronie polskiej i niemieckiej oraz między sektorami (polityka, administracja, gospodarka, społeczeństwo obywatelskie, nauka). 3. Budowanie i ustanowienie platformy dla lepszej koordynacji poziomej (niemiecko-polskiej) i pionowej (między sektorami i poziomami administracji) oraz dla intensyfikacji współpracy instytucji transgranicznej. Te cele stanowią istotny wkład w osiągnięcie konkretnego celu programu w priorytecie 3. /Das Fördergebiet, die sächsisch-polnische Grenzregion, durchläuft einen tiefgreifenden Transformationsprozess. Klimawandel und Umweltveränderungen, erneuerbare Energien und der absehbare Ausstieg aus dem Kohlebergbau, Bevölkerungsalterung und Abwanderung, insbesondere von gut ausgebildeten Gruppen der Erwerbsbevölkerung, sozialer Wandel, Digitalisierung und veränderte Arbeitsbedingungen sind allesamt sich überschneidende und komplexe Herausforderungen im Fördergebiet. Obwohl sich die Herausforderungen auf beiden Seiten der Grenze im Detail unterschiedlich darstellen, ist die Region eng verflochten. Die Intensivierung der grenzüberschreitenden Zusammenarbeit im Rahmen des TriLand-Projekts wird dazu beitragen, die Erfahrungen auf beiden Seiten der Grenze zu nutzen, um bewährte Verfahren zu entwickeln und die Wiederholung von Fehlern in der Vergangenheit zu vermeiden. Das übergeordnete (politische) Ziel des TriLand-Projekts ist die Förderung einer nachhaltigen Entwicklung und die Steigerung der Wettbewerbsfähigkeit des Fördergebiets im Hinblick auf die Energiewende und den Kohleausstieg. Zu den spezifischen Zielen des Projekts gehören: 1. Kapazitätsaufbau bei den Entscheidungsträgern, um die aktuellen und künftigen Herausforderungen des regionalen Transformationsprozesses in Bezug auf Demografie, Arbeitsmarkt, Wirtschaft, Umwelt und Klimawandel sowie Natur- und Kulturerbe bewältigen zu können. 2. Nutzung und Verknüpfung der Wissensbestände auf polnischer und deutscher Seite sowie zwischen den Sektoren (Politik, Verwaltung, Wirtschaft, Zivilgesellschaft, Wissenschaft). 3. Aufbau und Etablierung einer Plattform zur besseren horizontalen (deutsch-polnischen) und vertikalen (zwischen den Sektoren und Verwaltungsebenen) Koordinierung und zur Intensivierung der Zusammenarbeit zwischen grenzüberschreitenden Institutionen. Diese Ziele leisten einen wichtigen Beitrag zum spezifischen Ziel des Programms im Rahmen der Priorität 3.

meta.title: Joint promotion and implementation of activities related to climate change resilience - natural disasters and fires
meta.institution: Provincial Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Lublin

card.solution: The common challenge of the Ukrainian and Polish sides in the border area, and at the same time the main goal of the project, is to support actions aimed at adapting to climate change and preventing the risks associated with natural disasters and catastrophes in the cross-border area of PL-UA. The implementation of the project addresses the problem of rapidly progressing climate change, including the threats associated with natural disasters. These phenomena require the partners' rescue capabilities to be adapted to carry out tasks related to these changes. In order to solve these problems, it is necessary to equip the existing transport base and rescue equipment so that rescue operations can be carried out properly. The project partners have identified three main problems: 1. Increasing threats resulting from climate change-induced natural disasters. 2. Insufficient rescue and firefighting potential of rescue units (facilities and competencies) to support actions aimed at adapting to climate change and natural disasters. 3. Lack of sufficient exchange of experience and cooperation between rescue units in the cross-border area to effectively manage crisis situations related to natural disasters and adapt to climate change. The planned tasks within the project will contribute to improving the effectiveness of rescue and firefighting services in the cross-border area of Poland and Ukraine in preventing the risks associated with natural disasters and catastrophes. As a result, the main project products will be equipment for rescue units, which will be purchased by the Main Department of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine in the Volyn Region in Ukraine and the Provincial Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Lublin. On the Polish side, the equipment will be used by the subordinate units: •2 operational pickup trucks with IT equipment setup – 2 units: Provincial Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Lublin, Municipal Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Zamość •Set of personal rescue equipment for operations in hard-to-reach areas – Municipal Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Zamość •Heavy rescue and firefighting vehicle – Municipal Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Lublin •Medium rescue and firefighting vehicle – Municipal Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Zamość •4x4 bus with specialized equipment – Municipal Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Lublin A mast point system will be installed in the Tomaszów, Hrubieszów, Chełm, Włodawa and Biała counties. The property owners have confirmed that they are granting permission for the installation of radios with associated equipment on their land. No permits are required for the installation of this equipment. The project also includes the reconstruction of the Training and Practical Center for Fire Volunteer Training and Rescue Training Center at 17a Rescuers Heroes Street in Lutsk for the Main Department of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine in the Volyn Region on the Ukrainian side. Additionally, project outputs will also include promotional and training materials. Overall, the project will equip and provide resources to rescue and firefighting units and train the personnel. Through these actions, the project will contribute to addressing climate change and improving the safety of residents, property, and the environment in the cross-border area of Poland and Ukraine. The project creates a solid foundation for future cooperation between rescuers in the cross-border area of Poland and Ukraine. The residents of the provinces in both regions covered by the project will be better protected from the consequences of natural disasters and catastrophes resulting from advancing climate change. Moreover, Polish and Ukrainian rescue units will enhance the potential response to a disaster in this region. The implementation of the project will establish a strong basis for further development of cross-border cooperation.

meta.title: Joint actions in the Siedlce-Ostrołęka Subregion and Volyn Oblast to prepare emergency services for combating fires, natural disasters, and other climate change-related hazards

card.solution: The common challenge for the Ukrainian and Polish sides of the border area, and also the main goal of the project, is to support actions aimed at climate change adaptation and prevention of risks associated with natural disasters in the cross-border area of Poland and Ukraine. The Lead Partner of the project is the Siedlce Municipality (LP), and the project partners are the Main Department of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine in the Volyn region (P2), the Municipal Headquarters of the State Fire Service in Siedlce (P3), and the Zbuczyn Commune (P4). The roles have been assigned in this way because the Siedlce Municipality has the most experience in implementing and managing EU projects. LP, P2 and P3 have already cooperated on a project in the framework of Interreg PBU 2014-20. The project's implementation addresses the rapidly advancing climate change and the resulting hazards related to natural disasters, which necessitate adapting the rescue potential of the project partners to the tasks associated with these changes. The project partners have identified three main issues: 1. Increasing threats resulting from climate change caused by natural disasters. 2. Insufficient rescue and firefighting capacity of the rescue units (equipment and competencies) to support climate change adaptation measures. 3. Inadequate exchange of experiences and cooperation between rescue units in the cross-border area to effectively manage crisis situations related to natural disasters and climate change adaptation. To ensure a comprehensive approach to the identified problems, the partners plan soft and investment actions. The project includes the following tasks: • Investment actions (purchase of rescue and firefighting equipment and alarms) • Organization of joint training for emergency rescue and firefighting services • Organization of a joint promotional campaign • Joint project management The planned tasks within the project will enhance the effectiveness of the cross-border emergency rescue and firefighting services in Poland and Ukraine in preventing risks associated with natural disasters. The project's main output will be the rescue and firefighting equipment acquired by the partners within the project: LP: • Central alarm system for siren control + 2 sirens (1 set) P2: • Pump-hose firefighting vehicle 6x6 (1 unit) • Water tanker for drinking water transportation (1 unit) • Specialized vehicle (2 units) P3: • Heavy firefighting vehicle GCBM 23 (firefighting tanker) (1 unit) • Light Sbus-type vehicle for transporting rescuers (1 unit) • Low-bed trailer with ramps for loader transportation (1 unit) • UTV-type vehicle with rescue trailer (1 unit) • Water scooter with rescue platform and trailer (1 unit) • Flat-bottomed aluminum rescue boat with engine and trailer (1 unit) P4: • Medium-sized 4x4 rescue and firefighting vehicle (1 unit) Additionally, the project will involve specialized training for the emergency rescue and firefighting services on both sides of the border (2 trainings in UA and 1 training in PL). Each training will involve 70 participants. Furthermore, the project will produce promotional materials and training materials. Overall, the project will equip and supply the rescue and firefighting units and provide training for the personnel. The project establishes a solid foundation for future cooperation among rescuers in the cross-border area of Poland and Ukraine. The residents of both regions covered by the project will be better protected from the consequences of natural disasters and the progressing climate change. Additionally, the Polish and Ukrainian rescue units will enhance their potential response to potential disasters in the region. The project's implementation creates a strong basis for further development of cross-border cooperation.

meta.title: JOINT EFFORTS ENHANCING CROSS-BORDER DISASTER RESPONSE CAPACITY

card.solution: Significant challenges for the Project area are prevention, detection and warning of natural and anthropogenic hazards. Fire and disasters do not stop at borders and neither does their impact. Firefighting units in Wizna and Ternopil district deal with a wide variety of risks - from firefighting to providing specialized services, such as technical rescue, emergency medical services, hazardous materials mitigation, etc. Fire rescue services together with cross-border local authorities they have a crucial role to play in strengthening the resilience of their populations and critical infrastructure networks and remain the ultimate warranty when capacities of resilience are disrupted at any level. Local authorities also must provide robust leadership in emergency management. In fact the common emergency problems are inherent for the Polish-Ukrainian cross-border area. What is shown in the document titled “Socio – economic analysis of the programme area INTERREG NEXT POLAND – BELARUS – UKRAINE 2021 -2027” identifying the major weaknesses in terms safety and cooperation issues: - Differences in procedures between countries; - Lack of cross-border rescue procedures; - Low awareness of residents in the field of safety; - Insufficient public information about various types of danger (infectious diseases, fire safety, etc.); The main target groups of the Project are fire rescue units and local authorities of cross-border area. Final beneficiaries: borderland residents and travelling people benefiting from enhanced fire and disaster security. Overall objective of the project is to increase efficiency of joint actions of participating authorities through the strengthening of staff’ and equipment’ capacities of the fire rescue squads from the PL-UA cross-border area. Specific objectives 1. to develop the competences and skills of the firefighters from Poland and Ukraine, 2. to generate and maintain a cross-border cooperation mechanism between the firefighters in two counties, 3. to enhance operational response capacities of the Polish and Ukrainian firefighting units Partners will carry out necessary purchases of equipment strengthening the cross-border emergency response capacity. Joint trainings will increase firefighters’ skills and efficiency of joint operations. Project develops a cooperation potential within borderland’s emergency response sector through 2 joint sessions of Cross-border Risk Management Workshop and elaboration of the “Cross-border Risk Management Strategy”. Established Cross-border Partnership for Disaster Risk Management – a long-term cooperation network to exchange of tools and good practices among Polish and Ukrainian emergency management stakeholders will work to strengthen expertise in cross-border disaster risk reduction among its members to improve the quality of programmes, Cooperation links set during the joint preparation and organization of project events will pay off in future with a new ideas and new joint solutions for cross-border emergency issues. Achievement of the Project outputs requires close cooperation between the Partners and is not possible without it. Same as sustainability and maintenance of Project’s results. Project outputs will help to establish a region geared to needs and challenges of natural and man-made threats, as well as civilisation, political and institutional changes. Project translates the EU's wish to build on common interests with neighbouring Ukrainian regions to build effective partnership between Polish and Ukrainian Partners towards a stable EU Neighbourhood in political, security and socio-economic terms. By promoting climate change adaptation and disaster risk prevention and resilience Project complements the Programme specific objective RSO2.4. Promoting climate change adaptation and disaster risk prevention and resilience, taking into account eco-system based approaches.

meta.title: FIRE SAFETY AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT SOLUTION FOR POLISH AND UKRAINIAN CROSS-BORDER COMMUNITIES

card.solution: Polish and Ukrainian neighbouring regions have much in common in terms of socio-economic standing and natural resources. However, despite these shared interests, there has been a lack of concrete efforts to coordinate approaches between the regions. Despite the borders that sometimes divide territories, the impact of fire is consistent across Europe, thus also across PL-UA border area. Because fire and disasters do not stop at borders and neither does their impact. Cross-border local authorities as the Applicant Stawiski Municipality and state fire rescue units as Partner 1 Main Department of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine in Ternopil Oblast have a crucial role to play in strengthening the resilience of their populations and critical infrastructure networks and remain the ultimate warranty when capacities of resilience are disrupted at any level. The Project builds awareness and appreciation of the importance of emergency infrastructure and reaffirms the cross-border commitment to keep the critical infrastructure and borderland’s communities safe and secure. Securing the cross-border infrastructure connects people and supports the critical infrastructure systems of borderland, is a trans-national priority that requires planning and coordination across the whole borderland community The main target groups of the Project are supported local authorities and institutions of cross-border emergency system, equipped fire rescue brigades and participants of the training events: fire rescuers and emergency sector stakeholders. Final beneficiaries: population of the borderland benefiting from developed public safety, as well as borderland residents, tourists and travelling people. Overall objective: Improvement of the institutional capacity to prevent and coordinate the management system for emergency situations. Specific objectives: 1. Improvement of competences and skills by joint trainings on the prevention of emergency situations. 2. Strengthening the institutional potential of cooperation between rescue services 3. Enhancing response capacity of fire rescue services through the purchase of specialized equipment. The enhancement of emergency response operational capabilities will be ensured by provision of safety equipment, such as 3 firefighting trucks and mobile firefighting ladder. The development of professional competences will be achieved by carrying out the 4 joint trainings for 120 firefighters and 2 “Cross-border Civil Protection Networking Workshops” for 40 cross-border civil protection stakeholders. Improvements in the disaster risk governance will be achieved by preparation of strategic document ‘STATE OF THE ART OF CROSS-BORDER DISASTER MANAGEMENT’ establishment of Cross-border Civil Protection and Safety Alliance - a joint initiative between borderland emergency policy and disaster risk governance stakeholders creates a basis for further cooperation within the joint cross-border emergency management system. The direct cross-border impact comes from engagement of the Partners in the preparation and implementation of the project. meta.title: Activities for the prevention of catastrophes and natural disasters in Polish and Ukrainian municipalities

card.solution: The strategic goal of the SAFETY4US project is to significantly enhance the resilience and operational capacity of the civil protection systems in the cross-border area of Poland and Ukraine against climate-related and anthropogenic threats, particularly fires and natural disasters. This will be achieved by: - Substantially upgrading the technical equipment and infrastructure of local fire and rescue services across all partner communes. - Strengthening cross-border cooperation and joint response capabilities through shared training, exercises, and the development of common methodologies. - Increasing public awareness and preparedness, especially among youth, through targeted educational activities and the dissemination of joint knowledge products in the field of first aid and procedures for natural hazards, disasters and attacks. The project is a direct response to identified critical needs, including obsolete firefighting equipment, long emergency response times, deficiencies in hazard warning systems, and insufficient public knowledge on disaster prevention, which are exacerbated by the increasing frequency and severity of natural disasters and the specific security challenges in the region. Partnership: The project brings together a dedicated cross-border partnership: - Lead Partner: Puchaczów Commune (Poland) - Project Partners (PPs): Ludwin Commune (Poland), Executive Committee of Liublynets Settlement Council (Ukraine), Ustyluh Town Council (Ukraine) Main Project Outputs: - Equipment & Infrastructure: - Purchase of 5 fire trucks, 1 quad and 1 rescue boat equipped for rescue and disaster recovery. - Purchase of extensive rescue equipment, protective gear for firefighters, drones. - Installation of fire alarm systems in 7 public institutions in Liublynets. - Reconstruction and equipping of a modern Safety Center in Ustyluh Joint Knowledge & Cooperation: - Development and publication of a trilingual (PL-UA printed EN online published) methodological manual for training citizens and volunteer firefighters piloting by pilot action in Ustyluh to test and refine the methodological manual. - A series of cross-border training sessions, including i.e. youth training, professional firefighter training, an integration study visit for youth rescue teams, pilot actions to check the methodology of education. Enhanced Protection Coverage: - An area of 38,454.96 ha will be covered by improved protection measures - Over 25,000 citizens will benefit from enhanced protection against natural and man-made risks.

meta.title: FIRE & WATERPROOF. Cooperation of the civil protection services of Lublin and Rivne

card.solution: The strategic goal of the project is to increase the resilience of the security system of cities against threats resulting from climate change and countering local risks of anthropogenic nature, by: 1. Increasing the level of safety of residents and the resilience of fire and flood protection systems 2. Intensifying cooperation between the civil protection services of both cities through the exchange of experience and developing joint solutions to respond to threats 3. Increasing the level of knowledge of the inhabitants of Lublin (LP) and Rivne (PP) on the threats resulting from climate change thanks to educational activities like press releases, online articles, sharing publication of "Rules of conduct in various emergency situations in the context of climate change and crisis situations" - in PL and UA. More educated individuals may be better equipped to understand the complexities of climate science and have more awareness of the risks of climate change The implementation of the project results from the needs that are indicated in many documents of operational and strategic importance for the cities. Lublin's strategic and operational documents raise the issue of adequate preparation of the city for flood hazards, indicating areas the most exposed to flooding. Rivne's main need is the need to adapt the fire protection system to the requirements related to the local government reform in Ukraine, as a result of which the area of operation of the municipal fire brigade is to be successively increased, especially from 2020, when the village of Kwasylów joined the Rivne Territorial Commune, which not only increased the area of the commune, but also extended the response time to fires by municipal rescue services. The main project outputs: - 2 emergency service units equipped to carry out rescue and disaster recovery operations (1LP and 1PP) - 200 participants of the training workshops (4 different activities, 25 participants per partner at each workshop) - approx. 6300 ha of area covered by protection measures against wildfires in Rivne - investments in new or upgraded disaster monitoring, preparedness, warning and response systems against natural disasters – approx. LP:300K PLN, PP:10M UAH, which amounts to approx. 318 181 Euro. The main project beneficiaries are: - 2 emergency service units (1 LP,1PP) - approx. 492K citizens (approx. 242K LP and 250K PP) Significant challenges faced by the cities include adapting to climate change, mitigating, detecting and warning about natural and anthropogenic hazards. Adapting to these changes necessitates solutions development, risk management, boosting rescue services' expertise and raising public awareness about potential threats. In light of potential risks such as anthropogenic disasters, industrial accidents and, in case of Ukraine, missile attacks, there is a burning need for essential activities that would minimise their impact and educate the public on emergency response. The cross-border approach is essential for effectively security management and climate resilience. The urban area is characterized by different urban ecosystems that interact with different institutional levels, including different stakeholders and decision-makers, such as public administrations and governments. This can create many institutional conflicts in planning and designing the urban security. It would arguably be ideal for an urban area to be planned like a socio-ecological system where the urban ecosystem and institutional levels interact with each other in a multi-scale analysis. This work embraces a planning process that aims at being applied to a multi-institutional level approach that is able to match different visions and stakeholders’ needs, combining bottom-up and top-down participation approaches. In this way, the bottom-up and top- down approaches are useful to match the need of the community that uses the area with the vision of urban space development of decision-makers.

card.solution: Common challenges for the Programme area, within which the Lelis Commune, the city of Skole and the non-governmental organisation Euroregion Carpathians Ukraine - Carpathian Regional Development Agency draw knowledge and experience from each other. This is a process of identifying, analysing and transferring good practices that will contribute to the improvement of the implementation of regional development instruments and will ultimately result in the implementation of solutions that are beneficial to the citizens of both sides. The aim of the project is to prevent threats and mitigate their effects by modernising the technological line for sewage pre-treatment in the Lelis Commune and purchasing specialist equipment for municipalities (a vehicle, a hydraulic crane, a hook device, a water-pressure hooklift , slurry hooklift, spreader, plow) and rebuilding drinking water disinfection devices and purchasing a special truck for water collection for the city of Skole. Soft activities have been planned (i.e. conferences, a competition, open lessons and an eco-picnic, as well as developing a common concept for the protection of water resources on the Polish-Ukrainian border and a promotional film), which will raise awareness of disasters and threats caused by human activity. The modernization of the outdated sewage treatment plant will enable proper and trouble-free treatment of incoming sewage, and the purchase of a hook device, a hydraulic crane will also allow for the collection of waste transported from the Lelis Commune. In the long term, this will translate into an improvement in the condition of the natural environment. Considering the fact that the phenomenon of various natural disasters, especially droughts, has recently intensified, the Lelis Commune plans to purchase a vehicle adapted to transport, distribute and deliver water under high pressure, which will increase the Commune's ability to eliminate the effects of drought. Sudden snowstorms occurring in winter can paralyze or significantly impede the functioning of the city's infrastructure. Aware of this, the commune plans to counteract this type of natural hazard by purchasing a plough and a sand spreader for de-icing roads. The city of Skole also struggles with natural disasters, as it is located in the mountainous part of the Carpathians, where floods, storms, landslides, excessive snowfall and droughts often occur, which is why it plans to purchase a special car for a water utility, which aims to eliminate the effects of these natural disasters and ensure the supply of drinking water to nearby municipalities, whose residents usually draw water from deep wells, often containing hazardous exogenous substances created in geological processes. In order to ensure the proper quality of drinking water (limiting the incidence of stomach diseases, eliminating sources of epidemiological threats) and its failure-free supply to residents, the city of Skole plans to reconstruct facilities for disinfecting drinking water (including: reconstruction of water treatment plants and waterworks, technological pipelines, construction of tanks for clean water). Without the proper quality of water, the natural environment would be much poorer and less diverse. The project includes planned activities directly related to the specific objective of the Programme: Supporting adaptation to climate change and preventing the risk of natural disasters and resilience, taking into account the ecosystem approach. The implementation of the project will reduce the risk of natural disasters and increase resilience to their occurrence. The main results of the project will include investments in new or modernised monitoring, preparedness, warning and response systems for disasters and joint development of cross-border solutions. They will be used by all residents of the Lelis Commune and the city of Skole.

meta.title: Firefighters -volunteers on guard of the environment. Cross-border actions to prevent the effects of climate change.
meta.institution: The Association of Local Governments of Euroregion "Bug"

card.solution: The latest UN Global Assessment Report on Disaster Risk Reduction says that the number of disaster events has increased significantly in recent decades. Between 1970 and 2000, disasters occurred an average of 90-100 times per year. Between 2001 and 2020, by contrast, the numbers were 350-500. The study shows that if this trend continues, the annual number of natural disasters could rise to 560 by 2030. This is a 40 per cent increase. The UN report also shows that the frequency of extreme temperatures will triple by 2030. The increase in temperatures associated with a warming climate results in more frequent and longer periods of drought and this translates into more fires, both of infrastructure facilities and the natural environment, such as forests and peat bogs. In the project territory on the Ukrainian side, there have been 1132 fires in the last 5 years, resulting in 52 deaths and 12 injuries. A total of 18 forest fires and 11 peatland fires were registered. On the Polish side, there were a total of 1,694 forest and peatland fires between 2019 and 2023, with a total number of fatalities in fires of -162. In addition, on the territory of municipalities on the Ukrainian side, there are 65 hazardous facilities where flammable and explosive substances are stored. These facilities pose a serious threat to the population living on both sides of the border due to the increased risk of explosions and toxic emissions, which also poses a threat to the environment. The main challenge and need for public services in this context is to ensure the safety of local communities related to the protection of property, health and life. A problem that has arisen due to the increase in the number and frequency of natural disasters is the shortage of adequate equipment and specialised equipment for TSO units on both sides of the border. The higher number of fires that break out during periods of drought requires greater simultaneous use of both people and equipment. The main objective of the project is to support climate change adaptation and disaster risk prevention in the cross-border area in the Lubelskie Voivodeship and Rivne Oblast. As a result of the project, cross-border standards for disaster monitoring, preparedness, warning and response by local authorities and TSOs in the cross-border area will be developed. There will be an exchange of experience, improvement of the level of organisation and skills of TSOs in monitoring, preparedness, warning and response to natural disasters in the cross-border area. There will be an increase in the level of education of local communities on prevention and behaviour during natural disasters in the cross-border area. Cross-border uniformed services exercises in Poland and Ukraine will be carried out. Study visits for representatives of the administration and voluntary fire brigades will be organised. Firefighters will improve their qualifications by taking part in training courses in Poland on the principles of communication in the PSP radio network, and in Ukraine on qualified first aid. Two cross-border conferences will be organised. Educational activities for this group will include lectures in 10 Polish schools and 10 Ukrainian schools for a group of 500 participants. Lectures will be held for representatives of local authorities and residents from Poland and Ukraine as part of educational activities. In order to increase the ability to respond quickly in the event of natural disasters, the project will purchase equipment and supplies for TSO units on the Polish and Ukrainian sides. The project partners will purchase the equipment and then transfer it to the cooperating TSO units for use. Ownership of the equipment will be transferred to the municipalities on the basis of an agreement and protocols concerning the transfer of individual devices. The transfer of ownership will ensure the proper use and maintenance of the equipment, responsibility, and use in accordance with its intended purpose.

meta.title: Monitoring the quality of raw water used in the production of drinking and recreational water, for chemical and microbiological hazards, including agents causing infectious diseases that result from human activity
meta.institution: The Provincial Sanitary and Epidemiological Station in Rzeszów

card.solution: The idea of the project is to monitor pollution resulting from human activity in raw water used to produce drinking water and monitoring surface waters used for recreation. Monitoring will be carried out basing on the strategy of expanding the current range of water testing parameters by the scope of microbiological and chemical threats that are determinants of health problems occurring in connection with the use of water in the indicated rivers on both sides of the borders. Monitoring will concern microbiological and chemical threats. Microbiological monitoring will include the determination of coliform bacteria, including Escherichia and Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, Escherichia coli and Vibrio cholerae bacteria, which enter the water together with domestic sewage, mainly from unsewered areas. Additionally, pathogenic viruses that are capable of causing a rapidly spreading epidemic among people will be determined. The monitoring will also concern the analysis of environmental conditions that favor the development of toxic strains of cyanobacteria and their determination. Cyanobacterial microcystin toxins negatively affect the health quality of recreational and drinking water. Chemical monitoring will include the indication bisphenol A. It is a chemical compound used in the production of plastics. Bisphenol A belongs to a group of compounds that interfere with the action of human hormonal system (among others). As a result of the project, three new research methods will be created to determine water quality parameters. The implemented methods will allow for obtaining data on the condition and quality of water during monitoring (research). This data will be sent to local water and recreational water authorities. Additionally, residents covered by the project will be informed about the research results. The project will include cross-border activities, i.e. joint monitoring of the transfer of factors threatening human health through river waters, which will allow both partners to obtain information about water quality in the project's impact areas. However, the key goal is not only to analyze data, but also to effectively inform the public about potential threats related to water quality. As part of cooperation, an initial model (address database) of entities, including crisis management centres, local government and government administration, will be developed to exchange information and warnings in situations threatening the health and life of the region's inhabitants. This information is important for quickly responding to new threats so that communities can be effectively informed about water quality issues. If microbiological or chemical standards are exceeded, this information may be published in local media and on the websites of institutions responsible for public safety.

meta.title: Cross-border Roztocze - protection of the natural complex by improving the sewage management in the City of Tomaszow Lubelski and the District of Solonka

card.solution: The project is of a collaborative nature and will be implemented by three entities operating on the Polish and Ukrainian sides. Its thematic scope focuses on carrying out infrastructure works on both sides of the border, aimed at developing infrastructure and municipal services in the field of water and sewage management (construction of sewage treatment plants on the Ukrainian side and renovation/modernization of the water and sewage network on the Polish side), and consequently improving the local and regional state of the natural environment (soil, surface and groundwater). Considering the characteristics of the project mentioned above, it should be noted that it aligns well with, among others, the following challenges and preferred intervention directions specified in the Common Strategy of the Interreg NEXT Poland-Ukraine Program for the years 2021-2027: • Insufficient technical condition of sewage and water supply networks, • Countering the negative effects resulting from the peripheral location of the Polish-Ukrainian border, • Development of sustainable water management, supporting the protection of natural heritage and its resources, • Improvement of the quality of public services to eliminate development constraints in the border areas of Poland and Ukraine, • Counteracting environmental degradation and protection of the most valuable natural resources (both regions are located in the same geographical region: Tomaszów Lubelski City - Central Roztocze, Solonkа Village Council - Eastern Roztocze), • Strengthening cross-border cooperation between public institutions, enhancing their administrative potential, • Impact on low levels of socio-economic development, • Impact on climate change. Confirmation of the project intervention's alignment with the challenges for the Program area is its main goal, defined as follows: "Improvement of the technical condition of existing water and sewage infrastructure in the area of Tomaszów Lubelski City and implementation of a sewage treatment system in the area of the Solonkа Village Council, contributing to the improvement of the residents' quality of life, groundwater and surface water conditions, minimizing epidemiological threats, and pollution reduction." The main outcomes (expressed through indicators of the Interreg Next PL-UA Program) of this cross-border partnership project will be: 1. Number of urban wastewater treatment plants built - 1 unit. 2. Length of new or upgraded pipes for the public network for collection of waste water - 2.9 km, 3. Length of new or upgraded pipes for the distribution systems of public water supply - 1.3 km, 4. Participations in joint actions across borders - 110 people, 5. Population connected to improved public water supply - 80 people, 6. Population connected to at least secondary public waste water treatment - 8,000 people. The primary beneficiaries of the project outcomes will be individuals belonging to the group of end beneficiaries, namely residents of Solonkа Village Council (Ukraine) and Tomaszów Lubelski City (Poland), who will utilize the products of this project. The need for partnership and cross-border approach to project implementation arises primarily from: • Efforts of the partners aimed at generating a clear cross-border effect, identifiable at the level of significant reduction in sources and quantities of pollutants ultimately discharged into rivers, • Insufficient own funds of local governments to finance the project independently and formal requirements of the Interreg Next PL-UA Program, which, as known, require the establishment of a Polish-Ukrainian partnership to submit an application, implement the project, and ultimately address common cross-border issues identified both in the entire Program area and in areas under the jurisdiction of local governments, which have been detailed above and in the further sections of the application form.

meta.title: Cross-Border Eco Solutions in the Paprotnia and Klesiv Communes

card.solution: Opis projektu The project aims to address common environmental challenges and promote sustainable solutions in the Paprotnia and Klesiv communes, despite the absence of a shared river, watershed, or catchment area. By focusing on their shared EcoSolutions and similar issues, the project seeks to implement initiatives that enhance ecological well-being, resource management, and community engagement. Through collaborative efforts, both communes can work together to create a positive impact on their local environments while fostering a sense of shared responsibility for the greater ecological harmony in the region. The project addresses the common challenge of outdated water and sewage infrastructure and its impact on ecological health and climate resilience in the Paprotnia Commune (Poland) and Klesiv Commune (Ukraine). Both municipalities face similar issues, including inadequate wastewater treatment, sewage system deficiencies, and vulnerability to climate-related events. Together, the project aims to tackle these challenges through a collaborative and comprehensive approach. The primary objective of the project is to enhance ecological solutions and sustainable water management in the Paprotnia and Klesiv municipalities. By modernizing sewage infrastructure, preventing pollution, and fostering cross-border cooperation, the project seeks to: •Improve wastewater management and sanitation infrastructure. •Enhance ecological well-being and climate resilience. •Promote responsible water usage and ecological awareness. •Strengthen cross-border collaboration for sustainable development. Main Products and Beneficiaries: •Construction of Sanitary Sewage System: The project aims to build a gravity-pressure sanitary sewage system with connectors in Kaliski, Paprotnia, Poland. It involves installation of gravity and pressure systems, connectors, and a sewage pumping station, benefiting approximately 60 residents (sewage network: 3,5725 km) •Reconstruction of Sewage Treatment Plant (1 item): A new sewage treatment plant will be established in Klesiv, Klesiv, Ukraine. This involves upgrading distribution networks for water (0,061 km) and sewage (0,008 km). • Water and sewage management conference: A cross-border conference with participants from both countries will discuss climate-related water challenges and solutions. The outcomes will lead to a Cross-Border Strategy of Good Practices. •Educational Activities for 600 Students: Educational projects in both countries will raise awareness about climate change, water conservation, and responsible usage among school children. •Opening and Closing Conferences: Conferences will be held in Poland and Ukraine to promote the project's objectives, achievements, and outcomes. The project necessitates a transboundary approach due to shared challenges, mutual benefits, and the need for joint solutions. Both communes face similar issues, and their proximity makes cross-border cooperation vital. A transboundary approach allows for knowledge exchange, cost-effective solutions, and comprehensive ecological improvements that go beyond individual municipality capacities. The collaboration strengthens both regions' resilience to climate change, encourages sustainable development, and fosters cross-border partnerships. In conclusion, the project's integrated approach addresses the shared challenges of outdated water infrastructure and ecological well-being in Paprotnia and Klesiv communes. By modernizing sanitation systems, promoting awareness, and fostering cross-border collaboration, the project strives to create a sustainable future for both communities while contributing to regional and ecological development goals.

meta.title: Development of sewage infrastructure in two cities - Suwalki and Ternopil
meta.institution: Water Supply and Sewerage Company in Suwalki

card.solution: The general objective of the project is to improve the quality of natural environment in the cities of Suwałki and Ternopil and in the cross-border Programme area. Modernization and renovation of sewage system infrastructure in Suwalki (PL) 0,742 km long and Ternopil (UA) 1,362 km long enable to avoid environmental pollution by sanitary sewage system in Suwalki (incl.Czarna Hancza river and residential areas) and Ternopil (incl.Seret river and residential areas) and improve safety of sewage management UC "Ternopilvodokanal” provides water supply and wastewater disposal services in Ternopil and nearby villages which are used by 222000 people. The total length of wastewater networks is 295,9 km, of which 167,6 km are dilapidated. The specified sewage pipelines to be reconstructed within the project were laid in 1988 and due to long-term operation are significantly worn, which leads to the occurrence of repeated emergency situations. The most dangerous is the probability of emergency situations, in case of damage to two lines of pipelines at the same time and create a threat of wastewater leaks to the surface in areas of intensive residential areas and on the roads of the city or even to Seret River. It is necessary to carry out reconstruction of the wastewater collectors from WWPS No.9 at 27 Sheptytskyi street to WWTP on Obizna street, D-630mm – in total 1.362 km long (2 lines x 681 m), open method that means complete replacing of old pipes with new ones, along with the construction of two switching chambers with manholes and laying 303 m of electric cable. The open method of laying the pipeline consists in digging a trench of the required depth with their subsequent strengthening and placement of the pipes themselves. The sewage infrastructure in Suwalki is managed by Water Supply and Sewerage Company in Suwalki. The total length of the sanitary sewage system in the city of Suwałki which was operated by the Company, is 130,7 km, of which almost 15% is over 40 years old. The most exploited sections of the network are located in Reja Street and on the section from Hubala St. to the Zastawie St. pumping station. Large-diameter pipelines are made in concrete technology, which are subject to progressive degradation and must be urgently renovated. Sanitary sewage system intended for renovation using the trenchless method, without disturbing the structure of the surface by inserting a special fiberglass lining soaked in epoxy resin inside the channel and then hardening with high temperature or ultraviolet rays: sanitary sewage system using the trenchless method will be renovated: from Hubala St. towards Leśna St.: 562 m long and in Reja St.: 180 m long also 3 chambers/wells in this Reja section will be replaced. Main project outputs Length of new or upgraded pipes for the public network for collection of waste water: 2,104 km (0,742 km Suwalki), (1,362 km Ternopil) Participations in joint actions across borders: 30 participants (15 Suwalki) and (15 Ternopil) Result indicator: Solutions taken or up-scaled by organisations: 1 common solution for the modernization of the sanitary sewage system developed by 2 partners and on the basis of a comprehensive report on sustainable sewage management. The modernized sewage infrastructure in two cities will be carried out in two ways, in Ternopil using the traditional open method, i.e. digging ditches and replacing of old pipes with new ones (1,362 km long) and in Suwałki using the trenchless method (technology) for sanitary sewage system renovation without digging and disturbing the structure of the surface (total: 0,742 km long). There will also be conducted 1 joint online workshop and an online final conference with presentation of a comprehensive report on sustainable sewage management (e-version in 3 lang.:PL-UA-ENG)

meta.institution: Water Supply and Sewage Company Ltd in Siedlce

card.solution: Project will be implemented in the area of ​​the border between Poland and Ukraine in the city of Siedlce (S) and the city of Ivano-Frankivsk (IF).The main objective of project is in line with the assumptions of the Interreg NEXT Poland-Ukraine Programme by supporting the development processes of border regions.The scope of the project is in line with priority 1.Environment, Specific objective 1.2.Promoting access to water and sustainable water management. The common challenges for the project partners are: -insufficiently developed water supply networks in S and IF, -low environmental awareness of residents of the cities about efficient water management. Main objective of the project is to make the monitoring and management systems of urban water supply technologically efficient, modern, which would meet today's requirements by: 1.improving public water supply network with installation of new modern equipment with new monitoring and management (ІТ) systems and as a result in both cities decreasing water losses and increasing quality of drinking water for all of citizens; 2.improving communication services for recipients using new IT (GIS systems, chatbots, new methods of access and payments) and as a result more friendly services for citizens especially for people with disabilities, increase ecological awareness of residents about using water in their cities. Main outputs of the project are: -modernised 1 water treatment plant in Siedlce with a new equipment; -modernised 1 water treatment plant by modernising 40 water pumping stations in IF with a new equipment for pressure, monitoring and management; -construction water supply network: 0,493 km in Kraszewskiego Str. in Siedlce; -one water supply emergency repair car for the water supply company in Ivano-Frankivsk and one passanger electric car for technical services in Siedlce for efficient reaction to damages in the networks; -equipment (spectrometer and chromatograph) for controlling of water quality and and quick response to changing indicators; -software with the necessary computer hardware and mobile devices for operating services for management and communication. The beneficiaries of the project will be water supply companies in Siedlce and Ivano-Frankivsk. Ivano-Frankivskvodoekotekhprom utility is 100% municipal enterprise, founded and fully owned by Ivano-Frankivsk City Council. It is responsible for water supply and sewerage networks in Ivano-Frankivsk. After the project completion Executive Committee of IF City Council by official decision will transfer all works and equipment to the balance of municipal enterprise, which will be further responsible for operation and maintenance. IF City Council as the owner of Ivano-Frankivskvodoekotekhprom ensure the sustainability of the results and the achievement of the indicators. Final beneficiaries are approx. 340.000 inhabitants, enterprises and public utility entities using the built infrastructure and improved services. (2,34 % of inhabitants on the program territory). Joint preparation of tasks covered by the project by the Polish and Ukrainian partners, joint implementation and joint financing with the participation of EU funds from the Programme in the form of co-financing are planned. The implementation of the project would not be possible without financial support from the INTERREG Programme because tariffs for the water are regulated by the state and the income of Municipal companies don't allow to cover such big investments. Additionally the war in Ukraine acts as a worsening factor for investing only with own funds. The Polish side has a better starting position in water monitoring and management, the Ukrainian side is better developed with residents' communication and IT solutions for contact and payments. Result of the project will be good synergy of resolving two main challenges in both cities by sharing knowledge and technologies on both sides of the border.

meta.title: WATER IS THE SOURCE OF LIFE - PRESERVING THE SHARED NATURAL HERITAGE OF THE CARPATHIANS IN THE OLSZANICA AND VELYKYI BEREZNYI COMMUNES THROUGH THE IMPROVEMENT OF WASTEWATER MANAGEMENT

card.solution: Proper management of municipal sewage is absolutely essential and aims to maintain sustainable water resource management within the Program area. Therefore, supporting rational water resource management is crucial in this region, including the construction of new facilities and the expansion of sewage networks, especially in rural areas. Implementing appropriate solutions is of paramount importance for preserving water quality, public health, environmental protection, and ensuring sustainable water resource management. The overall objective of the project is the protection and enhancement of the natural environment, including water resources, through effective municipal sewage management. This objective will be achieved through the following specific goals: - Reduction of environmental pollution through the development of sewage infrastructure and improvement of sewage management. - Increase of ecological awareness among residents regarding nature conservation, particularly water resources, and the promotion of sustainable management within the project implementation area. Promoting sustainable water resource management, including sewage management, and joint efforts to protect and improve the state of these resources are crucial for several important reasons: - Ensuring access to clean water, - Protection of aquatic ecosystems, - Minimization of climate change impact, - Avoidance of water conflicts, - Sustainable economic development. The main outputs and results: 1. Construction of sanitary sewerage in Olszanica Commune along with connections and accompanying infrastructure and technical facilities with a total length of 6,498.70 m. It is planned to construct 65 sewer manholes serving as prepared connection points for properties to the sewage network (63 households with 242 residents and 2 public facilities). 2. Construction of sanitary sewerage in Velykyi Bereznyi along connections and accompanying infrastructure and technical facilities with a total length of approximately 5584 m, and three sewage pumping stations will be built. As a result. The number of subscribers using sewage disposal services will increase by about 200 households (approximately 1000 people) and 7 multi-story buildings (approximately 360 people). Additionally, two social and cultural facilities will be connected to the network. 3. Promotional Campaign: - Production of an Educational-Promotional Documentary Film titled "Water is the Source of Life – Let's Protect and Conserve it for Future Generations". - Joint Environmental Education Program in Local Schools for 500 students (250 students under LB and 250 students under B1). The program will be titled "Saving Our Planet – Protecting and Conserving Water". This program will consist of a series of 7 workshops conducted in primary schools for groups of 25 students each from the Olszanica and Velyka Bereznyanska municipalities. Each Partner will conduct 10 repetitions. Benefits of the project that will be observed on both sides of the border include: - Elimination of pollution in the San and Uzh rivers and their local tributaries, resulting in improved environmental conditions in legally protected areas and their immediate surroundings. - Preservation of the local river fauna and flora and their riparian zones in good condition. - Increase in employment and revenues in the peripheral rural areas along the border. Engaging youth in pro-ecological activities will result not only in raising ecological awareness but also in joint pro-ecological youth initiatives.

meta.title: Improvement of the transboundary environmental protection system of the Carpathians through the development of water and sewage infrastructure - integrating the spa communes of Solina and Skhidnytsia in the fight for a clean environment

card.solution: Disorganized sewage management poses one of the most significant threats to the natural environment. It results in pollution of soil, surface waters, and groundwater, primarily. The Solina Commune faces a significant challenge due to the lack of complete sewage infrastructure in the communes's constituent localities. The failure to construct sewage systems leads to further environmental degradation of an extent and scope that are difficult to ascertain. Conversely, the state of the water supply network in Skhidnytsia is very poor, with over 50% of the water supply network being overused and in a constant state of emergency. Drinking water losses during transport and distribution in this network average around 70%. The overall goal of the project is the protection and enhancement of the natural environment, including water resources, through effective wastewater management. This objective will be achieved through the following specific goals: - Reducing environmental pollution by developing wastewater infrastructure and improving wastewater management practices. - Minimizing water losses from water supply systems and enhancing the rational use of water. - Increasing residents' ecological awareness regarding reservoir protection, particularly water resources, and promoting their sustainable management within the project area. Promoting sustainable water resource management, including wastewater management, and collaborative actions aimed at protecting and enhancing these resources are crucial for several significant reasons: - Ensuring access to clean water. - Protecting aquatic ecosystems. - Minimizing the impact of climate change. - Avoiding water conflicts. - Sustainable economic development. The main scope of the project: 1) Construction of a sanitary sewerage network (6,9971 km) with the necessary technical infrastructure for the village of Werlas in the Solina Commune (28 households (approximately 106 people), 1 public facility and 5 businesses connected). 2) Reconstruction of 3,7km of water pipeline in Skhidnytsia (435 private subscribers will be connected(2 600) ppl, as well as 27 businesses and public facilities). 3) Three-day ecological workshops focused on environmental protection and water conservation are planned for the youth from the Solina Commune (20 participants) and the Skhidnytsia Community (20 participants), aged 14-15 years. 4) Two ecological project conferences will be organized for representatives of local authorities, environmental non-governmental organizations, nature conservation institutions, and youth representatives. 5) Production of a promotional film titled "Water's Trail", focusing on the conservation of water resources and their sustainable recreational use. The purpose of the project is to enhance cooperation through the exchange of good practices based on the implementation of sustainable development principles. The main benefits of the initiative include the protection and safeguarding against pollution of locally flowing rivers and groundwater. From a cross-border perspective, the investment in the Solina commune is also significant for residents of western Ukraine. The hydroisohip map indicates that within river alluvia in the Podkarpackie Voivodeship in Poland, groundwater flow follows the course of rivers. This suggests that cross-border flows from Poland to Ukraine are possible, allowing pollutants to penetrate groundwater across the border. The consequences for the environment can be irreversible and exacerbate residents' comfort and health conditions.

card.solution: The project "Clean Water for All" aims to address critical water and sewer infrastructure challenges in the cross-border areas of Augustów and Burshtyn. The overarching goal is to provide clean and safe drinking water, protect water resources, promote sustainable water use, and foster socio-economic development. The project tackles four main problems: inadequate water infrastructure, lack of environmental awareness, limited cross-border cooperation, and insufficient socio-economic development. These issues lead to compromised health, hindered economic growth, and environmental degradation. To mitigate these challenges, the project focuses on upgrading water and sewer networks, raising environmental consciousness, fostering cross-border collaboration, and enhancing infrastructure. It aims to create a comprehensive water management framework that benefits residents, educational institutions, local authorities, investors, and tourists. The project's general objective aligns with the Poland-Ukraine Interreg Program 2021-2027 priorities, emphasizing sustainable water management, circular economy transformation, and environmental protection. Specific objectives include environmental protection, balancing infrastructure disparities, and strengthening cross-border collaboration. By implementing advanced technologies, responsible water use campaigns, and infrastructure improvements, the project strives to achieve sustainable growth while preserving the environment. It aims to reduce water losses, enhance efficiency, and minimize pollution. The project engages various stakeholders, contributing to better living standards, environmental preservation, and a more sustainable future. The project will yield three primary products: a. UPGRADED WATER AND SEWER INFRASTRUCTURE: Improved water and sewer networks, upgraded wells, and renovated deep wells will ensure clean water supply and efficient wastewater management. This will benefit residents, schools, businesses, and tourists in both partner cities. b. ENHANCED ENVIRONMENTAL AWARENESS PROGRAMS: Educational campaigns, workshops with experts during conferences, and community partnerships will promote responsible water use and environmental consciousness. Addressing biases and prejudices through collaboration enhances mutual understanding and cooperation, contributing to more effective and lasting solutions. c. Improving infrastructure, promoting eco-friendly practices, and fostering cross-border relations will stimulate socio-economic growth in both partner areas. d. The challenges are complex and require multifaceted solutions that draw from the expertise and experiences of both partners, making a transboundary approach crucial.

meta.title: PACT - Partnership for a Cleaner Tomorrow. Cross-border project to improve sustainable wastewater management in Yaroslav and Zaleszczyki
meta.institution: The Water Supply and Sewage Company in Jarosław

card.solution: The main objective of the project is to build effective cross-border cooperation between the city of Jarosław and Zaleszczyki and to develop joint solutions in the field of creating sustainable water and sewage management. The main products of the project are: - development of the cross-border "Strategy for sustainable water and sewage management Jarosław-Zaleszczyki", which will enable systemic activities in the field of protection of water resources and will support sustainable water management in the area covered by the Program - conducting surveys and developing 2 reports diagnosing the state of water and sewage management in Jarosław and Zaleszczyki - conducting 12 participatory meetings with residents on both sides of the border - development of 8 environmental expertises - organization of a total of 3 conferences (2 in Jarosław, 1 in Zaleszczyki) - organization of 8 trainings (3 in Jarosław and 5 in Zaleszczyki). During these activities, experience and knowledge in the field of water and sewage management will be exchanged between the project partners. - construction of approximately 8,4 km of sewage network in Jarosław, which will enable 282 residents of the northern part of the city of Jarosław to be connected to the network in the area of ​​Dolnoleżajska, Brodowicze and Stawki streets: 94 residential buildings will be connected to the designed sewage system (approx. 3 people per household - in total 282 people). The implementation of the sewage system in question will make it possible in the future to connect building plots (currently undeveloped) intended for single-family housing, located in the area of ​​the following streets: Dolnoleżajska, Brodowicze, Stawki. The parameters of the planned sewerage facilities have been selected in a way that will enable their further expansion in the future, in order to connect properties located in the area of ​​streets, among others, to them in the future. Piaskowa, Łazy Kostkowskie, Kolaniki, Żwirowa, Lipowa, Kamienna, Diamentowa, Szmaragdowa, Bursztynowa. - reconstruction of the sewage treatment plant in Zaleszczyki. The treatment plant will be used about 9,000 people, residents of Zaleszczyki and tourists. - promotion of the project at every stage of its implementation (issuing a total of 200 information brochures, organizing press conferences, publishing 1 article in the industry press, creating a website in Zaleszczycki Wodokanal, creating a bookmark on the website of PWiK Jarosław Sp. z o.o.). meta.title: Water resources protection through the development of sewage infrastructure as a joint challenge of Lesko Commune and Khust Town in the fight for a clean environment

card.solution: Both partners share the common element of transboundary rivers. Effective protection of these rivers requires joint and coordinated investment actions on both sides of the border. Mutual pollution cross-contaminates, adversely affecting the environment, particularly surface and groundwater, across the entire border area. Proper management of municipal sewage is of fundamental importance for the areas covered by the project and will lead to maintaining a sustainable water management system. The overall objective of the project is to improve the condition of the natural environment, including surface and subsurface water resources. This objective will be achieved through the following specific goals: - Reducing pollution by municipal sewage in areas of particular natural heritage significance for the border regions of Poland and Ukraine through the construction and modernization of sanitary sewage networks. - Developing an enhanced natural environment management system in the Lesko Commune and the town of Khust by enhancing the qualifications of personnel. - Increasing environmental awareness among residents regarding conservation, particularly of water resources, and promoting sustainable management practices within the project area. Given that the investment is a part of a partner project within the context of Polish-Ukrainian cross-border cooperation, jointly achieving the aforementioned goals will ultimately accelerate and strengthen cross-border developmental processes on the border of Poland and Ukraine. The indicators of this impact will include: - Improved watercourse cleanliness. - Preservation of unique fauna and flora in good condition. - Creation of new jobs in the tourism sector. - Increased revenues for economic entities in the tourism industry. - Consequently, a reduction of social exclusion phenomena on both sides of the border from a social perspective. Main outputs: 1. Construction of a sanitary sewage network section and modernization of 4 sewage pumping stations in the Lesko Commune (1,545km). As a result, a total of 77 people will be connected to the network. 2. Construction and reconstruction of sewage networks along the several streets in Velykyi Bereznyi. The main outputs and results: 1. Self-flow sewage – 3,007 km, pressure sewage – 0,681k m, sewage pumping stations – 3 items. 2. Number of people connected to at least secondary public waste water treatment – 1791. 3. Two parallel environmentally-oriented events are planned in Lesko and Khust for the volunteers. This will involve a joint action of collecting litter along the riverbanks: the San River in Lesko (involving youth and adults from Lesko Commune) and the Tisza River in Khust (involving youth and adults from Khust). Both actions in Lesko and Khust will take place simultaneously, with approximately 50 participants from each country. 4. A collaborative educational-promotional film will be produced. 5. Organization of "Protecting Water Resources" seminars at both partners places (40UA, 30PL people). The main benefits of the undertaking are the protection and safeguarding against contamination of locally flowing rivers, particularly the transboundary San and Tisza rivers, resulting in an improvement of the natural environment and its key natural assets, which are also utilized by tourists. The joint implementation of the project will establish a partnership approach, bridging the gaps in experience and organizational potential among partners. The project's implementation in partnership will reinforce the ongoing cooperation with the Ukrainian partner and the preservation of the natural heritage area, which constitutes the greatest wealth and asset of the borderland, contributing to the development of related tourism. Well-developed cross-border cooperation will also constitute significant potential for its further growth, as well as the preparation and implementation of cross-border projects.

card.solution: The project submitted for evaluation is of a partnership nature and will be implemented by two local government units operating on the Polish and Ukrainian sides. Its thematic scope will focus on conducting infrastructure works on both sides of the border, directed towards the development of infrastructure and municipal services in the field of sewage management (construction/reconstruction of sanitary sewage networks), ultimately leading to the improvement of the local and regional natural environment (soil, surface water, and groundwater). Considering the aforementioned project characteristics, it is essential to highlight that it aligns well with various challenges and preferred directions of intervention defined in the Common Strategy of the Interreg NEXT Poland-Ukraine 2021-2027 Programme: 1. insufficiently developed sewage 2. counteracting negative effects resulting from peripheral location of the Polish-Ukrainian borderland 3. development of sustainable water management, supporting protection of natural heritage’s biodiversity and its resources 4. improving quality of public services in order to eliminate development limitations in border areas of Poland and Ukraine 5. counteracting a degradation of natural environment and protection of the most valuable natural assets (these activities are in line with the EU's postulate of Europe that uses environmental resources more efficiently) 6. tightening cross-border cooperation between public institutions, strengthening their administrative potential 7. impact on a low level of socio-economic development 8. impact on a climate changes Confirmation of the above thesis regarding the alignment of the project's interventions with the challenges of the Programme area is its main objective, which has been defined as follows: "Improve the sanitary conditions in the area of the Dołhobyczów Municipality and Sokal City, contributing to the enhancement of residents' quality of life, groundwater and surface water conditions, minimization of epidemiological threats, and reduction of environmental pollution." Basic outputs (expressed by indicators of the Interreg NEXT Poland–Ukraine 2021-2027 Programme) of such defined orientation of analyzed cross-border partnership project will be: 1. Length of new or upgraded pipes for the public network for collection of waste water (RCO31) - 8,354 km 2. Population connected to at least secondary public waste water treatment (RCR42) - 23 295 people 3. Participations in joint actions across borders (RCO81) - 40 people 4. Number of participants of the trainings for the institution (PLRO150) - 20 people The users of the project outcomes will primarily be individuals categorized as the group of ultimate beneficiaries, i.e., residents of the town of Dołhobyczów (Poland) and the city of Sokal, who will be connected to the newly constructed or reconstructed sewage networks. The need for a partnership and cross-border approach to project implementation results primarily from: - the partners' aim to generate a clear cross-border effect that is identifiable in terms of significantly reducing the sources and quantity of pollutants discharged into the Bug River. This also has a positive impact on improving the river's water quality (Bug River flowing on both the Polish and Ukrainian sides). - Insufficient own funds of local governments to finance the project on their own and formal requirements of the Interreg Next PL UA Programme, which, as it is known, require an establishment of a Polish-Ukrainian partnership in order to be able to submit an application, implement the project and ultimately solve common cross-border problems identified both in the area of entire Programme and in areas subordinated to local governments, which have been presented in detail above and in further part of the application form.

card.solution: The common challenge and main goal of the project is to support access to clean water and sustainable water management in the Polish-Ukrainian region and to improve the quality of people's lives by developing sewage infrastructure and improving sewage management. The subject of the project is the expansion of the sewage system and modernization of the sewage treatment plant, the development of a practical guide on water protection issues and good practices in this regard, the creation of a cross-border platform for the exchange of knowledge and experience in the field of water and sewage management, an information and educational campaign. Positive benefits that the construction of the sewage system and the modernization of the sewage treatment plant will bring to the partners and the Polish-Ukrainian region: *improvement of the natural environment (wastewater will be properly treated before discharge into the environment, which will contribute to the protection of aquatic ecosystems and diversity) *improving the quality of people's lives (safe disposal of pollutants is crucial to protect public health as it prevents the spread of infectious diseases that can be transmitted through sewage) * economic development of the area (good sewage infrastructure is an important aspect for economic development, attracting investments, creating jobs and increasing the attractiveness of the place) The project will strengthen cross-border cooperation between the Konopnica Commune and Terebovlia and strengthen people-to-people contacts. meta.title: Clean water - development of sustainable water management in the transboundary area.

card.solution: Water is a limited and vulnerable resource - essential for life and development. For many decades, the key tasks of water management were exclusively concerned with the use and technological utilisation of water. However, progressive climate change is strongly affecting both environmental resources and needs. Adaptation measures that also take into account land-use planning solutions are therefore necessary, and one of the key resources in this process is water. Proper management of its resources is therefore particularly important. The described phenomena have intensified strongly in the last few decades and cause negative effects, which are also a serious problem in the Polish-Ukrainian cross-border area. Particularly noticeable are the increases in temperatures that cause periods of drought which translates into water shortages. Although overall water consumption in most of the cross-border area has decreased in recent years, there are still shortcomings in terms of sewerage network coverage and availability of clean water. The population, especially in Ukraine, is often connected to an inefficient and outdated public water supply network, resulting in both water losses and a deterioration of drinking water quality. On the Polish side, the situation looks better, although there are cases, especially in rural areas, where entire villages are not connected to the sewage system. The current situation is due to infrastructural shortcomings, manifested in an underdeveloped sewage and water supply network and low awareness among residents and public institutions. The diagnosed problems are also related to the project area, where in the Bukowsko commune the village of Dudyńce does not have a sewage system, as a result of which the environment (especially streams) is polluted through leaking septic tanks and sometimes residents pouring sewage directly onto fields or into streams, which are then transferred to the San River. This situation is also due to a lack of awareness on the part of residents that well-treated sewage can be reused in nature in the form of water. More broadly, this problem relates to a lack of knowledge on how to manage water sensibly, especially in times of climate change. On the Ukrainian side in Rudky, the village centre lacks a functioning sewage network and individual septic tanks do not meet sanitary requirements. The old sewage network infrastructure is highly degraded and disused due to lack of public funds for modernisation and expansion. The leakage of sewage into the ground poses a high sanitary and environmental risk as it then finds its way into the Wysznia River and then into the San River. As a result of the project, the level of development of sustainable water management in the transboundary area in the Bukowsko Municipality and Rudky Town will increase. The length of the sewerage infrastructure will increase by 4,086 metres on the Polish side and 2,513 metres on the Ukrainian side and there will be an improvement in wastewater management in the Bukowsko Municipality and Rudky Town. Rainwater storage and reuse infrastructure will be developed in the Bukowsko Municipality and Rudky Town. In the Municipality of Bukowsko, two rain gardens will be constructed in the villages of Dudyńce and Pobiedno. In the Town of Rudky, a reservoir will be created to collect rainwater and then use it for firefighting. The level of awareness of residents about the water cycle and the need for water management in the Bukowsko Municipality and Rudky Town will be increased through participation in workshops and conferences.
