meta.title: Cross-border development of water supply and sewerage system - Good Water Tyczyn - Pustomyty
meta.institution: Municipal Utilities Company "Eko-Strug" Limited Liability Company

card.solution: The common goal and the expected change is to improve the quality of residents’ lifes and adapting Tyczyn (TM) and Pustomyty (PST) to changing climatic conditions by increasing the availability of good water and protecting the natural environment of the borderland from pollution through the development of the sewage system. Poland (SDG report 2022) has very poor renewable freshwater resources (1600 m³/person/year). This is one of the lowest values in the EU (3 times less than average). The situation in UA is even worse - 1240 m³/person (State Water Resources Agency - 2019). According to the UN, less than 1700 m³ means water security threat.The most important problems diagnosed in the border area include underdeveloped water/sewage infrastructure which negatively affects the environmental, social and economic spheres. The low degree of water supply (about 66% in TM and 53% in PST) and sewerage (62% in TM and 35% in PST) adversely affects not only the comfort of life, but also the level of sanitary safety, as the risk of gastrointestinal diseases increases, due to the consumption of water with undetermined parameters, mainly by the uncoordinated creation of domestic water intakes (wells), as well as through the large number of domestic septic tanks (which cause groundwater contamination through leaks). Both cities have become convenient places for settlement, as they are adjacent to large and important urban centers (PST = Lviv, TM = Rzeszow). This has an impact on the steady population/clients growth (TM: 10,499 people in 2019 to 11,397 in 2022; PST: 2019 - 20,410 clients to 20,604 in 2022), which translates into increases in water consumption and more wastewater. Insufficiently developed and often outdated water/sewage infrastructure isn’t able to meet these challenges, that’s why significant increases in failures have been observed (TM own data for water: 2019 - 15 failures, 2022 - 20 failures = 33% increase + sewerage 18 and 23 respectively = 27.8% increase) and in PST (own data for water: 2019 - 32 failures, 2022 - 79 failures = 146.9% increase + sewerage 98 and 312 respectively = 218.4% increase). The ongoing war in UA also has had a significant impact on the catastrophic changes in access to water. The investment is of strategic importance for the border provinces (Rzeszow and Lviv), which also face the problem of inadequate amount of water for supplying residents during periods of drought (and due to the ongoing war). The well-developed networks belonging to the Partners can also serve as an emergency water supply for these cities. PL/UA common challenges: droughts/climate changes, water supply interruptions and/or significant reductions in water pressure, environmental pollution due to lack of sewerage, increasing number of failures, low awareness of residents about the need to save water. In response to the above, the partners identified the main objectives of the project as: - Increase availability and ensure good quality water for newly connected 210 Poles and 3544 Ukrainians (+3923, which are already connected to this pipeline) through the construction of new water pipeline PL-3,8 km, UA-1,2 km. - protecting the environment through the development of an improved public sewage system: PL – 2,76 km (connecting 207 Poles) and by modernizing sewage system for 7361 Poles and 6731Ukrainians. - Adaptation to changes by increasing awareness of saving and obtaining drinking water in emergency situations among 1200 Poles and Ukrainians A cross-border approach is necessary, as both partners have different experiences, thanks to the exchange of which (by joint training, creation of joint procedures – 10 PL/UA employees) the UA partner will gain the necessary knowledge on modern solutions and technologies used in water and sewage systems and the PL partner will gain knowledge on how to respond more effectively in crisis and critical situations. The above will benefit the residents of TM, PST - indirectly also Lviv and Rzeszów

meta.title: Improvement of the cross-border environmental protection system in the city of Garwolin and the commune of Mokobody in Poland and in the city of Brody in Ukraine through the development of sewage infrastructure

card.solution: The project Interreg4water was prepared in partnership between the city of Garwolin, the commune of Mokobody, the city of Brody and the Carpathian Euroregion association, and shall be considered as a joint, complex response to the identified common problems and needs of participants from the cross border area i.e.: • inadequate sanitary sewage system and wastewater treatment which cause negative consequences for the environment and have essential influence on the quality of living of inhabitants in Garwolin, Mokobody and Brody area. • lack of inhabitants' awareness of proper water management, conservation and treatment. It is particularly important to shape the right attitudes among the youngest residents (children, school and high school students), who in the future will be responsible for shaping local policies and functioning of cities in an increasingly difficult ecological situation caused, among others, by global warming. • moderate capacity of local units and key stakeholders involved into wastewater management. The awareness of the existing challenges and directions of development is a key factor in maintain sustainable water management in the Program area. The main goal of the joint project is increasing of the environmental protection and the quality of life of inhabitants of the cross-border area through development of sewage infrastructure and improving sustainable water management as well as ecological awareness. As a result of project implementation, the sewage system in Garwolin (2,92 km length) and Mokobody (4,728 km length) will be expanded, and the outdated and inefficient sewage treatment plant in Brody will be modernized and developed. In addition, a number of soft activities will be carried out aimed at increasing the ecological awareness of the inhabitants of the participating cities, with particular emphasis on young people. The project also includes the development of common concepts and strategies as well as the exchange of experience and training for employees of institutions dealing with water resources and wastewater management, which will significantly increase the competences of public entities in this area. Thanks to the cross-border partnership and the opportunities offered under the INTERRG NEXT Poland-Ukraine 2021-2027 Programme, it will be possible to implement both the investment component and unique soft activities of a common cross-border nature. Project plan and approach is straightforward and include the involvement of all participants to the common activities from the project beginning supported by transparent promotional campaigns in order to inform all communities on the joint cross border initiative.

meta.title: Clean Bug - joint activities of the Drohiczyn Commune and the Dobrotvir Town Council for protecting biodiversity of the Bug Valley

card.solution: The quality of the natural environment of the cross-border area is a key aspect of the high quality of life of its inhabitants. It determines its attractiveness and tourist and economic potential, which should be further explored in a sustainable manner. The Bug Valley is a key element of the cross-border shared ecosystem. The Bug river plays a very important role in the ecological security of the eastern part of Poland and the western- southern part of Ukraine due to the fact that it provides a number of ecosystem services. Therefore, significant challenges for the area covered by the project and the Program include: environmental pollution, presence of illegal landfills, persistently low level of waste recycling, low level of awareness of sensitive issues among a wide range of stakeholders and residents, insufficient area of green infrastructure in cities. The aim of the project is to protect the biodiversity of the cross-border ecosystem of the Bug Valley through joint actions to reduce the level of pollution, to develop green infrastructure and to promote environmental education. The project involves supplementing the waste management infrastructure with specialized garbage trucks and the installation of 18 places for waste segregation, liquidation of illegal landfills on both sides of the border with a total area of 4,561 ha (1 ha PL, 3,561 ha UA), as well as renovation of landfill sites by planting about 500 trees and enrichment of the urban and degraded area with green infrastructure in Dobrotvir with an area of 2,95 ha. The project will also include cleaning the banks and the bed of the Bug River over a length of approximately 290 km, as well as an extensive educational campaign. The project will lead to the creation of an innovative exhibition and educational space in Drohiczyn, aimed at conducting intensive ecological education of various social groups. The culmination of the project will be a study of best practices for protecting the biodiversity of the Bug Valley and handling municipal solid waste, as well as drawing up a handbook of good practices to be implemented by other local governments. As part of the project, protective measures will be implemented in 4 Natura 2000 Areas (The Bug Refuge, the Lower Bug Valley, Poleska Bug Valley, the Middle Bug Valley) and 5 other protected areas (Zakaznyk Verkhobuzkyi Nature Reserve, Sviata Hora Nature Monument, Tadani Nature Reserve, the Fedoriwka Reserve and the Bug Valley Protected Landscape Area). About 3000 people will participate in project activities (study visits, conference, cleaning campaigns, ecological competition and picnics). Thanks to the implementation of the project, each party will benefit primarily in the form of improving the condition of the Bug Valley ecosystem. The region’s attractiveness in terms of tourism development will improve. The Polish-Ukrainian local governments along the Bug River and their organizational units will have the opportunity to establish and strengthen neighborly cooperation and exchange experiences in the field of environmental protection, waste management and eco-education of local communities. The local community will learn how to segregate waste and care for the environment, which they can do on a daily basis to reduce the negative impact on the environment. As a result of the project, residents will also benefit from improving the attractiveness of the region, which will translate into financial gains in tourism. The implementation of the project under the indicated partnership is very important due to the Bug River connecting the entities and the common need to maintain a clean environment, which has a direct impact on daily life of the inhabitants of this region. Implementation of the project on its own would only have a limited impact, which would be of minimal importance in the case of the river ecosystem.

meta.title: DEVELOPMENT OF GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE CROSS-BORDER AREA OF THE SIEDLCE MUNICIPALITY, HORODOK COMMUNITY AND THE PRYVILNE COMMUNITY

card.solution: The project is a response to similar problems identified by the Partners in the PL/UA border region related to insufficient green areas in urbanized areas or their low quality, which directly affects issues of biodiversity conservation in inhabited areas, the occurrence of the urban heat island phenomenon, spatial order, or the implementation of principles of sustainable development as a whole. Through the implementation of the project, the Partners also want to initiate and promote cross-border cooperation in the field of environmental protection, so that actions taken on both sides of the border are consistent with each other and jointly produce a synergetic effect. The main objective of the project is to strengthen the protection of existing green areas and increase the area of green spaces, as well as to preserve biodiversity in the urbanized region of the border through the renovation of 1 park and the construction of 1 park on the UA side as well as the construction of 9 pocket parks on the PL side. The effects of the project will be noticeable in many aspects: - Improvement of the quality of the local natural environment through the protection and increase of green areas conducive to biodiversity conservation, reducing the urban heat island effect, supporting natural retention, and reducing urban pollution - Improvement of quality of life- thanks to the implementation of the project, residents of areas affected by its activities will gain attractive green areas for relaxation and recreation, which will have a positive impact on their well-being and health - Social integration, inclusion of socially excluded individuals in the life of the local community - the opportunity to spend time in a shared attractive public space for residents - Improvement of spatial order and aesthetics of the city through the development of degraded areas The main product: 9 new pocket parks in the city of Siedlce 1 revitalized park in the town of Horodok 1 new park in the municipality of Pryvilne (village of Ivanne) 1 "Action Plan"- a jointly developed document defining the action plan for environmental education in the border areas between PL and UA The main beneficiaries of these products will be the local governments and residents of the project areas, who will gain access to attractive green spaces that directly improve living conditions in urban areas, as well as educational institutions that will receive an innovative document serving as the basis for modern environmental education. However, the infrastructure created/revitalized as part of the project will be accessible to all interested parties, including people with disabilities. When it comes to environmental issues, administrative boundaries are not of great significance. Environmental problems can occur to the same extent on both sides of the border. The border only determines the regulations that apply to the partners regarding nature conservation and climate change prevention. As Poland is a member of the EU it is bound by strict guidelines for its members (such as achieving climate neutrality by 2050). However achieving these goals in the border areas of PL and the EU is not solely dependent on the efforts of individual entities due to the transboundary nature of pollution - the efforts of one side can be undermined by the lack of similar actions on the other side of the border. Therefore joint efforts are needed in the border areas to protect the natural environment as best as possible. With this in mind the applicants have decided to form a partnership and establish a common path for environmental protection in their respective areas and, in general, in the PL/UA border area. Based on the positive results of previous programs the partners hope that their efforts will also serve as motivation for greater interest in protecting the natural resources of the border region as a common good of both countries and lead to the establishment of further transboundary agreements.

meta.title: New historical life of Wiśniowiec and Tarnobrzeg parks

card.solution: Cross-border restoration project of historic parks in Tarnobrzeg (Poland) and Wiśniowiec (Ukraine) and assessment of their ecosystem value in terms of historical development is aimed at improving the condition of the environment, strengthening the protection and preservation of landscape monuments (objects of the nature reserve fund), biodiversity of green infrastructure in urban areas and reducing pollution. The project aims to popularize the value of park plantings for the environment (urboecosystem). As part of this project, it is planned to carry out joint research of the vegetation cover of two parks (Ukrainian and Polish), quantitative and cost indicators of their ecosystem services and development of proposals for improving the ecological condition of facilities and their dissemination. The overriding goal of the project is meeting the recreational, cultural, educational and environmental needs of the residents of the housing estates (Ukrainian and Polish) with the expected increase in environmental awareness of park visitors. The main objective of the project is to improve the ecological condition of historic parks in the border regions of Poland and Ukraine - in Tarnobrzeg and Wiśniowiec, to assess the general condition of the parks in terms of development and implementation of recommendations regarding the improvement of the condition of green areas and their ecological functions. To achieve this goal, the following main directions have been set: - developing a concept for the development/restoration of urban landscapes; - measurement of biometric indicators of trees and shrubs; - determination of quantitative and valuable indicators of ecological functions of trees in terms of their ability to reduce the environmental pollution, carbon sequestration, oxygen production and regulation of the water flow; - analysis of the information received in terms of various ecosystem services, categories of green areas and species composition; - presentation of the information received in the form of an interactive map; - developing possibilities and prospects for presenting the obtained results to local authorities, interested persons and organizations; - implementation of the proposed actions to improve the ecological and aesthetic condition of parks and increasing their ecosystem value. As a result of the project implementation, the following is expected: 1. Preparation of applications regarding the condition of parks and their green areas; 2. Quantitative and qualitative assessment of ecosystem services of two parks; 3. Recommendations for improving the sanitary, aesthetic and ecosystem condition of parks; 4. Ecological effect from the implementation of measures to improve the condition of parks and to increase their ecosystem value; 5. Preservation of the common natural and cultural heritage of Ukraine and Poland; 6. Sustainable use of environmentally valuable areas; 7. Dissemination of experience in the implementation of projects for the protection of landscape monuments - historical parks (organization of a scientific and practical conference, development of methodological recommendations); 8. Raising the ecological awareness of the inhabitants of the nearby housing estates and people visiting the facilities. The main beneficiaries of the project are scientists/researchers of historic parks and biodiversity of objects in Poland and Ukraine, residents of Tarnobrzeg and Wiśniowiec, especially young people, Eco-activists and park visitors. It is planned to use a comprehensive cross-border approach to implement the project with the participation of participants from both countries, scientists, eco-activists and other interested people. Cross-border approach will allow to attract different specialists with varied experience and approach to solving problems and undertaking joint efforts to protect natural and cultural heritage.

meta.title: Biodiversity in the green infrastructure of the Bialystok County and the city of Uzhhorod.

card.solution: The project responds to a number of problems in the Program area, including negative effects of global climate change, drought and water shortages, failure to treat environmental protection as a priority, threats to human activity and the development of infrastructure for natural resources or joint activities related to environmental protection between entities from Poland and Ukraine. Given the uniqueness of the natural resources located in the Program area, it is important to protect them from both climate-related and non-climate-related natural hazards, and from threats related to human activity. Anthropogenic activities negatively affect flora and fauna. A great issue is proper water retention, which causes its excessive accumulation and flooding. To address these issues, the partners plan to implement several innovative cross-border biodiversity activities. The partners decided to create a green infrastructure around their units - the choice fell on hospital infrastructure with large areas to be developed. In the first stage of the project (WP1), research will be commissioned for universities/research units/experts in the field of: analysis of topography, habitats and biodiversity. Bialystok County and Executive Committee of Uzhhorod City Council will conduct a biodiversity study around the hospitals, in which they will determine the selection of appropriate vegetation for biodiversity from the Podlaskie Region and a list of vegetation characteristic of biodiversity from the Transcarpathian Region, issue recommendations on appropriate biodiversity management around the hospital, analyze topography, habitats and biodiversity on the hospital site, prepare recommendations on methods of soil care and biodiversity vegetation planned for planting on the hospital site. Information and results regarding biodiversity will be exchanged between partners. The second stage (WP2, WP3, WP4, WP5) is to increase ecological awareness among the society and to develop the concept of biodiversity in green public infrastructure of partners. Study visits will be held and training will be conducted (e.g. in the field of planning and maintenance of green areas, adaptation to climate change, environmental goals or DNSH - Do No Significant Harm) enabling the cross-border acquisition of knowledge and new skills - training sessions for the participants from Poland and Ukraine who both will atend in equal numbers. The activities of the project will cover a total of 480 people, including: 40 people trained + 140 people participating in joint cross-border events. WP2 will end with the final report "Biodiversity + infrastructure = green urban infrastructure" (1 jointly developed solution). This report will be another comprehensive solution that will later influence the planning of future investments of partners in environmental, social and economic terms. The last implementation stage will be construction and planting works around the hospitals in Lapy (1st stage) and Uzhhorod. These are to be exemplary investments showing how to design and implement infrastructural investments using biodiversity - green infrastructure. The total area of reclaimed land used for green or other areas will be 1.84 hectares. The implementation of this project will allow the achievement of the general objective of the project, which is the development of cross-border biodiversity in the infrastructure of the Bialystok District and the city of Uzhhorod.

meta.title: Cooperation beneficial for the climate – the development of the green infrastructure in Łęczna and Kowel

card.solution: Common challenge and main objective of project is to prevent, mitigate and counteract effects of climate change, protect, preserve and enhance biological diversity of the Polish-Ukrainian region and improve quality of life for people by creating nature- and climate-protecting elements of green infrastructure in Łęczna and Kowel. Subject of project is development of green infrastructure in Łęczna and Kowel through: revitalization of riverside areas and slopes surrounding Old Town, Podzamcze Park and former granary building in Łęczna; arrangement of Świnka River valley area in Łęczna; new plantings; construction of recreational architectural structures in revitalized areas; revitalization of Lesya Ukrainka Central Park and Taras Shevchenko Park as urban green spaces in the center of Kowel and revitalization of green area located next to Center for Dialogue of Cultures along in Kowel with adjoining riverside areas; informational and educational campaign on climate and biodiversity protection; organization of ecological picnics in Łęczna and Kowel as educational events; project opening and closing conference; project promotion; project management. Positive benefits that green infrastructure along with educational activities will bring to partners and the Polish - Ukrainian region: mitigating, alleviating and countering impacts of climate change; ensuring growth of biodiversity by creating of habitats that enable proper functioning of ecosystems; improving condition of natural environment and enhancing of quality of life for people; mitigation of urban heat island effect; increase in share of green infrastructure in total urban area; increased access to green infrastructure located in areas of unique natural and landscape value, including legally protected areas such as the Nadwieprzański Landscape Park; improvement of aesthetics and better utilization of public spaces in Łęczna and Kowel. Informational and educational campaign will provide knowledge and awareness to communities shaping and solidifying appropriate behaviors in caring for environment. Project will strengthen cross-border cooperation between Łęczna and Kowel and foster people-to-people contacts. Project outcomes: Surface of protected and valuable natural sites other than Natura 2000 – 12,70 hectares. Number of supported forms of nature conservation – 2 pcs. Number of carried out information and education campaigns – 1 pc. Jointly developed solutions – 1 pc. Solutions taken up or upscaled by organizations – 1 pc. Rehabilitated land used for green areas – 21.14 hectares. Project is targeted towards local authorities, schools, students and residents of Łęczna, Kowel and the Polish-Ukrainian region. The longstanding collaboration between Łęczna and Kowel has allowed for identification of common problems and challenges in ecological sphere, climate change mitigation, biodiversity protection and improving quality of life for residents, which can be addressed only through joint cross-border project. Project will be implemented through integrated cooperation, coordinated actions and knowledge and experience exchange. Partners will collectively agree on, prepare and actively participate in project activities. Created infrastructure will be accessible to all users. Project outcomes will benefit residents of Łęczna, Kowel, individuals from the Polish-Ukrainian region and beyond. Project actions will lead to achieving common results and goals that will serve partners on both sides of border. Łęczna and Kowel will have ecologically and aesthetically valuable infrastructure for the Polish-Ukrainian region. Łęczna and Kowel are designated as urban centers with supra-local significance tasked with stimulating regional development. Project offers opportunity to influence socio-economic development from local (city) to regional (province/oblast) level. Project creates conditions for increasing social, ecological and landscape attractiveness of both cities and regions.

meta.title: CARPATHIAN YOUTH FOR ECO SMART EDUCATION
meta.institution: State University of Applied Sciences in Jaroslaw

card.solution: The interactive nature center in the Uzhanskyi National Nature Park will not only show visitors the diversity of local flora and fauna, but will also offer exciting interactive exhibits that will turn learning into an interesting journey. The center at Uzhhorod National University, on the other hand, will be more focused on the academic aspect of environmental education and will serve as a platform for research and interdisciplinary cooperation. Both centers will actively engage not only pupils and students, but also a wide range of other visitors and tourists seeking to deepen their knowledge of the Carpathian nature through interactive exhibits, multimedia presentations and excursions to nature reserves. These learning methods are designed to stimulate curiosity, encourage critical thinking, and provide hands-on experiences that make the learning process not only informative but also fun. On the other side of the border in Jaroslaw, an analogous educational center and green areas will be built. The main theme of the center will be the preservation of biodiversity through education in the field of honey bees. The services of the center will be addressed to children, youth, students and the local community.A special topic developed and shown in the center will be the impact of the Carpathian bee on the biodiversity of the region, especially its flora and sustainable agriculture. The interactive center will be used for exercises by students as well as university participants during school trips and study visits The importance of preserving the biodiversity of the Uzhansky and Magursky National Parks cannot be overestimated. These parks are real treasuries of biodiversity and ecosystem balance, which play a key role in preserving the natural heritage of the Carpathians. The project will conduct a comprehensive audit of the ecosystems of these parks, the results of which will be used to develop effective strategies for their conservation and restoration. To popularize knowledge about the unique nature of these parks, albums will be created that describe their biodiversity in detail. These albums will be not only visually appealing, but also scientifically sound, and will be a great addition to educational material for schools and universities. In parallel, the project envisages the implementation of specialized environmental education programs for primary and secondary school students in the border regions. These programs will include practical classes, excursions, and environmental projects to help young people understand the importance of nature conservation and biodiversity. Particular attention will be paid to engaging children and students who will be active participants in all stages of the project, from excursions to scientific research. The tangible results of the project will be numerous. First, the creation of natural science exhibition centers will raise the level of environmental education and awareness in the region. Secondly, the implementation of educational programs will ensure the training of a new generation of citizens capable of responsible attitude to the environment. Third, the cross-border nature of the project.

meta.title: Cross-border Biodiversity - protection of valuable natural areas in Strzyzewice, Chelm, Lviv and Zymna Voda

card.solution: The main objective is to restore and protect the biodiversity of historic parks in Poland and Ukraine. The steps taken will lead to the protecion of areas of natural and cultural value, to slowing down the degradation of nature and to harmonizing the management of natural areas of great importance separated by the state border, and thus to protecting their biodiversity. Historic parks are a valuable natural element of the landscape. Old trees play a huge natural and ecological role - they are a living environment for many organisms, which is important for preserving biodiversity. Many of these organisms are threatened with extinction and owe their existence only to old trees. The project aims to preserve biodiversity by raising awareness and knowledge about the importance of park woodlots as natural habitats. The project focuses on the valorization of the natural resources of historic parks along with the assessment of their condition (dendrological analysis, archaeological research, analysis of water retention in the park, preparation of site and height maps for design purposes, historical query of the park), what will allow planning of long-term protection. The improvement of the condition of trees will translate into the stabilization of historic parks as habitats for animal species that use trees as nesting, feeding, shelter or communication routes, as well as the occurrence of lichens and fungi associated with trees. The project involves the development of concepts, maintenance and protection of old trees in historic parks in the Strzyzewice commune, (Piotrowice), in the area of the Public Provincial Specialist Hospital in Chelm, in the commune of Zymna Voda and in the area of the Saint Yura’s Archcathedral in Lviv, which will allow to preserve valuable natural areas in these regions and to develop common standards for their protection. As a result of the project, the historic gardens (former monastery Gardens of Saint Yura) as three nature monuments of local value will be implemented. They will serve as the park-monument of gardening and the park-monuments of horticultural art in Lviv, Ukraine. As part of the project, trees will also be marked and the Center for the Protection of Ancient Trees will be established in order to create a facility of the nature reserve fund of Ukraine - a botanical nature monument. The project also concerns the purchase of equipment necessary for the proper conduct of research and maintenance of parks. The project will contribute to increasing the awareness and enriching the knowledge of participants about historic parks (managers, local authorities, inhabitants of the region) through study visits, practical training in the assessment of the health condition of trees and conducting environmental and educational activities, training, quests, conferences, purchase of equipment. These affairs, as well as the planned conference and meetings with residents, will allow to exchange experiences and good practices between the participants. The result of these actions will be the joint development of guidelines that will make it easier for park managers to plan and conduct further activities and develompent of the areas. This type of cross-border events receive more media attention, thanks to which there is a chance for good media coverage of the topic of protection of historic parks, and thus also creates possibility to affect the public opinion and decision-makers more effectively. In addition, implementation of the project will build a positive image of nature in the minds of citizens as a common good and a symbol of uniting nations.

meta.title: Urban Lungs – Smart Green Infrastructure Solutions for Urbanized Communities in Poland and Ukraine.

card.solution: Project acronym: UrbanLungs. The project covers the suburbs of the city of Jarosław - town of Wysocko and Pawłosiów in the District of Jarosław in Poland and the city of Uzhhorod in Zakarpattia Oblast of Ukraine. It is addressing the problem described in Specific Objective 1.3 - "Strengthening the protection and conservation of nature, biodiversity and green infrastructure", including urban areas, and reducing all forms of pollution. This is an ambitious plan aimed at reducing rate of pollution, which opens a new chapter of improving of green zones in the project territory. The overall objective of the project is to improve existing and create new urban green areas in the border regions of Poland and Ukraine through the elaboration of scientifically based concepts for revitalization and development of green areas in urban communities in line with the EU standards and climate change responding concepts based on 4 pilot projects in Uzhhorod territorial community and DistrictJaroslaw . The project objectives include the development of scientifically based concepts for the development of green urban areas, the revitalization of 3 existing and the creation of 1 new green zone, as well as the dissemination of best practices and project recommendations among other 75 (64 UA and 11 PL) municipalities in the Zakarpattia Oblast and Podkarpackie Voivodeship. Addressing these challenges requires an integrated approach and the participation of experts in the fields of ecology, biology, landscape design, urbanism, public engagement and sustainable development. It also involves ongoing cooperation with local communities, government agencies and other stakeholders to ensure the success and sustainability of the project. The project will produce reports on the impact of green spaces on pollution and the environment in the cities of Uzhhorod, Wysocko and Pawlosiów, an environmental inventory of green spaces in Tetiana Park in Uzhhorod, a dendrological inventory and a concept for the development of the territory of the Manor and Palace Complex in Pawłosiów and the Palace and Park Complex in Wysocko, as well as recommendations for increasing and/or reviving green spaces for urban communities in the border areas of Poland and Ukraine developed in the course of the project implementation on the basis of scientifically sound concepts. In addition, a number of educational activities will be held for students and secondary school pupils who want to study ecology and urbanism, as well as develop their analytical, critical and practical skills. As a result of the scientific and practical conference, a collection of conference materials, joint methodological recommendations developed based on the results of the research will be published, and a cross-border forum on the importance of implementing green space policy for the sustainable development of border communities in Ukraine and Poland will become a platform for creating a memorandum of cooperation between representatives of Polish and Ukrainian communities and developing a joint algorithm of actions to improve the condition of green areas on the ground. By focusing on the restoration and expansion of green areas in towns and the development of scientifically based methods for revitalizing green spaces, the project not only improves the environmental condition of cities, but also contributes to the creation of a healthy and harmonious environment for communities. The project will unite the strong Ukraininan scientific and pracical expertise in ecology and environmental sciences with Polish experience and knowledge in green zone planning in line with European standarts, that will allow to produce best solutions for PL-UA green infrastructure together with its implementation in practice. It will create not only new partners link at different levels but long-term cross-border effects on reduce air polution in the borderzone.

meta.title: Creation of Cross-Border Centers for Preventive Examinations in Lubelskie and Volyn Regions
meta.institution: Voivodship Occupational Medicine Center, Prevention and Treatment Unit in Lublin

card.solution: Unfavourable socio-demographic phenomena are visible in the program area, which, thanks to undertaking cross-border cooperation, can be a starting point for joint actions and tackling challenges. Common problems, especially in the field of health protection, can be solved jointly by partner regions. In the area of health, the following challenges are observed: 1. An aging society and unfavourable demographic forecasts in both regions, an increasing number of post-working age people with multiple diseases. Cancer is one of the main causes of death, especially in the context of an aging population and limited access to health care. In some areas of both regions, access to preventive examinations is limited. 2. Low awareness of preventive health care: in both regions, the public's awareness of the need for regular preventive examinations is too low. Education and information campaigns are essential to convince residents to participate in such activities. 3. Low level of interregional cooperation in the field of health: interregional cooperation in the field of health is insufficient so far and shows great potential. The project aims to create a platform for mutual exchange of experiences and best practices in the field of preventive health care. Thanks to the planned infrastructural activities and additional equipment, the health infrastructure will be supported, which will improve and access health care in the program area and will contribute to mitigating the effects of unfavourable demographic changes in the common area. Overall objective of the project is establishing the Center for Disease Prevention and Health Promotion in Lublin and Center for Center of Preventive Examinations and Rehabilitation in Lutsk, what will contribute to increasing access to broadly understood preventive care in cross-border areas, constituting a significant step in solving problems in the field of public health. Centers for Preventive Research will serve as key places to achieve this goal, providing access to examinations and diagnostics for the inhabitants of the Lubelskie Voivodeship and Volyn Oblast. The Centers mentioned above will be separated as interdisciplinary units in the structure of: Voivodship Occupational Medicine Center, Prevention and Treatment Unit in Lublin (VOMC in Lublin) and Mother and Child Hospital in Lutsk (MCH in Lutsk), respectively. The infrastructural part of the project includes renovation and purchase of equipment used to provide health services and preventive measures. This action increases the potential of units in the above-mentioned areas and contributes to increasing the availability and quality of health services provided in the field of outpatient specialist care and medical rehabilitation for the inhabitants of both regions. It is planned to develop and implement prevention programs in order to increase awareness of the importance of preventive actions and health promotion among the local inhabitant. The project is addressed to the inhabitants of the Lubelskie Voivodeship and the Volyn Oblast, who will be able to use the infrastructure and widely understood preventive activities. The project is addressed to the medical staff of beneficiaries, who, thanks to cooperation and mutual training, will be able to exchange experiences and knowledge, which may lead to an increasing the quality of services and the development of new innovative approaches in the field of preventive health care. Cross-border action is particularly important and valuable in the context of geographical proximity and similar challenges faced by both regions. Cooperation between them will allow for the use of common resources, exchange of knowledge and experience, and increase in the effectiveness of activities in the field of preventive health care. In addition, the cross-border approach has the potential to bring the communities of both regions closer together.

meta.title: TransCare: Cross-Border healthcare and palliative care
meta.institution: INDEPENDENT PUBLIC HEALTH CARE FACILITY IN SIEDLCE

card.solution: Welcome to the world of the TransCare project! Our project was born in response to a shared challenge faced by both Poland and Ukraine - ensuring high-quality long-term care, especially geriatric, palliative and hospice care in the cross-border region. Together, we aim to develop solutions that will positively impact the lives of our patients. Our main goal is to improve access to long-term care, providing our patients with support and top-level care. We plan to achieve this through three specific objectives. Firstly, we intend to renovate the Hospital building in Siedlce and to purchase necessary medical equipment, as well as to create a gait laboratory in Lutsk. These actions will enable us to create a modern infrastructure tailored to the needs of our patients, including those with disabilities. Secondly, we focus on developing infrastructure for geriatric, palliative and hospice care to ensure effective rehabilitation, swift diagnosis and treatment of patients both in stationary settings and in their places of residence. The new medical equipment will be crucial in providing efficient long-term care. Thirdly, we invest in the qualifications and effectiveness of medical staff by organizing joint Polish-Ukrainian training sessions. Collaboration and knowledge exchange in the cross-border region will allow us to develop common solutions and enhance the quality of long-term care. We are aware of the ongoing war in Ukraine due to Russia's aggression, necessitating innovative approaches to providing care outside of hospitals. As part of our collaboration, we will develop a concept which will enable and facilitate the implementation of mobile medical brigades. The publication on organizing and functioning of these services at patients' homes will be distributed on partner websites and among other medical units. Thus, our experiences and knowledge will be accessible to others, helping to develop similar solutions and improve healthcare quality in the region. As a result of our efforts, we will establish a modernized foundation for long-term care and provide new medical equipment to improve care standards. Our actions will impact not only patients and staff but also the local community, other healthcare facilities, the partners themselves and our founding entities (local government). Our cross-border approach is essential because both sides face similar challenges and need joint solutions. Cooperation among partners will enable us to more effectively achieve project objectives, to exchange knowledge and experience, as well as to tailor solutions to the specific needs of the cross-border region. Together, we will develop innovative solutions regarding mobile palliative care brigades, enhancing the healthcare quality for our patients. Our TransCare project is not only about caring for patients' health but also about building bridges between our countries, benefiting not just us but the entire community. Together, as a united team, we will tackle the challenges of an ageing society, civilization diseases and crisis situations. Our project is a unique opportunity to improve the quality of life for our patients, to build stronger cross-border cooperation and to create innovative solutions in long-term healthcare. TransCare is a joint journey that is only just beginning!

meta.title: Joint development of accessible and resilient health care for elderly and disabled patients of Bialystok and Volyn hospitals
meta.institution: Autonomous Public Health Maintenance Organisation Jędrzej Śniadecki Voivodship Polyclinical Hospital in Bialystok

card.solution: The project is a joint response of Autonomous Health Maintenance Organization Jędrzej Śniadecki Voivodship Polyclinical Hospital in Bialystok and the municipal enterprise “Volyn Regional Hospital of War Veterans” to the insufficient access to modern and effective health care, especially for elderly and disabled people, in Białystok and Volyn regions. The project overall objective is to improve accessibility and resilience of cross border health care for elderly and disabled people through modernization of Białystok and Volyn hospitals’ infrastructure and equipment. Overall project objective will be achieved through: - improvement of treatment base for elderly and disabled patients by purchase of specialized medical equipment for both hospitals and modernisation of hospital departments - supporting of resilience of public health systems by joint development and sharing of treatment methodologies for elderly or disabled patients in hospitals and dissemination and exchange of good practices and knowledge between medical staff - supporting the family members of patients in care of elderly and disabled people (consultations, information campaign) in Partner’s hospitals. The health care for elderly and disabled people, including those who have suffered from wars will be more efficient, average length of stay in internal medicine department will shorten. Modernisation of hospital premises will create better conditions for treatment, increased hygienic conditions will decrease possibility of nosocomial infections, purchase of medical equipment enabling certain examinations directly at the patient’s bed and facilitating self-mobility will speed up recovery and hospital stay will be shortened. The modernized hospital wards will be adapted to the elderly people and people with disabilities needs and more accessible. The target group of the Project will be both Partners hospitals and their employees, while the final beneficiaries of the Project will be the patients of the partner hospitals. The patient group consists of the inhabitants of the borderland region as well as tourists and any individuals in the emergency situations; also refugees staying in the cross border area. The impact of the project concerns improvement of accessibility and resilience of health services – the problem important for both sides of the Polish-Ukrainian border through modernization of infrastructure, purchase of specialized medical equipment, professional development of doctors and specialists taking part in the project and sharing their knowledge with the foreign partners, support for patients’ families and caretakers. Jointly developed by hospitals from both countries methodologies base on experiences and knowledge of specialists and institutions from both sides of the border and show a clear cross-border value, impossible to achieve without this cooperation, reflecting joint approach of both hospitals and generating synergy effect. Developed methodologies will allow to take care and treat elderly patients with regard to their specificity, special needs and multi-morbidity in different hospital wards in situation, when specialist care in geriatric wards is limited. Developed solutions, sent to medical institutions in the Programme area, accessible on Partners’ websites, will be a useful tool of medical care in the Programme area. Medical staff from both sides will work together during workshops and working group activities, using and exchange their everyday experience for finding the best solutions for better health care services. Direct meetings and online consultations of medical staff during trainings, workshops and working group works will result in mutual learning and creating new solutions and modern approaching to the problems, which could be disseminated in the Programme area.

meta.title: A joint initiative of The Dr. Jozef Psarski Mazovian Specialist Hospital in Ostroleka and Municipal Non-Profit Company “First Clinical Territorial Medical Union of Lviv" as increasing the availability of health care services.
meta.institution: The Dr. Jozef Psarski Mazovian Specialist Hospital in Ostroleka

card.solution: The most important and the biggest challenge in the field of the project is the long transport time of patients (Ostroleka) and the shortcomings in medical equipment - angiograph (Lviv). Therefore, the main objective of the project, both in Poland and Ukraine, will be to investigate and then mitigate the negative impact of long patient transport times and the quality of medical equipment on the level of health care, this will lead to improved access, fast and effective emergency medicine and modern healthcare in both hospitals. The following specific objective of the project will lead to the achievement of the general objective: 1.Modernization of the infrastructure in the Mazovian Ostroleka Specialist Hospital (helicopter landing site) and modernization with the help of an angiograph as part of the modernization of the medical infrastructure of the vascular surgery department of the hospital in Lviv – by creating conditions of care in Ukrainian and Polish healthcare facilities. 2.Joint meetings, exchange of good practices, workshops and training in cardiology, vascular surgery and emergency medicine - will affect the preparation and implementation of innovative procedures used in: a. medical rescue and solving the problem of the impact of long patient transport time (Ostroleka and Lviv) on the effectiveness of treatment; b. in the field of vascular surgery, modern methods of treating stroke (experience exchange, training) - collecting, testing and further dissemination of best treatment practices in the Ukrainian-Polish borderland. In the case of the hospital in Ostroleka, the most important factor that has a very negative impact on the use of quick and effective rescue procedures is the long time of transporting patients to individual departments, resulting from the distance of the current landing site from the hospital's emergency department. Measurements carried out in Ostroleka show that the time from landing the helicopter to reaching the appropriate branch is even more than an hour. This long time significantly affects the effectiveness of subsequent rescue operations. In the case of a hospital in Lviv, the problem is the lack of modern equipment for angiographic examinations, and the current device is already exhausted –which does not allow to conduct research in a proper and effective way. The current situation in Ukraine related to the war, internal migration and the increase in the number of patients requires equipping the hospital in Lviv with a new angiograph. This equipment will enable the diagnosis and treatment of various cardiovascular diseases, providing patients with accurate and timely assistance. An important element is the establishment of cooperation between specialists of both – hospital institutions in the framework of joint research, working teams, mutual visits and exchange of experience in the field of emergency medicine, cardiology and vascular surgery, what will affect the quality of medical care of both hospitals. This will increase the level of knowledge of medical staff, the use of the latest medical solutions and the possibility of using specialized equipment. Thanks to this, the hospital in Ostroleka will support its partner in the field of vascular surgery and highly specialized methods of treating patients after mechanical thrombectomy in the Department of Vascular Surgery of the Mazovian Specialist Hospital in Ostrolece. The hospital in Ukraine, will provide support from crisis management and the impact of patient transport time on the effectiveness of the emergency department. The procedures will be developed by a joint working team composed of specialists of hospitals in Ostroleka and Lviv. Participation in this work will be in equal proportions and will require on-line working meetings to develop appropriate practices, resulting in creation of target – procedures adapted to legal regulations in Poland and Ukraine.

meta.title: Improvement of health safety in the Losice district and Ivano-Frankivsk city
meta.institution: Independent Public Health Care Center in Losice

card.solution: The project involves cross-border cooperation between the Independent Public Health Care Center in Losice (Poland) and Central City Clinical Hospital of Ivano-Frankivsk City Council (Ukraine) in improving access to medical transport and diagnostics. The joint initiative responds to the problem identified in the joint strategy of the Interreg NEXT PL-UA 2021-2027 Programme, i.e. the growing number of people in the post-productive age and thus the ever-increasing need for healthcare. A particular area of concern is medical transport, which is most often used by seniors with limited mobility, including residents of rural areas, who find it very difficult to get to hospital due to the poor bus network/lack of a car. The project involves investment in public services to improve the well-being of an ageing population and mitigate the effects of adverse demographic changes on the population of the project partners' catchment area. Investment and education activities in the organisation of medical transport also support the resilience of health care systems in Poland and Ukraine, as they allow good access to health care facilities in crisis situations, such as war or the COVID-19 pandemic. In crisis situations, access to state emergency teams is limited, so hospitals and local governments through their autonomous actions can improve it. The main objective of the project is to improve access to medical transport and diagnostics in the Łosice district and the city of Ivano-Frankivsk. As a result of the project, the hospital in Losice will modernise and extend the hospital building with regard to the ambulance ramp and the adjacent surgical clinic, so that patients are helped as quickly as possible after arriving at the hospital by ambulance. In addition, the Polish hospital will, as a result of the project, replace one obsolete ambulance and three colonoscopes and gastroscopes with a video track each, which are used for the diagnosis of patients admitted to the reception area. Hospital in Ivano-Frankivsk has planned to purchase 2 ambulances as part of the project, (one of which will be equipped with a mobile X-ray machine for the rapid diagnosis of patients) and portable USG for diagnosis of patients in ambulances. The ambulances will be directly used for emergency medical services in the city and surrounding areas, including to help those affected by warfare. The project will have a positive impact on access to medical transport and imaging and endoscopic diagnostics among the inhabitants of the Polish-Ukrainian border region, in particular the Łosice district and the city of Ivano-Frankivsk, with a total population of nearly 260,000, of which nearly 90% are inhabitants of the Ukrainian city. Through cooperation, the project partners will improve access to medical transport and diagnostics in their areas of operation, while increasing the quality of medical infrastructure. Ukrainian language training has also been planned for the medical staff of the Losice Hospital, so that better medical assistance can be provided to the Ukrainian population in the Losice district. Residents of the Losice poviat and the city of Ivano-Frankivsk will have the opportunity within the framework of the project to enjoy educational events in the form of picnics, which will familiarise them with the principles of medical transport - both in their area of residence and in crisis situations such as war. At the same time, education will be provided on the proper use of emergency medical team calls, in view of the large number of unnecessary ambulance calls. The project will also have a multiplier effect - as a result of the project, a set of procedures will be created to be applied in situations of inefficiency of the state rescue system i.e. in emergency situations. In addition, a lesson handbook will be prepared for use by Polish and Ukrainian schools on the circumstances of calling a medical emergency team.

meta.title: Healthy and fit inhabitants of the Hrubieszow district and Luck region
meta.institution: Independent Public Health Care Complex in Hrubieszów

card.solution: The project involves cross-border cooperation between Independent Public Health Care Complex in Hrubieszow (Poland) and Rozhysche multidisciplinary hospital of Rozhysche city council (Ukraine) in the field of diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation of musculoskeletal disorders. The joint initiative responds to a problem identified in the joint Interreg NEXT PL-UA 2021-2027 Program strategy, i.e. the growing number of people in the post-productive age, and thus the increasing demand for health care. A special area of it is rehabilitation, from which largely benefited by seniors who are exposed to disabilities related both to the natural aging process and to injuries and overloads recorded during their working lives. The project involves investment in public services aimed at improving the well-being of the aging population and mitigating the effects of adverse demographic changes on the population in the area of influence of the project partners. Investment and training activities in the field of rehabilitation also support the resilience of health care systems in Poland and Ukraine. They allow to maintain as large a percentage of the population in labor activity, thereby reducing the risk of having to provide more personnel or hospital beds necessary for medical care of the disabled and elderly people. Keeping elderly people in healthy for as long as possible and early rehabilitation of people after physical injury, will help limit the increase in the number of disabled people (which brings with it the need for more financial outlays and additional staff resources needed to care for these people). The main objective of the project is to improve access to high-quality therapeutic rehabilitation of the musculoskeletal and nervous system in the Hrubieszow district and Lutsk region. As a result of the project, the Hospital in Hrubieszow will modernize and equip with kinesitherapy and physical therapy equipment, as well as furniture eqipment and IT equipment to inpatient and day rehabilitation department. Hospital in Rozhysche will purchase for the treatment of musculoskeletal diseases and neurological conditions, equipment for diagnostics (tomograph, ultrasound, electronegraph) surgical procedures (arthroscope, mobile operating table) and rehabilitation. The project will positively influence the rehabilitation and treatment of diseases of musculoskeletal and nervous systems among the residents of the Polish-Ukrainian border region, in particular, the Hrubieszow district and three hromadas of Lutsk region, i.e. Rozhysche, Kopachivka i Dorosyn, with a total population of nearly 100,000 population. Through cooperation, the project partners will improve the quality of the medical infrastructure in their hospitals and implement an extended rehabilitation offer. This offer will increase the hospitals' capacity to treat and restore the mobility of patients with musculoskeletal and neurological diseases. Will also be organised four training trips to rehabilitation and sanatorium centres in eastern Poland and western Ukraine, and will be provided training for physiotherapists. The project will also have a multiplier effect - as a result of the project will be created educational materials with the discussion of clinical and functional aspects of musculoskeletal dysfunctions most commonly occurring in the Hrubieszow poviat and Lutsk region. These dysfunctions include diseases of the spine, joints of the spine, hip and knee joints, consequences of strokes, and in particular also the consequences of accidents in agriculture, which is one of the most important economic sectors in both regions.

meta.title: Polish-Ukrainian Transborder Heart Care Collaboration
meta.institution: Cardinal Stefan Wyszynski Voivodeship Hospital in Lomza

card.solution: The project involves cross-border cooperation between Cardinal Stefan Wyszynski Voivodeship Hospital in Lomza (Poland) and Municipal non-profit enterprise "Lviv Territorial Medical Union - Multidisciplinary Clinical Hospital of Emergency and Intensive Care" (Ukraine) in the field of cardiology, with particular emphasis on diagnostic invasive and interventional cardiology. The joint initiative responds to the problems identified in the joint Interreg NEXT Programme PL-UA 2021-2027 strategy, i.e. - the growing number of people in the post-working age group, and thus the increasing need for healthcare, - high percentage of deaths due to cardiovascular diseases (41.5% in Poland and 56.5% in Ukraine) - inequalities in access to highly specialised healthcare in the Podlaskie voivodeship between the capital of the region and the rest of the region, - the lack of digitalisation of healthcare on the Ukrainian side. The project concerns investment in public services aimed at improving the health of the ageing population and mitigating the effects of adverse demographic changes in the border area. The main objective of the project is to improve access to specialised: diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases in the Polish-Ukrainian cross-border area. As a result of the project, the Voivodship Hospital in Lomza will acquire software for archiving, transferring, analysing and interpreting cardiovascular examinations, a modern angiograph and adapted premises for the use of the new device within a hybrid room, enabling the implementation of necessary interventions in the area of vascular surgery during the same operation. The Lviv Territorial Medical Union will purchase specialised medical equipment for the Heart and Vascular Centre at St Pantaleon Hospital, which is part of the organisation, i.e. ECMO, cardiac monitors, anesthetic breathing apparatus, an echocardiograph and a defibrillator. Integration with the dedicated cardiology software for the Lomza Hospital is also envisaged, so that angiography and echocardiography results will also be digitised at St. Pantaleon Hospital in Lviv. The project will have a positive impact on access to highly specialised cardiac care among the inhabitants of the Polish-Ukrainian border region, in particular Lviv, Lomza and the four counties of the Lomza sub-region, i.e. Kolno, Lomza, Wysokie Mazowieckie and Zambrow. The implemented hybrid room at the Lomza Voivodship Hospital will be only the second such room in the Podlaskie Voivodship, and the new procedures planned for cardiac surgery and interventional cardiology at the St. Pantaleon Hospital in Lviv will serve in particular people with post-traumatic stress disorder caused by warfare in eastern Ukraine, so the impact of the project will be even greater in the future. Thanks to their cooperation, the project partners will implement an expanded range of cardiac procedures, including invasive diagnostics, at their hospitals, which will increase the hospitals' capacity to treat and maintain the fitness of people of working and post-working age. Medical consiliums of eminent specialists from both hospitals will additionally jointly discuss the disease cases of certain patients with indications for interventional cardiology, so that they will receive an even better level of medical care. The project will also have a multiplier effect, as it will result in a scientific publication (which can also be used in other centres) on the treatment and diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases caused by post-traumatic stress.

meta.title: Children are the future - investments to improve the quality and accessibility of medical services at children's hospitals in Bialystok and Mukachevo
meta.institution: Ludwik Zamenhof's University Children's Clinical Hospital of Bialystok

card.solution: Despite the differences in the functioning of the public health care systems in Poland and Ukraine, health care units on both sides of the border face similar problems. Hospitals have been underfunded for years, which limits the availability of quality services. There’s a shortage of both equipment and medical staff. The situation has been exacerbated in recent years as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. In addition, the armed conflict on UA territory has increased the needs of the health system in both UA and PL, particularly in areas where there is an increase in refugees. For more than a year, refugee children from UA have been admitted to the Bialystok Hospitals and today account for approximately 8% of the number of hospital admissions. Western UA health units are reporting an increase in patients. The situation calls for intervention and support of health care systems on both sides of the border. The project will be implemented in a specific area-children's hospitals. The UA partner, hospital in Mukachevo, is facing new challenges: in addition to an increase in the total number of patients, the number of patients in the trauma and orthopaedic and psychiatric wards has increased significantly. This trend is a direct result of the escalation of the armed conflict in UA. Children are experiencing the effects of war on an equal footing with adults: they are suffering from complex injuries, they are suffering from restricted access to health care units, they are suffering from psychological trauma. The trauma experienced by children due to the necessity to leave home, to integrate in a new environment, the information about the loss of loved ones causes psychological trauma that stays with them for many years. The analysis of the situation has shown that it is important to support hospitals to improve diagnostic and treatment processes. An additional defined problem is to ensure that health records are kept and made available in electronic form (EHR). Due to the increase in the number of patients, more and more diagnostic examinations in electronic form, the demand for IT infrastructure increases. A separate problem is making health records available to patients in countries with different legal systems. We are all aware that a huge number of today's refugees will return to their country and their obvious right will be to access health records even after several years. In the area of IT, cyber security in the area of health is an important problem. In response to the above-described problems, children's hospitals from Bialystok and Mukachevo have decided to jointly implement a project aimed at improving the quality of medical services provided in both facilities by: - establishing long-term cooperation consisting of the exchange of good practices of medical staff, creating a basis for medical consultations between the units - jointly developing a mechanism for providing access to EHR, which, in accordance with the law in force in both countries, will allow refugees to view their records after the end of the armed conflict and return to UA - improvement of the IT infrastructure by acquiring hardware and software and organising training on the functioning of modern hospital IT systems and cyber-security - upgrading of staff competencies in areas relevant to the needs of the units - retrofitting of medical equipment to the hospitals resulting from a needs audit conducted in both units The above-mentioned activities require a cross-border approach and cooperation between the units located on both sides of the border due to: - different competencies of the medical staff of the partners - the possibility of supporting UA medical staff in the psychological care of young Ukrainian patients at the hospital in Bialystok - the knowledge of the law and the HIS systems in PL and UA, which would allow solutions to be developed to enable access to the EHR by patients treated in both countries even many years after the medical intervention.

meta.title: Joint development of rehabilitation services at municipal's hospitals in Bialystok and Volodymyr

card.solution: Despite the differences in the functioning of the public health care systems in Poland (PL) and Ukraine (UA), health care units on both sides of the border face similar problems. There is a shortage of both equipment and medical staff. A particularly difficult situation is noticeable in the field of: - rehabilitation services in both hospitals - the increased need for rehabilitation services results from the armed conflict in UA and the aging population on both sides of the border. - in PCK’s wards - Internal Medicine with a Cardiac and Gastroenterology profiles – the growing number of patients in the wards results from, among others, the large number of Ukrainian refugees staying in Bialystok and the fast and stressful lifestyle of the borderland inhabitants, which leads to an increased number of heart diseases and problems with the digestive system and intestines. - psychological support for patients in difficult situation - some of patients who are placed on hospital are frustrated by the diagnosis received or the lack of progress in treatment. They are very often single people who can’t count on the support of family or relatives. The depression, apathy and neurosis that patients are suffering from is not helpful for their treatment. For such people, the treatment process is prolonged and, consequently, hospital costs increase. The situation requires intervention and support to health systems on both sides of the border. The analysis of the situation showed that it is important to support hospitals to improve diagnostic and treatment processes. In response to all this problems Partners decided to jointly implement a project aimed at improving access to high quality medical services at both facilities through: - investment in infrastructure and equipment, which will benefit patients and hospital staff. There is a need to renovate 3 wards in PCK hospital: Rehabilitation clinic, Internal Medicine with a cardiac and Gastroenterology profiles. These wards receive the largest number of patients from the entire hospital. Patients will receive comprehensive care in the hospital. First, thanks to modern equipment, they will be properly diagnosed and treated. The new class of devices enables more accurate and precise diagnostics and therefore makes it easier for doctors to make a proper diagnosis and choose the right treatment. In next step, the doctor will select an appropriate package of rehabilitation services. This approach will mean that after being discharged from the hospital, the patient will not have to look for and wait for rehabilitation in another center. Finally treatment will take place in a comfortable enviorment. - improving staff competences in areas relevant to the needs of the units, with a particular focus on innovative methods in rehabilitation and pain management, through training courses and study visits for hospital staff - establishing long-term cooperation through the exchange of good practice among medical staff, creating the basis for teleconsultation between units, which will benefit patients and staff of the units - improving the IT infrastructure through the purchase of equipment and software, including for teleconsultation and the organisation of training courses on cyber-security, which will benefit hospital staff and patients. All activities implemented in the project will contribute to ensuring equal access to healthcare and increasing the resilience of healthcare systems in the project area. The above activities require cooperation between units located on both sides of the border due to: - the different competencies of the medical staff of the partners - the possibility to support the PL partner in the implementation by the UA side of a gait laboratory and the practical use of biomechanical variables in the identification and treatment planning of movement disorders, - the different approaches of both parties to the psychological care of patients, - growing threats in the area of cyber security.

meta.title: The goal - healthy human "engines" in Lutsk and Pulawy: improvement of assistance for people with heart attacks and strokes in the Lutsk Community and Pulawy
meta.institution: Independent Public Health Care Center in Pulawy

card.solution: The identified deficits in the area of health care in the area of Pulawski District and Volyn Region relate to diseases affecting the largest percentage of residents described as civilization-related. The needs of both communities are very similar, which is why the partners decided on joint implementation of activities, which will allow the use of common experience and knowledge leading to a synergistic effect. The main objective of the planned project is to counteract civilization diseases in the Pulawy district and Volyn region. The goal of the project is in the common interest of the partners, which is to increase the awareness of the population and improve preventive and diagnostic measures with particular emphasis on the area of neurology, cardiology and cancer. The specific objectives are: - Increase access to preventive measures in the areas of cardiovascular, neurological and oncological diseases, -Improving the quality of the diagnostic process - by reducing waiting times, increasing the precision of the tests performed and introducing new procedures. Achievement of specific goals will be possible by increasing the number and accuracy of medical procedures performed in the facilities as a result of the purchase of modern specialized medical equipment. Fast diagnostics on precise equipment will affect the acceleration of the therapeutic process. Coordinated educational and promotional activities will be an additional element enabling the achievement of the set goals. The project will add value to the program strategy by achieving the following indicators: -Capacity of new or upgraded health care facilities - 95,000 people/year. As a result of the investment, the capacity of Independent Public Health Care Center in Pulawy will be 55,000 persons/year, and Municipal Enterprise Medical Association of the Lutsk City Territorial Community will be 40,000 persons/year. The value of the indicator was determined on the basis of historical data and real forecasts related to medical procedures covered by the project. -Commonly developed solutions - 1 solution The jointly developed solution will be a "Handbook on cross-border cooperation for medical institutions”, developed jointly by Independent Public Health Care Center in Pulawy & Municipal Enterprise Medical Association of the Lutsk City Territorial Community. -Annual number of users of new or upgraded healthcare facilities - 95,000 users/year. As a result of the investment, the annual number of users of the Independent Public Health Care Center in Pulawy will be 55,000 persons/year, and Municipal Enterprise Medical Association of the Lutsk City Territorial Community 40,000 persons/year. The value of indicator was determined on the basis of historical data and realistic forecasts related to the medical procedures covered by the project. The results of the project will benefit: residents of the Pulawy municipality and Pulawy County, as well as the Lutsk municipality and employees of IPHCC in Pulawy and Municipal Enterprise Medical Association of the Lutsk City Territorial Community. Implementation of the planned scope alone would not have been possible, while the purchase of equipment and modernization of premises could have been implemented without the participation of a partner, the scope of educational activities (study visit and training, including the performance of tests on the purchased equipment) and the planned preventive program would not have been possible to implement at such a high level without the assumed cooperation between Independent Public Health Care Center in Pulawy and Municipal Enterprise Medical Association of the Lutsk City Territorial Community. The mere purchase of equipment by each of the partners separately would not allow to achieve the goals and indicators that will be possible only through the synergy effect. The cooperation of partners, the exchange of knowledge and experience is a key element allowing the realization of all the adopted goals.
