meta.title: Improving access to eye care in the Polish-Ukrainian cross-border region

card.solution: The joint challenge for Partners of the project is to improve access to medical care and to increase the quality level of medical services in transnational areas. The Programme area is mostly poorly inhabited - average inhabitation density is 80 persons per km2. In both countries decrease of number of inhabitants has been noted. Demographic prognosis tend to show further decrease trends for the majority of regions participating in the Programme. The ageing society also means more ill persons requiring medical care. Unfortunately, differences among sub-regions of the area covered by the Programme are clearly visible as far as an access to medical care is concerned. These problems co-relate also with the lack of staff. The access to diagnostics, emergency care and preventive procedures is of a crucial importance to people’s health on both sides of the border, hence it should be supported. In addition, COVID- 19 pandemic turned out to be a serious threat to the effectiveness of health care, however, much greater challenge for Ukrainian system of medical care are the results of war. In order to solve these problems, it is necessary to further maintain and develop transnational cooperation between medical services of both countries. The project is of a crucial importance for the improvement of an access to high quality medical care and supporting the patients in the Partners’ areas. Hence, this will help in solving of the identified issues in both facilities on both sides of the border It is strictly connected with priority 2: HEALTH of the Programme Interreg NEXT Poland-Ukraine 2021- 2027: Providing an equal access to medical care and supporting the resistance of medical care, including the basic medical care, and supporting the transfer from institutional care to home and community care. The project is an answer to identified shortages and includes activities leading to the increase of number of the conducted ophthalmic operations. As a result, it will translate into increased access and quality of providing medical care in Debica and Ternopil. Main target of the project is to create durable cross-border cooperation between medical units in Poland and Ukraine, for the purpose of increasing the access to high-quality medical services in the region. The main products of the project will be as follows: 1.Operating theatre equipped with modern medical devices. 2.Ophthalmic Unit in Ternopil provided with modern equipment for eye microsurgery 3.Conferences, meetings and trainings for medical staff. The project will have a significant transnational impact on both sides of the border, including the project Partners, target groups and the area included in the Programme. 1.Benefits for the Partners One of the targets of joint performance of the project is the exchange of experiences in the scope of eye microsurgery and joint development of qualifications of medical teams working in Ophthalmic Units in Medical Care Centres in Debica and in Municipal Non-commercial Enterprise "Ternopil Regional Clinical Hospital". Cooperation between medical facilities from Poland and Ukraine will create stable partnership network which may lead to future projects and transnational initiatives helping to support innovations and the quality of medical care in the area. 2. Benefits for target groups An access to medical services will be improved. Patients from both sides of the border, including the elderly, will be able to benefit from the effects of the project performance - new operating theatre and special equipment. The hospital will significantly shorten waiting time for surgery for patients. Benefits will be felt on both sides of the border. Joint cooperation allows for maximum usage of resources and abilities of both countries which translates into more efficiency in achieving the project’s goals. Thanks to the project actions, the quality and availability of medical services will be significantly improved.

meta.title: Look inside yourself - increasing access to specialized diagnostic imaging in the Polish-Ukrainian border area
meta.institution: St. John Paul II Mazovian Voivodeship Hospital in Siedlce Ltd.

card.solution: The project involves cross-border cooperation between St. John Paul II Mazovian Voivodeship Hospital in Siedlce Ltd. (Poland) and Communal non-commercial enterprise of the Lviv Regional Council Lviv Regional Clinical Diagnostic Center (Ukraine) in improving access to high-quality imaging diagnostics, with particular emphasis on magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography. The joint initiative responds to the problems identified in the joint strategy of the Interreg NEXT PL-UA 2021-2027 Program strategy, namely. - the growing number of people in the post-working age group, and thus the growing need for health care, - high percentage of deaths caused by cancer (26.5% in Poland and 13.4% in Ukraine) - deficiencies in the digitization of health care on the Ukrainian side. The project involves investment in public services aimed at improving the health well-being of an aging population and mitigating the effects of adverse demographic changes in the border area. The main objective of the project is to improve access to high-quality imaging diagnostics in the field of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging in the Polish-Ukrainian cross-border area. As a result of the project, the Mazovian Regional Hospital in Siedlce will modernize the premises of the Imaging Diagnostics Department, including moving a second CT scanner from an external container to its target location in the building, purchase and implement new IT equipment, stations for preparing descriptions of X-ray, CT and MRI examinations, and implement modern software for teleradiology with extension of speech transcription, management of imaging results and their analysis with the possibility of using AI. Imaging diagnostic department will also gain queue management system for efficient patient registration for medical examinations. The Lviv Regional Clinical Diagnostic Center, in turn, will replace an outdated MRI dating back to 2007 (the replacement will be preceded by necessary adaptation work in the laboratory premises), as well as purchase and implement equipment to create a digital archive of medical images and a call center for patient appointments. The project will positively influence access to specialized diagnostic imaging among the residents of the Polish-Ukrainian borderland, especially the Siedlce subregion and Lviv region. The solutions for the organization and description of CT and MRI examinations of both hospitals will be among the unique ones in the entire Polish-Ukrainian borderland. Thanks to the cooperation, the project partners will implement software for managing the documentation of imaging results in their hospitals, as well as improve the state of the diagnostic facilities' infrastructure in terms of IT equipment, medical apparatus and the condition of the laboratories' premises, which will increase the hospitals' ability to diagnose, treat and keep healthy people belonging primarily to cancer risk groups. The undertaking will also have a multiplier effect - as a result of the project, medical procedures will be created for the preparation of descriptive protocols for magnetic resonance imaging and CT scans, as well as the establishment of priorities for urgently ordered examinations. The material will take into account the simplification and standardization of processes for organizing and describing examinations, which may translate into shorter waiting times for both the examination itself and its accurate description. The project will also include specialized training for the staff of both partners, i.e. doctors, nurses and radiology technicians, among others, in the interpretation of imaging results, the use of model medical procedures for describing examinations, prioritization of examinations when there are many urgent cases among the waiting list, as well as in the area of new diagnostic techniques, including the use of AI as a tool to assist and reduce the time for preparing the examination description.

meta.title: Ensuring accessibility of health care services to patients with cardiovascular diseases in the Polish-Ukrainian border area through modernization of medical infrastructure and equipment
meta.institution: Autonomous Public Health Maintenance Organisation Jędrzej Śniadecki Voivodship Polyclinical Hospital in Bialystok

card.solution: The project is a joint response of Autonomous Health Maintenance Organization Jędrzej Śniadecki Voivodship Polyclinical Hospital in Bialystok and Yuri Semenyuk Rivne Regional Clinical Hospital to poor access to the health care system in the provision of diagnostics and treatment in cardiovascular diseases in borderland area (Białystok region and Rivne Oblast) which results in high mortality and disability rate of the population. The project overall objective is to improve jointly accessibility and resilience of health services in cardiovascular diseases in Białystok region and Rivne Oblast by modernization of medical infrastructure and equipment, knowledge exchange and prophylaxis promotion. Overall project objective will be achieved through: - improvement of treatment base for cardiovascular diseases by purchase of specialized medical equipment for both hospitals and reconstruction of operating block in Yuri Semenyuk Rivne Regional Clinical Hospital; - supporting of resilience of public health systems by dissemination and exchange of good practices and knowledge between medical staff; - improve the awareness of prophylaxis of cardiovascular diseases among patients and inhabitants of the Programme area by organization of open days – preventive actions and promotion of healthy life style The result of project realization will be enhanced access to health care in the provision of diagnostics and treatment in cardiovascular diseases. Both Partners hospitals and their employees, and also the patients of the partner hospitals as the final beneficiaries of the Project will benefit from joint project realization. The patient group consists of the inhabitants of the borderland region as well as tourists and any individuals in the emergency situations; also refugees staying in the crossborder area, inhabitants of Białystok region and Rivne oblast in the age 18+. As a result of the project implementation, used/insufficient medical infrastructure for cardiovascular diseases diagnosis and treatment will be improved by purchase of specialized medical equipment and modernization of medical infrastructure (better anghiography, faster diagnosis with CT use). Specialist knowledge about new CVD treatments will be improved by dissemination and exchange of good practices and knowledge during 2 conferences and 4 trainings. Experience exchange workshops on hospital management and resilience of health care systems will give a chance for familiarizing with management issues and procedures in both hospitals: Rivne hospital will share its experience of acting in difficult conditions caused by war in Ukraine, while Białystok hospital in accessibility. Awareness about prophylaxis of cardiovascular diseases and healthy lifestyle among Białystok region and Rivne oblast inhabitants will be increased by dissemination of knowledge among patients through open days organization and joint information campaign. meta.title: Cross-border Interaction for Modern Diagnostic & Therapeutic Approaches at Regional Hospitals of Lublin Voivodeship and Zakarpattia
meta.institution: Stefan Cardinal Wyszyński Provincial Specialist Hospital Independent Public Health Care Centre in Lublin

card.solution: Two partnering regions - Lublin and Uzhhorod - are facing difficulties in the modern diagnostic and therapeutic methods in the field of cardiovascular diseases and diseases requiring neurosurgical treatment in particular of victims of military conflicts. Victims of war are any person who suffers from armed conflicts, hostilities or wars. These injuries can have a variety of forms and affect both the body and the psyche. Experiencing war or experiencing traumatic conflict-related events can lead to chronic stress and mental disorders such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These emotional states can increase the risk of heart disease by affecting the cardiovascular system, increasing blood pressure and leading to unhealthy behaviors such as excessive alcohol consumption or smoking. Wars often destabilize societies, leading to a loss of access to basic health services, education and work. This, in turn, can affect people's lifestyles, leading to a worse diet, lack of physical activity and other risk factors for heart disease. Likewise wars can disrupt food supplies and lead to nutritional shortages. Lack of access to healthy and balanced meals can increase the risk of heart disease by affecting cholesterol, blood sugar and blood pressure. During war, health systems are often overloaded or completely destroyed. This leads to difficult access to medical care and medication, which can negatively affect the control of chronic diseases, including heart disease. Also can lead to the release of toxic substances, such as chemicals or radioactive substances, which can have a negative impact on the health of the heart and blood vessels. During wars and armed conflicts, the risk of physical injuries, including chest and heart injuries, increases. This can lead to serious cardiovascular complications. Therefore, the main problem defined are the old-dated medical equipment, low level of access to modern diagnostic and healing procedure, low level of access to specialized equipment for diagnosing blood vessels in various areas of the body, e.g. heart, brain, lower limbs or coronary vessels, insufficient knowledge of medical personnel regarding the diagnosis and treatment of victims of armed conflicts of the Polish partner and low level of knowledge of medical personnel regarding treatment methods in the field of the cardiovascular system of the Ukrainian partner. The CROSSDIAM project will challenge this issue enlarging the treatment base for cardiovascular diseases, and diseases requiring neurosurgical treatment in particular of victims of military conflicts. The hospital in Lublin and also in Uzhhorod will purchase angiography imaging system of hybrid cardiovascular operations. Also Ukraine partner will gain new equipment for the clinic's diagnostic laboratory. Now, the diagnostic laboratory's technical equipment for testing does not meet the clinic's growing needs in terms of test volume, speed, accuracy, and outdated reporting format (non-digital, requiring a complete upgrade to modern systems). Finally, the exchange of knowledge between staff during the seminar will provide sharing and know-how between Ukrainian and Polish doctors on hybrid operations and cardiovascular diseases. Also the actions at the projects increasing the level of of knowledge of medical personnel regarding the diagnosis and treatment of victims of armed conflicts of the Polish partner and the level of knowledge of medical personnel regarding treatment methods in the field of the cardiovascular system of the Ukrainian partner. Purchase of the new equipment and improved knowledge of doctors will ensure better medical services on European standard for the residents of Lublin and Uzhhorod. The diagnosis will be conducted faster and the treatment will be more advanced technologically, reducing the disproportion in living on both sides of Polish-Ukraine border.

card.solution: Project partners – Voivodeship Hospital in Suwałki and Volyn Regional Clinical Hospital, taking into account the analogous socio-economic conditions of Podlaskie and Volyn oblast, among others: the growing health debt resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic situation and, additionally in Ukraine, the armed conflict, armed conflict; the successive increase in morbidity and mortality rates for many diseases of civilisation, including in particular cancer and the cardiovascular system and ageing population, as well as coinciding identified needs (reflecting expected changes to make to the current situation in the partner institutions/regions) arising from the above, including, i.a.: • implementing innovative management tools and the technical, technological and organisational solutions correlated with them – Lean Healthcare; • improving the quality of medical infrastructure in the area of surgery, as a medical speciality with broad application in the treatment of many conditions – purchase of modern medical equipment and apparatus, modernisation of premises (as a model for Lean Healthcare; • improving the quality of medical infrastructure in the area of surgery – purchase of modern medical equipment and devices, adaptation of premises; • increased expertise in emergency response and operations, with a particular focus on battlefield injuries; • an increase in staff knowledge and awareness of the role of modern management methods in improving medical processes; undertake a joint project formed of a wide range of activities bringing tangible benefits to hospitals in PL and UA on the basis of exchange experiences, know-how and good practices. All of the above-mentioned needs addressed in the joint project boil down to one main objective in the form of improvement of equal access to specialist medicine in the field of surgery in Podlaskie and Volyn regions by cross-border cooperation undertaken. The project will be implemented through the direct involvement of and for the benefit of two major hospitals – Voivodeship Hospital in Suwałki and Volyn Regional Clinical Hospital, which are key multi-profile specialised units in their respective border regions. At the same time, when analysing the impact of the project, it should be pointed out that in addition to the direct beneficiaries (target groups) the project brings the positive impact to the final beneficiaries – inhabitants of the border regions. Each partner has a specific unique potential, desired to be acquired by the other party, and the range of activities covered by the project has been configured to ensure that the unique competences are transferred to each other, such an effect that cannot be achieved without the cooperation. This forms the basis of the project's added value – combining the objective. i.e. improved access to high quality specialist medicine services in PL-UA border area with innovative management solutions. It is also the basis for a strong CB partnership bringing mutual benefits to the institutions, regions and their people, improving the socio-economic situation of the Programme area. card.solution: The project seeks to solve key common problems facing the Polish-Ukrainian border area in terms of accessibility to highly specialized and quality health care services in light of the changing demographic-economic-political situation, in particular: • underinvestment in equipment of medical entities; • adaptation of medical solutions to the needs of the aging population due to their limited mobility and dispersion of urban centers through the use of telemedicine tools; • the need to continuously improve the knowledge, qualifications and skills of medical personnel due to the constant advances in diagnosis, treatment and prevention in the field of gastroenterology, particularly colorectal cancer; • the application of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis of gastrointestinal diseases; • the need to carry out information and education activities aimed at residents of the cross-border area with regard to prevention and spreading knowledge; • about the necessity of taking preventive measures (informational, educational) combined with basic diagnostic tests for gastrointestinal diseases in the borderland; The main goal is to minimize or relatively even out the deficits in medical care of patients struggling with gastrointestinal diseases through close cooperation between Polish and Ukrainian medical personnel and implementation of a systemic common approach to the patient by increasing the substantive knowledge of residents and medical personnel and increasing the quality of services provided through the purchase of innovative, highly specialized endoscopy equipment. meta.title: THE CARPATHIAN NARROW-GAUGE RAILWAYS - A JOURNEY IN THE FOOTSTEPS OF THE CARPATHIAN FOREST RAILWAYS
meta.institution: FOUNDATION OF THE BIESZCZADY FOREST RAILWAY

card.solution: The project focuses on two areas in the Eastern Carpathians, associated with the history and location of preserved historical forest narrow-gauge railways in Majdan (PL) and Vyhoda (UA). For both areas, the history of narrow-gauge railways and the potential utilization of this heritage represent a significant but underutilized tourism potential. One of the main challenges of this project is the INSUFFICIENT USE OF THE TOURIST POTENTIAL FOR LOCAL SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. As a result, both areas experience economic stagnation, an aging population (high youth migration, negative birth rate), and often unemployment. Tourism development presents a great opportunity, and therefore, innovative actions need to be taken to increase the average length of stay and tourism revenues. To achieve this, both areas need to implement innovative measures and expand, enhance, and integrate their offerings through cross-border cooperation. The overall objective of the project is to increase the role of tourism based on the endogenous historical and cultural potential in the development of Polish-Ukrainian border areas in the Eastern Carpathians. The expected changes that the project will bring about include: - Facilitating cooperation and exchange of experience between project partners and surrounding communities in cross-border areas to develop and promote a common, integrated offer of sustainable tourism. - Expanding and enhancing the offerings of project partners. - Creating a cohesive image by equipping public spaces and narrow-gauge railway station areas in Majdan and Vyhoda in a way that enhances the quality of these places as tourist attractions while respecting their history and the value of the surrounding nature. These changes will be achieved through investment and soft measures implemented in the project, such as building innovative infrastructure for the Bieszczady Forest Railway Station in Majdan, introducing alternative forms of pro-ecological railway and bicycle transport in the Eastern Carpathians, developing visitor infrastructure and walking/cycling routes along the Vyhoda heritage railway route, joint familiarization visits to present an integrated joint tourist offer with the Carpathian Forest Railways logo to travel bloggers and tour operators, cross-border workshops on creating a common integrated tourist offer and joint cross-border festivals promoting local heritage and tourism attractions. The main target groups of the project include institutions related to cultural heritage, operators of tourist attractions, and tourism service providers (approximately 20 entities), travel bloggers, and tourism operators from Ukraine and Poland, local development agencies (3 entities), and representatives of local and regional authorities (6 entities). The project will involve approximately 1,070 participants. The ultimate beneficiaries are enthusiasts of narrow-gauge railways, tourists, residents, and entrepreneurs from the project areas (approximately 140,000 in PL and 80,000 in UA). From a cross-border perspective, both target areas face the challenge of harnessing the untapped economic potential of cross-border tourism by offering visitors a joint tourist offer that includes a cross-border trip to the neighbouring historical railways still in operation in the Eastern Carpathians. Currently, there is a lack of cooperation, joint marketing, and exchange of tourists between partners. This is further exacerbated by a lack of information about tourist attractions, services, and accommodations, leading to a lack of awareness among tourists about the attractions they can experience on the other side of the border. The project will enable both areas to access visitors and tourists from the other side of the border and enter the cross-border tourism market with a joint offer that integrates more diversified and meaningful holiday experiences within a single trip to the heritage railways.

card.solution: The current cross-border cooperation on the Polish-Ukrainian border between various entities from the public sector, civil society, and primarily residents, is not very intensive. A new impetus and bottom-up initiatives are needed to achieve the goal of promoting and supporting the establishment of new contacts, relationships, and initiatives at the interpersonal level, in order to achieve long-term cooperation. Taking such actions will help to significantly increase trust and establish new interpersonal relations among the residents of the Programme area. Additionally, it should be emphasized that the Russian invasion of Ukraine has significantly changed and limited the cooperation between institutions and residents of the border region, thereby requiring additional measures to address new challenges. The war and its consequences have had a profound impact on the situation in the Ukrainian part of the Programme area. It has also caused an unprecedented influx of refugees to Poland. The response to these needs and challenges is the implementation of the SPF, the main objective of which is to build mutual trust, in particular by encouraging interpersonal activities through the implementation of small projects. The specific objectives of the SPF include: - increasing the use of cultural/natural heritage and the development of education, integration of border residents and building mutual trust and good neighbourly relations. meta.title: Improvement of the quality and safety of cross-border railway connections by works on the line no 101 in Werchrata and in Lviv railway station

card.solution: The Project addresses urgent challenges caused by the unprovoked Russian aggression on Ukraine. This conflict has drastically changed transport needs and increased passenger and freight flows, requiring upgrades to previously underutilized infrastructure for smooth, safe, and efficient cross-border connections. On the Ukrainian side, the project focuses on improving services at border crossings, with special emphasis on Lviv railway station, a crucial logistics hub through which over 56% of international passengers transited in 2024. Since the conflict began, Lviv station has served as a humanitarian and evacuation center for thousands of refugees, including persons with disabilities. However, the station lacks inclusive infrastructure, limiting access for persons with disabilities, elderly passengers, and others with special needs. Passenger numbers increased to over 3.1 million in 2024, with requests for assistance rising 2.5 times. On the Polish side, the project will upgrade line no. 101 and Werchrata station to improve speed (from 30 to 70 km/h), capacity, and reliability, providing alternative routes and strengthening the railway system. The technical condition of line no. 101 is deteriorated, with the last major repair in 1975. The project also includes enhancing coordination among infrastructure managers, railway operators, and border control guards, along with training to improve border security and efficiency. Key goals are to renew track infrastructure, ensure unhindered access for low-mobility groups at Lviv station, increase safety and efficiency, and support Ukraine’s European integration by aligning with EU standards. The project will benefit approximately 3 million passengers annually, including vulnerable groups such as evacuees, injured military personnel, and persons with disabilities, while optimizing border crossing capacity and management. The project aims to: • improve the quality of existing infrastructure of the line no. 101 by increasing the speed on parts of the line from V=30 km/h to 70 km/h, resulting in a 4-minute travel time savings; • improve the quality of existing infrastructure by renewal of the surface of the track no 9 in Werchrata station; • ensure unhindered access to Lviv station for people with disabilities and other low-mobility groups to trains and tunnels; • increase the level of safety and efficiency of using the station infrastructure; • support Ukraine's European integration course by adapting the station to EU standards • strengthen the cooperation of the stakeholders and increase the level of safety and security of the railway transport system. The implementation of the Project will contribute to the integration of Ukraine into the European transport area, increase the level of accessibility for all categories of passengers and ensure safe and comfortable conditions for users of the railway infrastructure, The project will also increase the level of awareness of the border control guards for the specific needs of the categories of the passengers from the target groups by providing trainings to the staff involved in passenger checks. The realization of activities in the border crossing area will eventually improve the capacity of border crossing points by improving services for passengers and the quality of the infrastructure in the border area The project will be implemented under 5 work packages: 1) Infrastructure works on the line no 101 (PLK); 2) Construction and installation works at Lviv station (UZ); 3) Joint training scheme (PLK +UZ); 4) Promotion (PLK+UZ); 5) Indirect costs (UZ), including; 5.1 Staff costs; 5.2 Administration; 5.3 Travel and accommodation.

meta.title: Enhancing transport infrastructure to strengthen Polish-Ukrainian connectivity via road 850 in Lubelskie and H22 in Rivne

card.solution: The project "Enhancing transport infrastructure to strengthen Polish-Ukrainian connectivity via road 850 in Lubelskie and H22 in Rivne" directly responds to the pressing challenges of mobility, safety, and infrastructure inefficiencies in the cross-border area between Poland and Ukraine. The common challenge tackled is the poor quality and insufficient capacity of road infrastructure in the Programme area, which hinders economic cooperation, delays freight and passenger traffic, and reduces regional competitiveness. The project area includes the Lubelskie Voivodeship in Poland and the Rivne Region in Ukraine—regions with strategic cross-border relevance, particularly in terms of logistics, trade, and transport connectivity. On the Polish side, the project focuses on the reconstruction and modernization of voivodeship road no. 850 in Tomaszów Lubelski, a key link between national road no. 17 (E372) and the border crossing with Ukraine. The road serves both regional freight traffic and daily commuters, with current traffic exceeding 9,100 vehicles per day. Due to insufficient load-bearing capacity, narrow roadways, lack of pedestrian and cyclist infrastructure, and outdated intersections, the road poses safety risks and delays. On the Ukrainian side, the project modernizes road connections between the Klevan and Zoria Territorial Communities and the H-22 national road, providing access to the regional multimodal freight terminal. In 2024, the terminal in Klevan is projected to handle 17,013 container movements, with 70% transported by road, leading to over 17,000 individual vehicle movements. The current infrastructure, designed for a capacity of only 370 vehicles per day, is now handling approximately 140 freight trucks daily. With traffic expected to increase to 500 vehicles daily, expanding road capacity is vital to avoid further congestion and safety hazards. The overall objective is to enhance cross-border connectivity and economic cooperation between Poland and Ukraine by improving road infrastructure capacity, safety, and efficiency in compliance with EU standards. The project supports Policy Objective 3 of the Interreg NEXT Programme: "A more connected Europe by enhancing mobility," and contributes to Specific Objective 6.1: "Developing and enhancing sustainable, climate-resilient, intelligent, and intermodal national, regional, and local mobility." The main outputs include the reconstruction of over 10.5 km of DW 850 in Poland, capital overhaul and new construction of over 2.1 km of strategic roads in Ukraine. These infrastructure works are expected to reduce travel time for freight transport by up to 3 minutes, improve logistics coordination, and significantly reduce noise and air pollution in residential areas. The direct target groups include local communities, more than 47,000 businesses in Rivne Region (including 434 logistics companies and over 3,200 transport and warehousing entrepreneurs), regional road authorities, freight transport companies, and local governments on both sides of the border. In total, over 2 million residents live within the Project’s impact area, including 13,852 people in Klevan and 11,841 in Zoria, of which more than 5,500 are children. The Polish part of the Programme area includes approximately 800,000 people in 54 municipalities. The Applicant is Lubelskie Voivodeship. The Project will be implemented by the following patners: - Lead Partner (LP): Lubelskie Voivodeship, The Project is implemented on behalf of Lubelskie Voivodeship by the Voivodeship Road Administration Office in Lublin, a regional self-government organisational unit of Lubelskie Voivodeship, acting pursuant to the Statute of Lubelskie Voivodeship, the Statute of the Voivodeship Road Administration Office in Lublin and Resolution No. CXXXII/2471/2025 of 10 June 2025. - Project Partner (PP): Department for Construction and Architecture of the Rivne Regional State (Military) Administration.

meta.title: Improving cross-border mobility by building the regional road no. 627 Kosów Lacki – Sokołów Podlaski and general renovation of the bridge in Terebovlia on M-19 national road

card.solution: The project is in line with the objectives of the EU cohesion policy, i.e. "a more connected Europe through increased mobility". The aim of the project is to support cross-border development processes in Poland and Ukraine by strengthening sustainable, climate-resilient, smart and intermodal national, regional and local mobility, including improving access to the TEN-T network and cross-border mobility. The main identified problems are the poor technical condition of the provincial road no. 627 and the increase in traffic. Traffic studies conducted in 2020 and 2021 by GDDKiA show a 20% increase compared to 2015 (Masovian Voivodeship: 4196 vehicles/day in 2015 vs. 5279 vehicles/day in 2020). The project partner's problem is the poor technical condition of the bridge and poor road safety. A load limit of 30 tons has been introduced. Most heavy loads are transported on a longer route by about 100 km. On the section of the M-19 road running through the Ternopil region, 188 road accidents occurred. Traffic volume on this section increased by 20% in 2022-2024. The aim of the project is to support cross-border development processes in Poland and Ukraine by strengthening sustainable, climate-resilient, smart and intermodal national, regional and local mobility, including improving access to the TEN-T network and cross-border mobility. The project will improve the safety and capacity of cross-border traffic between Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Romania. The modernized infrastructure will provide better connections to key transport routes for local (rural) communities and increase their mobility. The project will also have a positive impact on the flow of passenger/freight traffic between key regional nodes in Poland and improve traffic capacity in Ukraine. The main challenge faced by the project partners is the poor accessibility of the EU-Ukraine solidarity routes. In both regions, the availability of modern infrastructure, safe for users and environmentally friendly, remains problematic. This project is one of the steps to improve the accessibility of the regions and access to the solidarity routes connecting Poland and Ukraine. The investment is tailored to the economic and social needs of residents of both regions and local road users. Cooperation between partners is essential to achieve cross-border effects of the project, going beyond the administrative borders of one country. Integrated infrastructure activities on both sides of the border will improve the flow of people and goods and ensure coherence of regional development. Joint planning, exchange of experiences and mutual adaptation of technical and road safety standards will enable the creation of a coherent, modern and functional transport network. Only a coordinated approach will allow for the effective use of the potential of TEN-T routes and EU-Ukraine solidarity corridors. Regional road No. 627 connects to the TEN-T network in Ostrów Mazowiecka (S8/E67). Transport access to Ukraine is provided by expressways No. S8, S19 and S12). The project partner will carry out a comprehensive modernization of the bridge, which in its current technical condition poses a threat to users. The bridge is located in Terebovlia along the national road M-19, at kilometer 355+470 towards Romania. It is part of the European route E-85, within the TEN-T network. It is of strategic importance for the transport of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of civilians from frontline areas, and also serves as an important logistics hub for domestic and international transport. Cross-border cooperation will be implemented through online meetings, study visits and visits to construction sites, as well as constant exchange of knowledge and experience in the field of road modernization and improving road safety. Promotional activities will include, among others, information campaigns, boards and billboards, electronic displays and educational events for children on road safety.

meta.title: DigiClimAct - Climate Action in South Baltic Cities Goes Digital

card.solution: Climate change is now very high on the agenda, but its effects can differ locally. The Baltic Sea Region faces increasingly severe climate-related issues, such as intensive precipitation, flood events, and strong storms, leading to spatial planning and water management challenges. Many previous projects aimed to improve local strategies for climate adaptation, resulting in a comprehensive toolkit of targeted planning and design solutions, such as more flood-resilient infrastructure. Despite this practical toolkit for climate adaptation, local communities' uptake of climate-related policies and addressing current hazards is still insufficient. DigiClimAct addresses the vulnerability of the South Baltic Area (SBA) to the impacts of climate change. Several barriers have been diagnosed, hindering the institutional and social capacity of climate adaptation, including insufficient resources, conflicting interests, or uncertainty about future benefits. These barriers lead to the still too low acceptability of climate adaptation measures among SB communities. Although we observe that the general awareness of climate change is growing, a comprehensive understanding of the local climate adaptation measures is still lacking. This is partly due to the reliance on traditional means of promotion, such as academic publications, websites, or handbooks, which are inaccessible to many stakeholders. More effective and innovative dissemination strategies are needed to empower individuals to take action and advocate for change. Regional and local authorities in SBA must engage all societal levels to facilitate a sustainable transition. Yet, they lack effective means for systematic bottom-up interaction with these entities, hindering their potential to bolster societal resilience, raise climate change awareness and promote sustainability. Digitisation presents a promising avenue for achieving this goal. The project aims to increase the institutional and societal capacity to adapt and improve preparedness by adopting a digitisation strategy, which will be piloted in three project areas in Poland, Lithuania and Sweden. By applying a cross-border approach, we want to jointly tackle the problem of insufficient innovation in action for climate adaptation. DigiClimAct initiates a new network of creative interaction by piloting various digital applications (VR, immersive and interactive applications) to communicate climate knowledge and impact scenarios. These immersive environments and engaging visualisations, aimed at bridging the gap between expert knowledge and stakeholders, are created for a variety of target users, with different gender, age, ethnicity and income. DigiClimAct also provides a cross-border digitisation roadmap as a wider approach for disseminating climate issues to civil society to improve climate adaptation measures' acceptability and build social resilience. Finally, it delivers a digital handbook promoting the democratic perspective in climate action, providing checkpoints for citizens on how to increase the accountability and transparency of the decision-making process in their region. The project partners have expertise in the core areas crucial to its implementation: academic knowledge of environmental policies, skills in innovative digital technologies, and long-term experience in social capacity building and promoting climate justice. Only by joining all these competencies and networks, is it possible to create an operational digital strategy for more effective communication of climate adaptation amongst different social groups. The project also involves extensive collaboration with local actors from different backgrounds. Leveraging the approach of co-creation and social inclusion, DigiClimAct significantly improves our understanding of how to develop effective and accessible digital tools with digital inclusion in mind. As a result, it elevates the digitalisation level across different sectors of the regional economy.

meta.title: INCONE60 Green - Digital and green transition of small ports

card.solution: In the South Baltic region, small seaports face a common challenge - they grapple with varying levels of development and struggle to adapt to the digital era. Unlike larger counterparts, these small ports lack tailored management systems, hindering their efficiency and competitiveness. The INCONE60 Green project emerges as a collaborative effort to transform these challenges into opportunities, fostering sustainable growth and resilience. Aligned with the European Union Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR) and its Action Plan, the project focuses on key priority areas, including sustainable shipping, innovative technologies, and a globally competitive position in innovation. The project identifies a common territorial challenge in the South Baltic area – the need to enhance small seaports' competitiveness through digitalisation and the development of green technologies, aligning with the European Green Deal and other EU strategic initiatives. The main outputs of the INCONE60 Green project are: 1. SeaTech Port Management System - a digital tool tailored for small seaports, enhancing efficiency, reducing handling times, and contributing to the EU's goal of reducing transport emissions by 90% by 2050. 2. SeaWay software - intelligent algorithms estimating external costs, a crucial step towards internalising these costs and promoting environmentally friendly transport modes. 3. SeaStat database - an online repository of maritime statistics at national, European, and global levels, aiding informed decision-making for port development and developing recommendations for local and regional strategies. Cross-border cooperation is crucial for achieving the project's objectives as small seaports in the South Baltic region face shared challenges that require collaborative solutions. The project brings together partners from different regions, leveraging their expertise to develop innovative tools and strategies for small seaport development. The cross-border approach allows for a comprehensive analysis of these ports' common challenges and the development of tailored solutions. Building on the results of previous projects like INCONE60, Connect2SmallPorts and SECMAR, INCONE60 Green leverages existing tools and collaborations. The project integrates and extends the INCONE60 Cargo Flow Model, connects with maritime cybersecurity solutions from SECMAR, and builds upon the digitalisation status examination tool from Connect2SmallPorts.

meta.title: Baltic Biking UPGRADE

card.solution: Baltic Biking UPGRADE (BBU) will address the significant challenges of SMEs along the South Baltic part (PL,LT,SE,DK,DE) of the Baltic Sea Cycle Route – EuroVelo10 (EV10) when the SMEs are to create attractive bookable offers and successfully reach out to foreign markets. These challenges are mainly due to a lack of knowledge, underdeveloped bicycle-friendly standards, services & offer & a lack of business contacts and partnerships with relevant peers. This shall be achieved via: ▪ Rolling out bicycle-friendly services along the EV10: Based on cross-border knowledge transfer, basic standards for bicycle-friendly tourism SME offer&services are adopted and rolled out in the PPs countries. A training programme equips SMEs with tools and know-how to develop new offers &provide them to cycle tourists. ▪ Creating new SME products & offers for customers around the EV10: Matchmaking activities build up a cooperation network among different actors from all. Participating SMEs are supported to jointly develop new regional and/or cross-border cycling tourism products & offer for EV10 cyclists that can be promoted internationally. ▪ Joint marketing of the EV10 SMEs offer on various markets: The jointly developed new cycling tourism SME products & offers are promoted on the SBA market & beyond. This includes e.g. ready-to-use marketing strategy for SMEs, participation in cycle-specific tourism fairs, improvement of existing promotional tools to support SMEs' business like EuroVelo10.com website, fam-trips for tour operators, journalists/influencers. ▪ Strengthening the strategic development & management of the EV10: A network of actors from all EV10 countries is built up for joint development of the EV10. It is the basis for exchanging ideas & expertise & interaction among SMEs (BBu Platform) and their improved offer, as well as a coordinated long-term development of the route explained in the transnational Action Plan. BBU is in line with the Interreg objective: more competitive and smarter Europe by promoting innovative and smart economic transformation (…), and thus SBP Objective 1- Innovative South Baltic – enhancing innovation and internationalisation of local actors. meta.title: DeCoInter - Decarbonization of Maritime Sector and its Impact on Green Energy Transition
meta.institution: The Association of Polish Regions of Baltic Adriatic Transport Corridor

card.solution: The European Green Deal has defined climate goals as reduction of GHG emissions to 55 per cent in 2030 and climate neutrality in the year 2050. A crucial measure to achieve the EGD challenges is the transition into green energy sources, like alternative fuels and renewable energy sources (Repower EU policy). As a result, ports regions of Sothern Baltic Sea area and their maritime institutions/stakeholders will face challenges in the next decades, what’s more initiatives, should go beyond regulations and stimulate an even faster energy transition process not only in ports themselves but also in scale of port ecosystem and regions of location. Ports have always been playing a crucial role in energy sector being centres for reloading and storage of energy sources, so seaports are natural place for developing energy related projects. Today, ports must redefined its role, thus relevant strategies and actions should be undertaken both in the ports themselves as energy consumers, as well as in relation to their role as modern regional green energy distribution centres. The aim of the DeCoInter project is to support the region's energy transition process by increasing the use of renewable energy sources and improve availability of green alternative fuels. Therefore, it is necessary to prepare a methodological framework for the Seaports Energy Transition Strategy development as a large consumer and distributor of clean energy as well as to define a Scenario Model for development of the value chain of alternative fuels within the ports. At the same time, increasing awareness of the needs, available solutions and expected effects of the energy transition, based on the seaports technical, operational and market capacity, is a key factor of transition success. Moreover, the energy efficiency improvement and energy saving initiatives must find a way to be commonly implemented. Only by combination of these both elements, true low-carbon energy systems can be established and energy transition ensured. The energy transformation strategy must take into account both supply and demand elements, as well as appropriate prioritization of activities, which include both the level of impact on the environment (emissions), the specificity of energy receivers and its technical, operational and financial possibilities of their transition to green energy. The new sustainable fuels have been under development in the last years (e.g., methanol, ammonium, hydrogen, hybrid, electric propulsion), therefore ports, their partners and energy companies must adapt to this development. In addition to technology, an essential element of the system will be to ensure a sustainable value chain that will enable the delivery of alternative fuels from production sites, through transport, storage & distribution procedures, to consumers. Today, all technologies are at the implementation stage, therefore potential development activities should be analyzed in a scenario. The development of appropriate development models will therefore be an effective tool for planning future activities. The implementation of this task requires common efforts from seaports stakeholders, transport & energy sector as well as R&D entities, education and public sector. The LP is an association grouping seven local government regions, so policy-makers support is ensured. It is a partner of the European Commission in the development of the TEN-T network and the implementation of the green transport policy. Effective implementation requires building awareness among users, therefore preliminary identification of needs and preparation of an appropriate promotional campaign is needed. DEcoInter will also create a platform for networking and learning between seaport stakeholders, allowing for the implementation of an innovative solutions for blue renewables or value chain for green fuels. The project will offer training and education programs prepared and executed for seaport stakeholders and students.

meta.title: IMPETUS - IMPET build your wind energy future with US
meta.institution: Institute of Fluid-Flow Machinery Polish Academy of Science

card.solution: The main objective of Interreg’s Program is "To increase the blue and green growth potential of the South Baltic Area (SBA) through cross-border cooperation." We plan to contribute to that goal by laying a foundation for a regional ecosystem dedicated to a leap improvement in wind energy production, while: • developing cross-border collaborative links, • fostering spin-off SMEs’ creation, and • assist the existing SMEs by making the complete project-generated knowledge available in an Open Access Repository. We propose to achieve these goals through a challenging and highly motivational competition open to SBA’s university students and assisted by project partners sharing their complementary knowledge and expertise in the subject matter. Student teams will be expected to design and fabricate proof-of-concept demonstrators of wind turbines with substantially enhanced overall efficiency, meaning the improvement of the most important wind turbine characteristics, such as: • aerodynamic efficiency, • maintenance cost, • the level of produced noise, • the level of threat to animals and, particularly for marine wind turbines: • the seaworthiness of the turbine/floater system and • energy produced per unit area of a wind turbine farm. Achieving these ambitious goals will require high student teams’ motivation, very good working conditions and an efficient support environment. The main motivation will be based on the proven since 6th-century BC adage “Give them a fish and you feed them for a day. Teach them how to fish and you feed them for a lifetime.” In this particular case, students will have at their disposal all the necessary components to achieve with their hard work excellent results, which might be also very important for their future: • a repository of publications covering most of the subject matter – to save time on initial bibliography searches, • fully equipped manufacturing and computational facilities for each of the selected teams, • assistance and general support in solving inevitable problems – from project partners, • full information produced in the project preparation phase: .stl models, design, fabrication, testing solutions and computer codes developed in the IMPETUS project preparatory and proof-of-concept phase, and • Webinars prepared and delivered by project partners, covering the basics in analysis, design, fabrication and business acumen needed to level the ground among competing teams. Business acumen knowledge will be delivered to inject a measure of practicality in the developed solutions, and to facilitate the generation of spin-off SMEs by students so-inclined, wishing to use and further develop solutions produced by the IMPETUS project. To focus students’ attention and frame the effort, the competition will be directed specifically towards perfecting the concept of Vertical Axis Wind Turbine (VAWT) – a turbine with blades rotating with respect to a substantially vertical axis. We, the partners in the IMPETUS project consortium strongly believe that the body of recent research results warrants undertaking a serious effort to facilitate wide implementation of the VAWT concept as a complementary wind energy conversion method. In particular, the aerodynamic efficiency can be improved by the application of VAWT blade pitch control, to be perfectioned within the framework of the proposed project. The following jointly developed solutions will be provided: 1. Open Access Repository storing the complete project-generated information 2. Methods developed for passive control of blades in VAWT, 3. Methods developed for individual blade pitch control in VAWT, contributing to RCO116 programme output indicators. The entire output of the IMPETUS Project will be made available as Open Access. Therefore, the project will not bring any financial benefits, nor will it give any competitive edge to IFFM.

meta.title: BIOSOLFarm - "South baltic farms - an essential part of renewable energy systems"

card.solution: Climate changes, socio-political upheavals, and the ongoing pandemic have exposed the fragility of our current systems and highlighted the need for self-sufficiency in key areas such as food and energy. The high pricses of electricity, fertilizers, and fuels have increased the concerns of society. Given the vast expanse of land and the dominant share in the market, agriculture holds great potential to contribute to energy systems and to provide a more sustainable future for all. Agricultural farms, particularly those with access to biomass sources such as manure and plant-based material, offer enormous potential for anaerobic digestion and biogas production through boilers for hot water production. This solution not only increases energy efficiency, but it also contributes to the improvement of material flow and waste management. With an estimated total area of 37 million hectares of agricultural land in the region, there is ample opportunity to replace fertilizer use with digestate and reduce the pollution discharge into the Baltic Sea. Additionally, the large farm surfaces provide ample space for the installation of photovoltaics and wind power. To meet the peak energy demands, it is necessary to develop energy storage systems, such as batteries and hydrogen gas. While the challenges and opportunities for farms across the South Baltic Sea region may differ, a common goal is to improve energy production and storage at the farm level and increase energy security. However, many farms are too small to make optimal use of their resources and energy technologies such as anaerobic digestion. This is where the importance of small farmers associations comes in. By working together, these associations can pool their resources, knowledge, and expertise, and adapt it to their specific conditions. To overcome the challenges of introducing new business models, it is crucial for small farms to engage in knowledge and practice exchange. This can be achieved through cooperation and networking initiatives. Based on best practices, lessons learned, and case studies, the project will develop and evaluate pilot associations, and create a toolbox that supports the decision-making process for energy optimization, production, consumption, and storage. This toolbox will help farmers evaluate the potential for energy efficiency improvements and estimate the benefits that can be achieved. The project will facilitate knowledge exchange through study tours, training, workshops, and networking events. Based on stakeholder consultations, recommendations for farmers and policy makers will be developed to help in the creation of tools that promote the deployment of renewable energy systems in rural areas across the South Baltic region. The goal is to foster the growth of small farmers associations that prioritize green and efficient energy systems, ensuring energy security and food security for local communities and regions. The partnership will increase farmers capacity for research, development, and deployment of green energy systems, leading to cost reductions, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, and a more sustainable future. Cross-border partnerships with common goals and shared vision will drive the creation of policies and regulations that support the deployment of sustainable energy systems in scattered sources such as small farms and farmers associations. Joint monitoring, evaluation, and adjusting strategies will be necessary to continue the development of innovative renewable energy power stations, smart grid systems, and energy efficiency measures. By working together, small farmers associations can overcome the challenges and maximize the opportunities for energy production, consumption, and storage. The development of innovative solutions and business models, combined with cross-border partnerships of farmers and stakeholders will help to create a greener, more secure, and more prosperous future for all.

meta.title: Baltic EnerShift
meta.institution: Institute of Fluid-Flow Machinery of the Polish Academy of Sciences

card.solution: The Baltic EnerShift (BES) project addresses the urgent need to transition district heating (DH) systems in the South Baltic (SB) region towards sustainable, efficient, and resilient 4th- and 5th-generation district heating and cooling (4/5GDHC). Current systems rely heavily on costly biomass/waste fuels and suffer from outdated infrastructure, severely hindering regional and European decarbonization efforts. BES fosters innovation and intensive cross-sectoral collaboration to transform networks into world-leading, digitally enabled systems capable of meeting future energy demands and complying with stricter environmental standards. The objective is to effectively transform existing DH networks by integrating innovative tools, advanced digitalization, and strong cross-sectoral cooperation. This comprehensive effort will significantly improve energy efficiency, contribute to substantial greenhouse gas emission reductions, and enable the wider use of low-grade renewable and recycled energy sources, enhancing green energy production and ensuring greater energy security for the region. BES delivers three core Marketable Outputs (MOs): - Sector coupling tools: Services integrating electricity, heating, cooling, and waste heat recovery using digital technologies for optimal operation and improved resource efficiency. These tools are crucial for balancing fluctuating energy supplies, maximizing renewable energy use, and increasing overall system flexibility. - Grid optimization services: Tools for adapting DH networks to lower operating temperatures, ensuring longer system lifespans, and enabling predictive maintenance via advanced digital analytics. This involves advanced modelling to minimize heat losses during distribution and enhance network reliability and cost-effectiveness. - Customer integration services: Solutions connecting DH systems with building-level energy systems, offering real-time failure detection, flexible energy usage, and advanced energy-saving features supported by AI-driven insights. These services empower end-users and enable effective, flexible demand-side management. BES delivers key outputs, including jointly developed solutions, practical pilot activities, and reusable tools. The comprehensive support framework includes training packages for operators, technicians, and decision-makers to ensure lasting impact and robust know-how transfer. Crucially, the project will also implement Policy Recommendations and Advocacy, aiming to address regulatory barriers and promote an enabling policy environment necessary for the widespread and rapid adoption of advanced DH technologies across the region. The expected results include: - Significant reductions in energy losses and emissions, directly advancing the region's decarbonization goals in alignment with EU Green Deal objectives. - Enhanced operational efficiency and improved cost-effectiveness in DH systems through digital innovations. - A stronger regional capacity to adopt and implement cutting-edge 4/5GDHC solutions, fostering a durable culture of innovation and collaboration among stakeholders. BES adopts a unified, cross-border approach, pooling expertise from industry leaders and researchers across the SBR to accelerate the transition cohesively and inclusively. This collaboration is essential to overcome common regional challenges. The cross-border effort facilitates the exchange of best practices, provides scalable and replicable models, and strengthens regional resilience and energy security. BES is distinguished by its focus on deep digitalization. It uses smart diagnostics and analytics to transform physical processes into actionable digital insights. AI-driven optimization enables systems to adapt dynamically and predictively to demand fluctuations. The Training Frameworks ensure these technological advancements are accessible and practical, actively working to close the existing skills gap in the regional energy sector.

meta.title: BALTICBEAT - Building Commitment to Accelerate Clean energy Transition in the South Baltic

card.solution: The BALTICBEAT project will undertake initiatives addressing one of the critical challenges, namely, increasing the use of renewable energy and developing energy communities based on clean energy. Cross-border cooperation will lead to the development of toolkits supporting local administration, SMEs, and citizens in implementing solutions for the production and utilization of renewable energy. Furthermore, it will it will help support local communities interested in establishing energy communities based on renewable energy sources (RES) and innovative energy storage methods. The aim of the project is to increase renewable energy production in the South Baltic area by providing local actors with a set of tools to facilitate the preparation of this production and the management of RES, in particular to help create and develop energy communities. The use of project’s tools will result in enhancement of knowledge and interest in the proposed solutions among identified stakeholder groups. This will contribute to an increased share of green energy in the energy mix of the regions involved in the project. BALTICBEAT will conduct activities aimed at developing a common approach to address the challenge of the low share of renewable energy in the energy mix of individual countries. Standardizing this approach on a cross-border scale will facilitate the gathering and exchange of information on progress in implementing the adopted strategy. It will also exert pressure on regulators to create incentives and legal regulations to foster the implementation of innovative technological (in the field of clean energy) and organizational (in the creation of energy communities) solutions. Peer-to-peer learning and sharing of best practices on a cross-border level will raise awareness about the successful implementation of proposed solutions in one region, ultimately accelerating activity in other regions to level the playing field for involved stakeholders. Regarding the project partners and identified stakeholder groups, BALTICBEAT will for the first time introduce toolkits that: Strengthen the capacity of key local stakeholder groups to create and manage local energy communities and guide energy transformation processes at the local level. Moreover it will support the involvement of local communities in initiating and implementing energy transformation initiatives at the local level. These tools will be reinforced by a cross-border advisory platform and specialized, tailor-made training services to enhance the utilization of RES in the South Baltic Area (SBA). This will also facilitate the development of common behavioural patterns to overcome challenges and mobilize regional opportunities in the field of renewable energy. All project products will be designed and delivered in such a way, as to enable their adaptation and upscaling in other regions of the SBA. The project will be implemented in a cross-border manner in four countries of the South Baltic area. The partnership has been established in a balanced way to ensure optimal implementation. Four countries are represented and the partners are 3 research institutions, 2 NGOs, a business environment institution linked to the regional authorities and an SME. In addition, the project will be supported by 5 APs, selected to represent all target groups and to test and implement the project's solutions.

meta.title: Watt A Waste

card.solution: The SB region faces a critical need to accelerate the transition to renewable energy sources and reduce its dependency on fossil fuels. The shift from traditional energy generation to sustainable and locally available alternatives is essential to energy security and climate neutrality. The Watt-a-Waste (WAW) project contributes to this transition by integrating innovative waste-based renewable energy technologies that produce clean energy while reducing carbon emissions. The project puts primary emphasis on valorising the renewable (biogenic) waste fraction, while the non-biogenic part is addressed only as a complementary contribution that increases overall sustainability and energy efficiency. By leveraging advanced waste-to-energy conversion methods, WAW develops and tests solutions that integrate into regional and local energy grids through pilot-scale installations. These will serve as real-world models for energy recovery from waste fractions, ensuring efficiency in energy output with minimal environmental impact. Pilot Cases and Key Technological Innovations: - Pilot Case 1: Gdańsk University of Technology (GUT) GUT will lead a pilot using low-temperature dry reforming to process waste fractions into a gaseous energy carrier, optimizing recovery while minimizing CO₂ emissions. The pilot will test gas purification and carbon capture to ensure efficient integration into energy systems. It will operate under near-industrial conditions to allow scalability. While the main focus is on biogenic waste, non-biogenic residues such as plastics and rubber are considered only as an additional pathway to maximise the sustainability impact of the renewable energy transition. - Pilot Case 2: Klaipeda University (KU) KU will test pre-treatment methods that improve waste-to-energy conversion. This includes combined physical and biological techniques to raise energy yield and lower emissions. Pre-treated waste will be tested in Pilot Case 1, demonstrating a cross-border approach. The pilot will also assess integration with local waste management and energy systems. Special attention will be given to pre-treatment of biogenic waste fractions, which constitute the renewable part of the energy contribution. - Pilot Case 3: Leibniz Institute for Plasma Science and Technology (INP) INP will develop plasma-based technologies for waste-to-energy conversion, focusing on maximizing energy yield while minimizing emissions and secondary waste. The system will be enhanced with advanced gasification and conversion modules to achieve high-efficiency renewable energy production. Insights from Pilot Cases 1 and 2 will refine the plasma model. The plasma system will primarily target biogenic residues, ensuring measurable renewable energy production, with non-biogenic waste used in a complementary way to enhance efficiency. The WAW project aligns with Measure 2.1: Supporting Transition Towards Green Energy by demonstrating practical waste-to-energy applications that produce renewable energy while reducing carbon emissions. Quantifiable renewable impact will be highlighted by estimating energy output derived specifically from biogenic fractions, showing the project’s contribution to Measure 2.1 and Specific Objective RSO2.2. The project will: - Create scalable and adaptable waste-to-energy solutions for local grids - Develop best practices and guidelines for adoption of waste-derived energy sources - Support regional energy resilience by providing renewable energy carriers - Enable cross-border cooperation in energy innovation, ensuring technologies and knowledge are shared across the South Baltic Region

meta.title: DecarbonDHS - Decarbonization of district heating systems
meta.institution: Institute of Fluid-Flow Machinery Polish Academy of Sciences

card.solution: The project aims to promote the decarbonization of district heating systems and facilitate the transition towards sustainable and low-carbon solutions, by integrating renewable energy sources, energy efficiency, utilizing waste heat from industry and incorporating energy storage technologies. The heating and cooling sector consumes about half of the EU’s energy, 12% of heating is delivered by district heating systems which are fuelled mainly using coal and natural gas. Effective substitution of fossil fuels for heating/cooling systems is needed in respect to strategic goals: decarbonization, climate mitigation and reducing the ecological footprint, as well as energy security – reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels, including from hostile countries. There are several key challenges in the field of DH, especially in large cities, that need to be considered: aging infrastructure, energy efficiency (heat losses, grid optimization and waste heat utilisation), integration of renewable energy, heat demand fluctuations, high initial (investment) costs, regulations and policy, decentralization and smart grids, heat prices and its affordability. Addressing these challenges requires a combination of technological advancements, policy support, public awareness, and collaboration among stakeholders, including policy makers, city authorities, heat and energy providers, urban planners, researchers, and residents. Project focus on three key issues: • Roadmap to decarbonization of district heating (DH) in South baltic region (SBR); it will base on review of current state and potential prospective solutions • Demonstration of innovative, decarbonized low temperature DH systems in SBR; through pilot projects in multiple municipalities, feasibility and benefits of sustainable district heating solutions will be presented. The financial, environmental, and social impact of implemented district heating will be considered. The energy efficiency measures will include thermo-modernization of building, grid monitoring, modernization of DH network taking into account real heat demand and heating grid in modernized buildings, heat storages, Power-to-Heat, and waste heat integration (including industrial sources, wastewater facilities, as well as hydrogen production systems, i.e. electrolysers). Recommendations for policy makers will be formulated. • Capacity building and dissemination; recommendations related to study visit will be formulated, stakeholders will be engaged in the process of capacity building and series of seminar materials will be prepared for stakeholders. The activities include providing guidance, training, and financing recommendations to support the implementation of energy-efficient and renewable district heating plans. By fostering collaboration and knowledge sharing among stakeholders, we aim to strengthen cross-border cooperation and promote the adoption of best. Our project contributes to the promotion of green cities, the overall sustainability and energy security of participating municipalities. It plays a crucial role in empowering municipalities with the necessary expertise and capacity to develop and implement sustainable district heating plans, leveraging the benefits of energy storage for enhanced flexibility and reliability. Through the development of guidelines and best practices, we aim to inspire and support other regions and municipalities in replicating successful district heating projects, accelerating the global transition towards a low-carbon future. Partners will cooperate working in tandems including Expert Partner and Municipality/Municipal DH company. Expected results: • Significant reduction in carbon emissions • New energy technologies will be promoted • Successful transfer of pilot projects demonstrating the feasibility and benefits of sustainable district heating solutions • Strengthened collaboration and capacity building, empowering municipalities to develop and implement sustainable DH plans.

meta.title: LoCaGas - Low Calorific Gas for Green Power Production

card.solution: Methane is one of the most important greenhouse gases with a Global Warming Potential (GWP) of 34 on a timespan of 100 years, according to IPCC’s 5th Assessment Report. The concentration of methane in the atmosphere has more than doubled in the last 150 years and landfills are the third largest (16%) emitter of anthropogenic methane after fossil fuel production, distribution, combustion (33%) and livestock farming (27%). In the Baltic Sea region, there are up to 100 thousand of landfills including closed or abandoned sites, which pose environmental risks due to greenhouse gas emissions into the atmosphere. According to the Report of National Inventory Submissions to the UNFCCC, 2020, these landfills emit 782 kt in Sweden, 662 kt in Lithuania, 302 kt in Poland, 270 kt in Germany and 21 kt in Denmark of CH4 emissions. However, only a small number of these are equipped with gas extraction equipment (51 landfills in SE, 267 in PL, 10 in LT). In Denmark there are already 10 sites utilizing dual-fuel technology with Diesel as pilot fuel (all operated by Deponigas ApS). The objective of this project is twofold; the production of green electricity and heat, which in itself contributes to GHG reduction if the corresponding use of fossil fuels is offset, and reduction of GHG gases by reduction of spontaneous methane emission from landfills and elimination of methane emissions from different types of off-gases. In addition, transforming indigenous low-quality gas streams into power and heat contributes to the security of supply and diversification of energy systems. Sixteen EU member states have already applied a landfill ban on organic material, and, as the gas production in landfills declines when no new organic material is landfilled, the methane level decreases and conventional CHP production using an Otto engine is no longer possible. The current procedure is to cover the landfill and install so-called bio-windows, where microbes oxidize the methane to carbon dioxide. However, methane content is only reduced, not eliminated, through the use of such bio-windows, and there is no guarantee that all the methane produced inside the landfill will pass a bio-window before entering the atmosphere. In addition, the energy contained within methane is not utilized. In this project three different options to use landfill gas and off-gases with low methane (<40%) content will be evaluated and benchmarked. The three technologies are developed in different countries, thus the need for international cooperation is evident. The landfill gas is extracted by suction and the negative pressure prevents the methane from escaping to the atmosphere. The project idea is well aligned with the EU Methane Strategy as part of the European Green Deal. The project will result in a decision support tool and recommendations for landfill gas operators and other parties dealing with off-gases containing methane, to minimize methane emissions and produce green power and heat.
