meta.title: Re-Farm - Resilient Farm-based Green Energy Communities

card.solution: The South Baltic region faces a new reality of overlapping crises that challenge both its economic stability and energy security. Environmental disasters, rising prices, and geopolitical tensions have revealed how dependent rural areas still are on centralised, fossil-based energy systems. Farms across Lithuania, Poland, Germany, and Sweden increasingly generate renewable energy from solar, biogas, or biomass, yet most lack the tools to store, manage, and share this energy effectively. Without smart storage and digital control, renewable systems remain fragile, leaving communities exposed to disruptions in energy supply and market instability. REFarm – Resilient Farm-based Green Energy Communities – addresses these shared regional challenges by turning agricultural areas into active players of the green energy transition. The project demonstrates how small-scale renewable systems on farms can be combined with smart-storage technologies and digital monitoring to improve self-sufficiency, dependability, and resilience during crises. REFarm shows that every kilowatt produced and stored locally strengthens regional stability and contributes to the South Baltic’s shift toward sustainable, crisis-ready energy systems. The project is structured in a clear and logical way, moving from analysis and mapping to piloting, modelling, and long-term adoption.It begins with a comprehensive assessment of renewable-energy potential, regulatory frameworks, and resilience conditions across Lithuania, Poland, Germany, and Sweden. This analytical phase lays the groundwork for identifying real challenges faced by farms and defining opportunities for smart storage, digital monitoring, and local energy cooperation. Building on these findings, the project then moves to practical demonstration. Selected farms in each country will test small-scale smart-storage systems and digital-monitoring technologies, providing real operational data and experience. These pilot actions will not only prove the technical feasibility of such systems but also show how they can maintain energy reliability during market disruptions, environmental shocks, or grid instability. Finally, the lessons and data from the pilot activities will be transformed into long-term solutions. The project will establish the South Baltic Green Energy Community Network, connecting farmers, clusters, and regional actors committed to energy resilience. It will also prepare a Community Model and Roadmap, translating tested practices into guidance for policy, training, and future replication across the region. Through this step-by-step process, REFarm connects technology, governance, and community engagement in one coherent framework. It equips farmers and regional stakeholders with practical tools — the SmartReFarm Green Energy Toolbox — to manage renewable energy more effectively, while also providing policymakers with concrete evidence to improve regional and national frameworks. The project’s added value lies in its strong cross-border partnership and in building directly on the experience of the previous BIOSOLFarm initiative, which successfully improved energy efficiency on farms across the South Baltic region. REFarm takes the next step, moving beyond energy efficiency towards smart storage, digital monitoring, and community-based renewable-energy systems that strengthen local resilience and cooperation. This capitalisation ensures that tested collaboration and trust among partners evolve into new, more advanced solutions that no single country could achieve alone. The results will enhance regional energy stability, reduce dependency on external supplies, and make renewable energy not only sustainable but truly reliable — turning South Baltic farms into pillars of green resilience and security.

meta.title: BalticGrow -Cross-border innovation for sustainable rooftop ecosystems in the south baltic region

card.solution: Cities in the South Baltic region are increasingly dealing with heavy rainfall, urban heat islands, and the need to reduce CO₂ emissions—challenges that no single municipality or institution can solve in isolation. The “BalticGrow” project addresses this common struggle by advancing green and blue-green roof solutions designed to improve stormwater management, lower rooftop and ambient temperatures, enhance local biodiversity, and, where possible, integrate renewable energy production (especially solar). Our overall objective is to create, test, and scale up a new generation of multi-functional green roofs across Denmark, Lithuania, Sweden, Poland, and Germany. By applying joint research and development, we will produce five key outputs—ranging from a feasibility study and technology roadmap to a tailor-made, IoT-based monitoring system. In doing so, we anticipate a tangible change: the widespread adoption of innovative green roofs that can help mitigate flooding, cool buildings, support pollinators, and potentially increase solar panel efficiency. Ultimately, our project aims to spark cross-border policy, business, and community interest in more resilient and eco-friendly urban landscapes. To achieve these goals, BalticGrow takes a multi-step approach: Research & Analysis: Using hydrological modeling, material testing (including biochar-enriched substrates), and integration techniques for PV panels, we develop evidence-based strategies tailored to the Baltic climate. Stakeholder Engagement: We involve local governments, energy utilities, building owners, and residents in pilot actions, ensuring that each rooftop reflects the needs and conditions of its host community. Pilot Installations & Monitoring: Three cross-border pilot sites in different climatic zones will implement and test our solutions. We use an IoT monitoring system for real-time data on moisture, temperature, and energy generation, allowing continuous improvement. Technology Catalogue & Scale-Up: Findings from pilots and consultations feed into a comprehensive, multi-lingual Technology Catalogue and Decision-Support Toolbox, enabling others to adopt these solutions in their own urban settings. A cross-border approach is essential because the region’s coastal and climatic conditions transcend national borders, and each partner brings complementary skills—for instance, hydrological modeling expertise in one country, advanced energy systems knowledge in another, and robust stakeholder networks elsewhere. By pooling these resources, BalticGrow accelerates innovation, avoids duplicated efforts, and ensures that our outputs meet diverse regulatory and environmental contexts. Our project is innovative in combining multiple functions—stormwater retention, thermal regulation, biodiversity enhancement, and solar energy—into a single rooftop system validated by real-time IoT monitoring. We also foster broad adoption through business models and policy recommendations that pave the way for green roofs to become a mainstream element of sustainable urban development. By uniting science, community engagement, and practical demonstrations, BalticGrow seeks to generate lasting environmental and economic benefits for cities throughout the South Baltic.

meta.title: PortSHAZ - Enhanced Eco-Efficient Cargo Operations

card.solution: The PortSHAZ project addresses the significant challenge of environmental hazards associated with dry bulk cargo operations in local and regional ports within the South Baltic Programme area. This challenge is crucial because it impacts marine ecosystems, water quality, and the overall health of coastal communities. Overall objective and expected change: The primary objective of PortSHAZ is to develop and implement best practices and innovative technical solutions to reduce dry bulk cargo leakage. This leakage is a prevalent issue that poses substantial environmental risks. The project aims to create a balance between operational efficiency and environmental stewardship in port operations, thereby contributing to sustainable maritime activities in the South Baltic region. The expected change is a notable reduction in environmental hazards from port operations, leading to healthier marine ecosystems and improved water quality. Outputs and results: - Comprehensive Research Report: A detailed analysis of existing best practices in dry bulk cargo handling and identification of gaps. - Innovative Technical Solutions: Development and pilot implementation of new technologies and methods to reduce cargo leakage and enhance environmental protection in port operations. - Regional Strategy and Guidelines: Creation of a comprehensive strategy and set of actionable recommendations for reducing cargo leakage and protecting the environment. - Knowledge Dissemination: Publication and sharing of findings, best practices, and technical advancements with a broader audience. Approach and need for cross-border collaboration: The project adopts a multi-pronged, collaborative approach involving a consortium of partners from various regions. A cross-border approach is crucial because maritime environmental hazards transcend national borders and require a coordinated regional response. By leveraging collective expertise, resources, and shared experiences, the project fosters stronger regional cooperation and ensures more effective and widely applicable solutions. Innovation and Originality: What sets PortSHAZ apart is its focus on niche yet critical aspects of maritime operations - specifically, the leakage of dry bulk cargo. The project is innovative in its approach to combining research, technical development, and regional strategy formulation. It stands out for its commitment to integrating environmental protection with operational efficiency in port operations, setting a new standard for sustainable maritime activities in the South Baltic region. This overview encapsulates the essence of the PortSHAZ project under the revised priority of the Interreg South Baltic Programme, highlighting its alignment with the program's objectives and its innovative approach to addressing a common regional challenge.

meta.title: Ecomarinas
meta.institution: City of Gdansk - Gdansk Sports Center

card.solution: The "Ecomarinas" project, in times of visible climate change, is a response to the deteriorating situation of the fauna and flora of the Baltic Sea. Every year, various types of harmful substances are discharged into the Baltic Sea, including sewage from vessels. This situation also affects the tributaries of the Baltic Sea, which are characterized by high levels of pollution (e.g. with plastics and chemicals) as well as progressive eutrophication. Recreational boating has been increasingly popular in the South Baltic Region. Sailing and motorboat trainings pay little to no attention to the environmental aspect of boating, therefore new members to the yachting community mostly learn and adapt habits of previous generations of sailors, and those leave much to be desired. Simultaneously, recreational boating sector’s attitudes and demeanors seem to go unnoticed when it comes to their environmental practices, especially unconcern when running yacht's bilge pump or wastewater pump. „Ecomarinas” project aims at improvement of water management in the marinas of South Baltic Region. Comprehensive actions will be taken to ensure that marinas can provide their customers with equipment and knowledge on how to perform their yacht-connected activities with no harm done to the environment. To this end, the project envisages a number of activities consisting in conducting comprehensive comparative analysis and research in order to identify potential solutions for the sustainable use of water in marina management. This research will serve as a basis for meeting the challenges facing marina managers and developing effective pollution prevention and freshwater saving methods. For this purpose, partnerships and cooperation, based on quadruple helix model, will be established, among others: with local governments, marina operators (private and public), research institutions and pro-ecological NGOs (incl. civil society). A number of study visits will be organized aimed at exchanging experiences and verifying the pro-ecological solutions used, collecting and analyzing the information obtained, which will allow defining current conditions, challenges and possible solutions in marinas. Therefore, activities under the Project are aimed at increasing knowledge and supporting activities in the field of effective and sustainable water management, including limiting discharge of nutrients and hazardous substances to the sea and the catchment areas of rivers connected to the Baltic Sea. The activities in the project are mostly focused on marina operators, since they are the ones who have the influence on marina's environmental policy. Marina administrators know their customers, their habits and therefore are able to reach them and do the groundwork, as well as set the marina's internal standards of water management. However, extensive awareness raising will also be included: general information on anthropogenic pressure and conservation of the Baltic Sea will be prepared not only for sailors and marina administrators, but also the general public. In order to ensure the possibility of leading by example, pilot investments will be implemented in partner marinas, including the innovative hazardous liquid installation, which will enable or simplify disposal of oil, grease or other substances that are harmful to the environment if discharged directly into the water. To facilitate and popularize implementing suggested changes, marina operators and other interested stakeholders will be familiarized with tools that shall come to life within the project, such as educational toolbox, self-assessment tool, or environmental risk management plan. All the joint efforts will be crowned with The Sustainable Sailing Infrastructure Forum in Gdańsk, an event that will provide space for exchange of information and experience for all stakeholders involved in marina operation.

meta.title: ISMA - Innovative solutions for sewage sludge management in small wastewater treatment plants.

card.solution: Aiming for 100% coverage of rural and urban areas with sanitary wastewater systems is necessary for protection soil and water in the South Baltic area. However, it increases the amount of wastewater flowing into the treatment plants (WWTPs). Most of these WWTPs operate as activated sludge technology. Together with an increase in the amount of incoming wastewater increases the amount of sewage sludge. Currently this is one of the most serious problems that requires environmentally friendly solutions. The lack of good solutions in this area causes that small WWTPs may become a secondary source of contamination surface waters. On the one hand, due to technological limitations or the lack of limits on nutrient concentrations, small WWTPS my discharged insufficiently treated wastewater, and on the other hand, it may release into the environment insufficiently stabilized waste from municipal wastewater treatment (contaminated sewage sludge). These are two areas that require special attention to conduct safe water and sewage management and reduce eutrophication in the Baltic Sea area. The common challenge is therefore the use, in small WWTPs, green technologies which will reduce the negative impact of pollution from wastewater and sewage management on the Baltic Sea area. The project uses the knowledge and experience of EUROSLAM and STEP. It extends the analysis undertaken there with new possibilities, in line with changing knowledge, law and market needs. Currently, it is expected to impose more stringent limits on the quality of treated wastewater than currently in force, including lower nitrogen concentrations. It is also planned to change management standards for sewage sludge disposal. Currently, the sludge is dewatered and most often used as fertilizer in agriculture. However, they are contaminated with for example PFAS, heavy metals and microplastics. Increasing environmental requirements probably will stop this practice. Therefore new, environmentally friendly, solutions in the field of sludge management are needed. As part of the project, wastewater and sewage sludge will be subjected to pilot and experimental processes and analyzes that will allow the development and implementation of best practices in wastewater, therein sewage sludge, management. This is important for reducing the discharge of nutrients and nutrients hazardous substances into river basins and the Baltic Sea. The aim of the project is to reduce pollutants discharged from wastewater and sewage sludge into the environment, testing innovative green technology solutions and learning best practices. A cross-border corporation with universities and sewage treatment plant owners will help achieve our goals. A cross-border approach based on joint activities, exchange of experiences and flow of knowledge between regions is necessary for effective operation. The project includes an innovative approach to: a) biogas production as green technology in small WWTPs (1. methane production from the organic compounds in sewage sludge and, 2. methane production from CO2 form biogas and hydrogen gas from electrochemical process used for heavy metals removal from sewage sludge), b) water-safe and eutrophication-limiting digestate management, i.e. waste generated after biogas production (1. production of biochar and its use in agriculture instead of artificial fertilizers and as a replacement for adsorbents for removing pollutants from water, 2. treatment of water generated during sewage sludge processing). These approaches allow to reduction the discharge of nutrients and hazardous substances into river basins. The project promotes sustainable water management and waste disposal in the context of reduction pollution in the Baltic Sea region.

meta.title: BALTWRECK - Preventing massive marine waters chemical pollution from the leaking wrecks and munition
meta.institution: Institute of Fluid-Flow Machinery Polish Academy of Sciences

card.solution: The project addresses combating various hazardous substances in the aquatic environment in order to increase safety and water quality. There are around 20 000 known military and civilian shipwrecks on the bottom of the Baltic Sea, ca 10% of them are a source of contamination by fuels or residues of dumped munitions. More than 80 years after II World War some of the rusty wrecks leaks their hazardous fuel (eg. cancerogenic pyrolysis oil from “Stuttgart” contaminated already 40 ha of Gdansk Bay). Other wrecks are close to their decomposition and need thorough inspection to evaluate the risk and real threat to the marine life and to the various economic activities at sea. Decisions regarding monitoring, cleaning, or activities in a vicinity of shipwrecks are extremely slow, since expensive and research-intensive studies are needed in each case. The BaltWreck consortium believes it is time to join forces of marine research institutions, maritime administrations and policy makers in the region to tackle this serious cross-border challenge in a methodological, efficient and internationally-concerted way. The BaltWreck objective is to contribute to reducing pollution of the Baltic Sea by hazardous fuel, munitions and other remains of shipwrecks by jointly developing, demonstrating and implementing wreck management methods. This includes developing: (1) efficient wrecks diagnostics methods, (2) in-situ remediation technologies for hazardous fuels from wrecks as well as munition and explosives, (3) testing the developed solutions in at least 3 pilot locations and (4) examining the toxicological risk for marine ecosystems caused by dumped munitions and hydrocarbon deposits. The recommendations for policy makers, local marine and cities administration will be formulated. The project aims to include municipalities located in vicinity of wrecks in the decision process, by raising awareness of decision makers and general public via a series of workshops and conferences, as well as public information campaign. Partners will focus on four key areas: 1.Policy Review of management strategies regarding Baltic wrecks and common strategies will be presented to SBR governments. Environment protection agencies, maritime administration, tourism administration as well as cultural heritage institutions will provide their point of views to the problem, and look for synergies and best practices 2.Risk Assessment & decision making Project will provide a set of methods for wreck sites examination. This will include technology development for non-invasive wreck inspection, 3D object reconstruction as well as an array of chemical and toxicological methods to record contamination risks. The tool for decision support will be developed, to interpret the collected data via artificial intelligence and to calculate risk levels 3.Remediation In-situ bioremediation technologies using dedicated external and autochthonic microbes for combatting fuel (possibly munition) pollutions will be developed. These technologies base on aerobic (using oxygen) and anaerobic (not using oxygen) microbial consortia. 4.Public Awareness The public knowledge of hazards related to wrecks and their pollution is low. The public and administration awareness will be increased by meetings, seminars and public campaigns pointing to public health and environmental risks related to hazardous and cancerogenic fuels and munitions chemicals (including TNT and other). Documentation will be prepared, which could be displayed in municipalities in vicinity of historical wrecks. The excelent project Partnership is slightly imbalanced as WWII wrecks are situated mainly along the Polish, German and Lithuanian coast, this is why potential Danish and Swedish partners showed only limited interest to join consortium (being already involved in other projects). Partners outside SBR arcrucial for project implementation. The partner budget was correlated to partners engagement in the project activities.

meta.title: Circular MuSe - Promoting circular economy approaches that increase the resource efficiency of municipal services

card.solution: The project Circular MuSe supports municipal utility companies & municipalities in the South Baltic area in applying circular economy approaches in their services for citizens. In this context, the specific goal is to increase resource efficiency by reducing their consumption of raw-materials and production of waste by re-using them within the supply chains of municipal services. The geographic focus is on both urban and rural areas. This shall be achieved in the following way: WP2. Creating a “South Baltic Knowledge Hub on Circular Municipal Services” for cross-border capacity building & knowledge transfer: An international network & pool of circular economy experts from research & education institutions is created. It jointly explores & appraises available pre-work and best practices, and compiles an open comprehensive catalogue of case studies and available solutions, incl. “knowledge agents” for circular municipal services that can provide deeper information. On this basis and in dialogue with practitioners, the CE experts elaborate modular curricula for education & mentoring programmes for municipal utility companies and municipalities in smaller cities & rural areas. WP3. Piloting new circular approaches to enrich the portfolio of available solutions: The pilots include either the elaboration of feasibility studies and the practical testing & evaluation of technical-organisational CE solutions in selected municipalities. They will focus on the re-use of raw materials within individual municipal services, re-use across sectoral municipal services, or the utilisation & processing of collected household or industrial waste for them. The pilot measures involve the development of new CE solutions or the adaption of existing circular solutions to the specific demands of municipal utility companies. Special attention will be paid to waste that occurs seasonal or periodically in the municipalities - sand from street sweepers after road maintainance (PL) and bottom sediment from rainwater basins (SE and DK - different approaches). The approaches & results are documented & added to the “South Baltic Knowledge Hub on Circular Municipal Services” (WP2). WP4. Rolling-out support measures for circular municipal service provision: Based on the jointly elaborated curricula (WP2), education courses will be offered that provide municipal utility companies and municipal decision-makers with basic knowledge on CE approaches & existing solutions for increasing the resource efficiency of municipal services. They include (online) seminars and study trips to best practices. Furthermore, mentoring programmes are launched to guide & support municipal utility companies in the development & operationalisation of circular municipal services. The CE experts from the involved research & education institutions will act as trainers and mentors. Associations of municipalities or municipal utilities will support the organisation and promotion of the offers. Furthermore, arenas for further, direct cross-border exchange of practitioners’ & researchers on the subject are created. Based on a partnership that comprises research & education institutions, municipal umbrella organisations and municipal utilities, therefore, Circular MuSe will address the identified barriers for the deployment of circular approaches for municipal services that increases their resource efficiency in targeted ways and a comprehensive manner.

meta.title: BePacMan - Better Paper Packaging Management

card.solution: The paper packaging materials are omnipresent and the problem became more emerging during the COVID-19 pandemic as it facilitated the consumers behavior and caused an increase in online, ecommerce and social media market. The average consumer collects several boxes per week which end up in the waste management facility. Imperfection and leakages in the segregation and collection systems result in only partial recovery of paper packaging and contamination of the portion that ends up in the paper recycling facilities resulting in higher cost and environmental impact of the recycling process. Instead of recycling, recovery and regeneration, the share of the reuse could be increased to reduce the environmental footprint of the life cycle. The BePacMan project focuses on extending the life cycles of paper packaging through cross-sector and cross-border approaches to reuse in the South Baltic region. The partner countries will develop sustainable concepts, solutions and business models for this purpose and for structurized support to SMEs. Strategic collaborations will be set and exchange of the ideas with important stakeholders such as e-commerce, logistics and waste management companies as well as technology providers and political decision-makers will take place. In this way, new economically and ecologically sustainable business models for the reuse of packaging are to be developed. The packaging should remain in its shape for as long as possible, thus avoiding the generation of paper waste by reusing the paper packaging to extend the life cycle of the packaging materials and thus facilitate the shift from linear to circular resource use. At the same time, the energy and water costs for processing the paper can be further optimized through recycling and climate-damaging emissions can be reduced. In order to achieve the EU-wide greenhouse gas reduction targets for 2030, stricter regulations and adjustments to climate protection laws will follow. The BePacMan project offers the opportunity to establish new concepts in order to support trade and industry in implementing their climate protection strategies by reducing their CO2 emissions, to adopt to new market situation and to take responsibility for the material by each actor involved in the life cycle of paper packaging. The challenge is to develop supply chains that either are reversible or can provide a resources for the next supply chains. This could be done by development and innovations in on demand packaging or returnable packaging systems. Existing procedures need to be adopted to the new approach and these solutions need optimization to be efficient and economically feasible taking into account diversity of the market conditions. The solutions developed within the project will enable the improvement of waste management system for authorities and contribute to transformation of business models in logistic, parcel and ecommerce businesses. Those stakeholders make a significant contribution to the life cycle of packaging and should be responsible and obliged to mitigate the footprint. Many of the companies operate in different countries, with different frameworks, cultures and consumer awareness. The goal is to help them adopt and to point out effective solutions, together with increasing social awareness, providing new ways for waste prezention and management and opportunities for additional savings on packaging for people, small sales companies and local stores. Thus project focuses on the paper packaging lifecycle involving on land transport, and the partnership is also focused on that area

meta.title: Mental and Sustainable Mindscapes - raising awareness & competences of benefits of intersecting mental wellbeing and environmentally friendly tourism in the SB region

card.solution: Mental and Sustainable Mindscapes - a cross-border initiative to improve quality of tourism facilities and offers. We recognize that mental and sustainable tourism is essential for the long-term health and prosperity of the Baltic Region, ensuring that tourism development is compatible with environmental conservation, cultural preservation, and community well-being. By embracing sustainability principles, the region can continue to attract visitors while safeguarding its natural and cultural treasures for future generations. We also recognize that certification can be a powerful tool for enhancing the competitiveness, sustainability, innovation and overall success of tourism offers and facilities, while also contributing to the satisfaction and well-being of guests, employees, and local communities. The Mental and Sustainable Mindscapes project aims to support tourism operators and facilities, NGOs, public organisations and decision makers in the coastal regions of Germany, Denmark, Sweden, Lithuania, and Poland to improve their awareness and practices. The project has a number of added values that stem from its cross-border approach and cooperation, e.g.: development of common standards and certification methodology, transfer of knowledge and experience, creating synergies and complementarities. The project involves partners and associated partners from Poland and Lithuania. The project objective is development and implementation of mental and sustainable tourism certification programme for the SB Region. The certification programme will include tools and methodology developed within the framework of cross-border cooperation. In the first stage, which is the subject of this application, we intend to develop, implement and test the common operating methodology and the online self-evaluation tool for target groups. Using them, we want to certify at least 10 operators and/or tourist facilities in Lithuania and Poland during the project period. The project starts with 3 partners and will be widened in following years. Then, after analyzing the project effects and implementing the necessary modifications, we plan to expand the network of certification points and implement the programme in other countries of the South Baltic Region. The certification programme will require businesses to undergo regular (to be agreed by the partners how often) assessments to maintain certification status. In this way, operators will be motivated to constantly maintain high quality and/or introduce new innovative solutions in the field of mental and sustainable tourism. The project is innovative and unique in several ways: - It is the first cross-border project that focuses on mental and sustainable tourism in Poland and Lithuania - It adopts a holistic and comprehensive approach that covers numerous aspects of mental and sustainable tourism, from awareness and education to assessment and certification. - It creates a common brand and a certification scheme that can be recognized and trusted across the region and beyond. - It involves a diverse and partners that bring together expertise and experience from different sectors and domains. Despite high potential, mental tourism is still not very popular in Poland and Lithuania. For instance, none of the Lithuanian nor Polish tourism businesses has been ever included in the TOP 100 Green Destinations. https://www.greendestinations.org/home/what-we-do/solutions-for-travellers/top-100-2023-destination-stories/

meta.title: Horse tourism for everyone - Fostering inclusive & citizen-oriented horse tourism development in the South Baltic area

card.solution: Horse tourism provides considerable potentials to foster a more sustainable, resilient & inclusive tourism development in the South Baltic area (SBA): > It is a nature based & eco-friendly form of recreation that can make scenic nature (e.g. forests) and protected areas (e.g. Geoparks, nature reserves) accessible in sustainable ways. > Horse tourism is a growing segment (+5% horse riders / year) that takes typically place in rural area and an all-year round activity. Thus, it can help to prolong the tourism season and to create non-seasonal income possibilities in remote & economically weak parts of the SBA. > Equestrian tourism is based on livestock-thta has to be kept whole year. This creates opportunities for creating offers for inhabitant that directly improve their quality of life & well-being, in particular off-season (e.g. leisure activities for local children & adults). Equestrianism, therefore, is an outstanding potential for a citizen-oriented tourism development, which aims at benefits for inhabitants beyond income possibilities. Although equestrianism finds very favourable pre-conditions in the SBA (e.g. scenic landscape, attractive offers for beginners, close to tourism hotspots, attractive PoIs), the region lags behind international “champion destinations” (e.g. Brandenburg / DE) in terms of the intensity & benefits of equestrianism. The main reasons for this are: > Coordinated efforts to develop horse tourism are rare. Equestrian tourism providers largely left on their own, and lack support from the public side in particular. > The horse trail infrastructure in the SBA is partly outdated & not tailored to destination assets (e.g. no scenic routing, no connections to PoIs). > Equestrian offers that specifically address potentials for a sustainable, resilient & inclusive tourism development are missing (e.g. off-season packages, activities for inhabitants). > Equestrianism is perceived as “exclusive” leisure activity. This limits market potentials, and use of equestrian offers by inhabitants for well-being & quality of life. Against this background, the project turns the SBA into an inclusive all-year-round horse tourism destination. This will be achieved by supporting tourism providers in the creation & promotion of innovative offers that make equestrianism accessible to wider groups of visitors & inhabitants. Activities include: > WP 2: NETWORK BUILDING set ups up regional partnerships for inclusive & citizen-oriented horse tourism development, and connects them for exchange & joint actions. > WP 3: INFRASTRUCTURE UPGRADE involves the piloting & roll out of next-gen horse trails for more multi-faceted equestrian experiences (“trails with a view” in scenic landscapes, trails with stops at PoIs). > WP4: PRODUCT INNOVATION launches innovative horse tourism offers that open new target groups (e.g. horse walks for company teams), prolong the season (e.g. “horses & culinary” packages for silver agers) or tailored to inhabitants (e.g. daily yoga hours with horses). > WP5: REPOSITIONING launches a joint marketing campaign to change the “exclusive” image of equestrianism among both visitors & inhabitants, and to promote the SBA as inclusive “horse tourism destination for everybody”. The activities are implemented in five partner regions in PL, LT, SE, DK & DE, which turn into forerunners that jointly create models for potential followers in the SBA. The partnership comprises local & regional authorities, DMOs and innovative equestrian SMEs, which are supported by further APs (incl. equestrian SMEs, network organisations, best practice regions). The project, therefore, combines experiences from all 5 SBA countries for an innovative, integrated & joint approach to strengthen horse tourism in the SBA, which widens the group of visitors & inhabitants engaging with horses and uses equestrianism to improve quality of life of citizens beyond income possibilities.

meta.title: AIMused - Accessibility Integration and Artificial Intelligence for Museums

card.solution: The AIMused project addresses a common challenge in the SBR: the limited accessibility and inclusivity in tourism attractions for people with disabilities, senior citizens, and individuals with special needs. As demographic changes progress, the tourism industry must adapt to ensure that all visitors can fully engage with exhibitions and narratives. However, many attractions still struggle to implement inclusive solutions due to a lack of knowledge, resources, and technological support. This gap limits the participation of a significant portion of the population and prevents tourism sites from becoming fully open and welcoming spaces for diverse audiences. The overall objective of AIMused is to improve tourism attractions accessibility through the development and implementation of AI-driven tools and inclusive design solutions. The project will enable such institutions to provide an enhanced experience for visitors with various needs by integrating artificial intelligence into interactive tools. By increasing inclusivity, AIMused will foster a more diverse audience, ensuring that people with disabilities, seniors, and those with cognitive or sensory impairments can participate in the cultural, environmental and educational opportunities that tourism attractions offer. This may lead to a long-term change in the way museums, zoos, science centers, etc operate, setting a new standard for accessibility in tourism. The project will deliver four key outputs. Two types of guidelines that compile best practices, research findings, conclusions, and recommendations to enhance accessibility in cultural and tourism sites.They will be themselves designed with care of plain language and universal design principles. The first guideline will provide a broad perspective on accessibility in tourist attractions, presenting a detailed framework for inclusive design, the use of assistive technologies, and effective communication methods tailored to diverse visitor needs. The second guideline will focus on the implementation of AI-powered chatbots in tourism attractions, providing insights into their development, user needs, and practical applications to improve visitor satisfaction and engagement. These documents will serve as essential resources for cultural and nature institutions, helping them implement AI-driven solutions and accessibility improvements based on tested methodologies and wide cross-border research. Additionally, the project will develop toolboxes with physical and digital tools, to enhance visitor interaction, incorporating tactile models, 3D-printed replicas, and AI-based tools. Training materials and workshops will support museum staff and tourism professionals in applying these solutions, ensuring long-term impact. Publications and industry reports will further disseminate the project’s outcomes, facilitating knowledge transfer and the replication of successful strategies across the sector and region. AIMused will take a cross-border approach by bringing together tourism experts, accessibility specialists, and AI developers from all countries in the SBR. This cross-sectoral group will be large and diverse, thanks to the establishment of local Advisory Boards, which will support the project with their expert knowledge. This collaboration is essential because accessibility challenges in tourism are not limited to one country but affect the entire region. By working together, project partners can compare best practices, exchange knowledge, and co-develop solutions that can be adaptable to various cultural and linguistic contexts. Cross-border cooperation will also allow for extensive testing and validation of the developed tools with diverse user groups, ensuring that they are effective and widely applicable. Through this joint effort, AIMused will create sustainable, scalable solutions that can be adopted by tourism attractions across the region, ultimately making cultural and natural heritage more accessible to all.

meta.title: Youth Mental Health Alliance
meta.institution: Municipal Family Support Center in Gdansk

card.solution: Adolescence is a unique and formative time. Physical, emotional and social changes can make adolescents vulnerable to mental health problems. Stereotypically, childhood and youth are identified with the period of the greatest carefreeness and happiness. This is also the message of many marketing content. However, the statistics are alarming. For example, 17 percent of second-grade primary school students in Poland, when describing their emotions and mood last week, indicated a sense of sadness - according to a study conducted in 2022 commissioned by the Polish Ombudsman for Children. 29 percent of sixth-grade students referred to the same emotion, and as many as 32% referred to the poor condition discouraging them from being active. When it comes to secondary schools and technical schools, as many as 49 percent admitted to this type of apathy. They also indicated that they were overwhelmed by problems (45%) or felt that they were fed up with everything (44%). School stress levels in 2021 were at their highest in years. Since 2016, the level of stress experienced by students (especially among girls) has only increased. Unfortunately the similar situation is presented in The report, titled “Governance of the Service Delivery Chain for Youth Mental Health in Lithuania”. Report notes that in 2018, 24 percent of Lithuanian students in grades one to nine thought about suicide, 40 percent experienced low levels of psychological well-being, and 24 percent experienced bullying. Now, after the COVID-19 pandemic, the share of students experiencing severe psycho-emotional difficulties is at 20 percent compared to 14 percent before. In Denmark, mental health issues and mental illnesses are also highly prevalent among children and adolescents, and numbers have increased in recent years. This is according to a survey in a recent Danish report (Knowledge Council for Prevention: “Mental health and illness in children and adolescents aged 10-24 – prevalence, development and possibilities for prevention”, 2020). The number of 10-24-year-olds who are diagnosed with mental illness such as anxiety, depression, eating disorders, ADHD and autism, has increased over the last 20-30 years. 15 % of children and adolescents in Denmark are diagnosed with mental illness before the age of 18, and the number has increased for all categories of mental illness. Report „Mental well-being, mental distress and mental disorder among children and young adults, published by Swedish Research Council in 2021 present that also in Sweden the percentage of children and adolescents aged 11 to 15 years who state that they feel nervous or depressed almost every day has at least doubled since measurements began in the mid-1980s. Despite difficulties in that area parents, schools and other institutions often are not prepared to support children and youth in their problems. Public institutions operate in silos - they do not go beyond the scope of their tasks, there are no procedures that generate cooperation with other entities in order to solve a common problem. Schools, most of which employ psychologists, lack contacts with other services. Sometimes a phone call between 2 civil servants is enough to prevent serious consequences. We need to undertake interdisciplinary actions as we implement good practices from other countries to make a significant change in this area. Another problem is that mental health support systems within partner countries are unified – they are subject to the same laws and duplicate similar procedures and operating patterns. Therefore, their problems and challenges are also similar. This limits the space for possible inspiration and innovation. We believe that exposure to systems operating in other countries, under different rules, will be an opportunity to "step outside the box" and maybe find a key change factor.

meta.title: BRIDGE - Cultural and tourism education as a bridge for cross-border cooperation, networking and developing relationships with new partners

card.solution: The idea of the project partnership is a response to the current situation faced by many Polish organisations/institutions conducting cooperation with Russia, which was severed after the aggression against Ukraine. LP, as the lead partner in 2004-2021, has actively cooperated with Russia in the framework of several cross-border projects, to which it has also invited PP1, Warmińsko-Mazurskie Voivodeship, and the Municipality of Olsztyn. The concept of setting up the LP stemmed from the firm belief shared by the founding communes that promoting a single castle or a single town would never be as successful as promoting many castles located on a common Trail (about 750 km) leading through: Bytów, Lębork, Człuchów, Malbork, Sztum, Gniew, Kwidzyn, Nowe, Ostróda, Nidzica, Działdowo, Olsztyn, Lidzbark Warmiński, Kętrzyn, Giżycko. The Gothic Castles Trail was awarded Certificate of the Polish Tourist Organization in the competition for the Best Tourist Product 2022. LP and PP1 are organisations affected by the suspension of cross-border cooperation programmes with Russia and are therefore looking for new partners from the South Baltic area (SBA) in the field of regional, historical education of children and young people. LP intends to pass its experience and knowledge gained in Polish-Russian relations (e.g. live history lessons/knowledge competitions for pupils) to new partnerships from the Interreg South Baltic Programme countries. For the first time, the LP will cooperate with PP2 known for Hovdala Castle (100,000 visitors per year) and surrounding areas in the region - Wanås Castle, Bäckaskog Castle. The Partner also has a rich offer of history lessons in the castle. For the first time, the LP will also cooperate with PP3 dealing with, among other things, cultural education and tradition. The Cultural and Historical Museum in Rietavas, Giliogiris Manor, Cold War Museum in Plunge, among others, are located in the PP3 area. The project will be a test of new partnerships and a training platform for all PPs. The project will also respond to the need to define the goods and culture of the SBA as attractive, worth knowing and recommending by young people using means and tools used by this age group. The project will aim to: a. building cross-border cooperation and finding cross-border partners for local entities affected by the suspension of cross-border cooperation programmes with Russia, including partners from the Olsztyński subregion; b. to increase the capacity and skills for international cooperation among diverse partners and stakeholders to address common cross-border issues; c. to build up cooperation networks and empower children and young people as creators and consumers of cultural heritage of the SBA. It includes the following WP1: strengthening the cross-border cooperation in cultural education of young people and new Partners with activities: 6 study visits of young bloggers/influencers to Partners countries (2 visits to each country) with the results: articles/films/posts/rolls on blog/social media; 1 history and landscape knowledge digital competition for pupils in PL, LT, SE, - the competition will culminate in the presentation of at least 50 best works on a shared interactive map produced by LP with links to the websites of the PPs; 3 meetings of employees engaged in the culture/education/tourism industries in PL, LT, SE on topics how to alive sites to attract young inhabitants of the SBA. A novelty will be the use of LP’s organisational and content-related potential acquired in Polish-Russian projects for the benefit of PP2, PP3. The implementation of the project activities will be based on the experience and expectations of youth and young people as creators and recipients. The results of the project will be made available to Polish municipalities in the Olsztyński subregion, which have no partner in the Interreg South Baltic Programme countries e.g. Olsztyn, Nidzica, Lidzbark Warmiński, Kętrzyn.

meta.title: Comprehensive Cross-Border Initiative for Early Diagnosis and Holistic Support for FAS

card.solution: Alcohol use during pregnancy is a medical, psychosocial and sociological problem worldwide. Following recommendation of WHO about global alcohol action plan for 2022–2030 to minimalize the harmful use of alcohol including the reduce of prenatal alcohol exposure, we propose the project FASD-Bridge. Maternal alcohol consumption during pregnancy often causes damage to the unborn child. Prenatal alcohol exposure can cause growth abnormalities, craniofacial, cardiac, renal, osseous and ocular malformations, developmental, cognitive and behavioural disorders as well as limitations in partial performance and thus global limitations in everyday life. The center part of the current project is developing stronger links between research institutions and public entities across Baltic context by promoting regional cooperation and boosting knowledge, transfer of know-how and merging the best practices to strengthen the implementation of the global strategy in terms of individuals with Fetal Alcohol Syndrome (FAS) and Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD) and their families (biological, foster, adoptive). There is a need to focus more on the issue of alcohol consumption during pregnancy and on its consequences as well as to support families raising individuals with FAS and FASD in South Baltic Region. Key components: Building a network of cooperation: establishment of an international network of interdisciplinary experts, transfer of developed solutions to institutions involved in family care in partner countries. Jointly achieved increase in social awareness and professional education: information campaigns targeting medical and social care staff, training and workshops for those involved in the care of pregnant women and children, publication of project results in scientific journals and local media. Epidemiology in the Region and early diagnosis of FAS/FASD: harmonization of guidelines and definitions for FAS/FASD, assessment of regional prevalence of FAS/FASD in partner countries, development of awareness-raising tools (educational materials, social media campaigns), design and implementation of training programs for professionals (doctors, midwives, pediatricians) Support for families with children with FAS/FASD in the Region: analysis of the needs of families raising individuals with FAS/FASD (surveys, focus groups), development of a family support model, considering different family structures (adoptive, foster), pilot implementation of the support model in partner countries and its evaluation Scaling up: Jointly developed solutions, tools, methodologies, and practices will be standardized and made adaptable for other regions and countries, ensuring scalability. Partner institutions will collaborate with other national and international organizations to expand the reach of the FAS/FASD prevention, diagnosis, and support programs.Training programs for professionals and support systems for families will be rolled out on a larger scale through partnerships with health institutions, schools, and social organizations. Durability: The guidelines, support models, and educational materials will remain accessible to stakeholders, ensuring continued use after the project ends. The solutions will be embedded into healthcare, social care, and educational systems of partner countries, guaranteeing long-term impact. The international network of experts established during the project will foster ongoing collaboration, innovation, and knowledge exchange. The Consortium consists of 4 Regular Partners and 3 Associated Partners RP: • University of Gdansk (Poland) – LEADER • Departament of Neonatology and Pediatric Intensive Care, University Hospital Greifswald (Germany) • Klaipeda University Hospital (Lithuania) • “For the Family” Foundation (Poland) AP: • Swedish FAS Association (Sweden) • „Children for future” (NGO, Denmark) • Pomorskie Voivodeship / Regional Center for Social Policy of the Marshal's Office

meta.title: D-EFFECT- CIVIC SOCIETY DEMOCRACY LESSONS, BRINGING A YOUTH PERSPECTIVE IN THE EU POLICYMAKING AT ALL LEVELS IN LINE WITH YOUTH STRATEGY 2022-2027
meta.institution: Association of Polish Communes Euroregion Baltic

card.solution: The D-EFFECT is a need-driven project that is oriented to enable exchange and initiate better collaboration between cross-border stakeholders and local youth environment participants (which differ in scale and represent different approaches from bottom-up and top-down) in areas such areas as democracy, human and civil rights, political systems, and how young people can impact society. The project focused on development collaboration, based on various backgrounds, from 5 South Baltic countries, on the creation of a cross-border network – a „community of practice” that will design, test, and evaluate innovative solutions of Cross-Border Youth Democratic Festivals (CB YDF). This will be the first time that this measure will be adopted at a local scale, but also has a transnational character. This method will be adapted to local possibilities and needs of South Baltic cities and municipalities around a common challenge which is the slow abandonment of democratic values by young people. At the same time, it is vital to broaden the participants’ knowledge of the European Union - its structure and organization, history, and present and future values. The D-effect project promotes the cooperation of youth-oriented stakeholders in the SB Area and contributes to building the problem-solving capabilities of 21 stakeholders (9 project partners and 9 associated organizations from 5 countries: SE, DK, DE, PL, LT). Thus, it adds a new element to capabilities of better youth participation, engagement, and increased education of democratic values that can make local societies more sustainable and resilient and the entire region a more youth-friendly place. The key actors are local authorities, representatives of the youth environment, and the youth itself as target beneficiaries, for most of which the topic is still a novelty. D-effect will supply them with knowledge and tools to develop strategic approaches and implement concrete measures that bring democratic and EU values into local and regional practice. The capacity-building process involves a transnational peer learning process. Local youth supporting entities/ organizations from SBA will be assisted by R&D institutions/domain experts and co-create: (1) Local engagement and activism strategies for selected model regions that combine measures for (a) civic participation (b) democratic and EU values engagement (c) promoting multisectoral stakeholder & youth acceptance, understanding, and long-lasting cooperation. (2) A set of complementary pilot measures for democratic engagement and dialogue that depict typical use cases, and that adapt, test, and validate concrete solutions for the transferability of experiences in the SBA which will enable of participation of a wide range of stakeholders. The results are processed into a “D-Effect Toolbox” which will be promoted and disseminated by the newly established “SB Youth-oriented Helpdesk”, which will serve local communities with experience and support. It gives other local authorities, and youth specialists concrete guidance on how to foster youth policies/actions and is pro-actively & widely disseminated to them. The project will put into practice the local perspective of new methods and tools of democracy promotion based on democracy festivals as open platforms that unite different actors, groups, experiences, and dimensions. Based on the assumption that democracy is more than democratic institutions and written rules, but a culture to be nurtured by creating spaces and platforms where people can physically meet, talk to each other, get inspired, exchange opinions, and debate their ideas. D-effect turned towards networking activities at the local level. In this regard, steered towards the practical dimension of building engagement with different communities, and foster active civic engagement, a culture of discussion, and critical thinking in response to the alarming rise of authoritarianism and nationalism.

meta.title: BIOCHAR4SBR - Empowering Cooperation and Capacity for Sustainable Biochar in the South Baltic Region

card.solution: The BIOCHAR4SBR project unites farmers, municipalities, SMEs, NGOs and educational bodies from across the South Baltic Region to learn, exchange and cooperate around biochar — a practical solution linking rural development, climate action and circular economy goals. Biochar serves both as a technical topic and a cooperation platform, helping partners explore how it improves soil, valorises organic waste, captures carbon and reduces pollution, while building the trust, skills and governance capacity needed for effective cross-border collaboration. The project focuses on small local actors and newcomers to international cooperation — farmers, cooperatives, rural SMEs, community-based organisations and NGOs. Many already experiment with biochar for soil improvement or waste valorisation but lack experience, networks and procedural knowledge to scale their efforts. BIOCHAR4SBR helps them overcome these barriers through peer-learning visits, mentoring tandems, and hands-on demonstrations. Participants gain both technical understanding of biochar and practical cooperation competences such as communication, partnership building and project design, preparing them for future Interreg or Horizon Europe initiatives. Local and regional authorities — municipalities, development agencies and advisory bodies — are key to scaling up sustainable rural practices but often lack participatory tools to involve citizens and small organisations. By taking part in mapping, governance dialogues and policy workshops, they will learn to translate biochar innovation into community-driven local development actions. This process strengthens institutional capacity, transparency and inclusion, ensuring that local governments can manage and sustain cross-border cooperation beyond the project. Civil-society organisations and clusters act as bridges between practitioners, policymakers and citizens. Their involvement in awareness campaigns, challenge labs and exchange events promotes inclusive decision-making and strengthens the culture of cross-border cooperation. By embedding gender equality, youth engagement and community participation into environmental activities, the project ensures that the green transition is socially just and inclusive. Educational and intermediary institutions — such as vocational schools, innovation hubs and development centres — will serve as multipliers of knowledge, integrating biochar-related content and cooperation methods into future training and development programmes. This guarantees the continuity and long-term use of project outcomes, supporting capacity building across the region. Citizens, youth groups and rural communities will join outreach events and open demonstrations, directly experiencing the environmental and economic value of biochar. Their participation transforms sustainability concepts into tangible local actions, fostering a shared South Baltic identity built on cooperation, learning and innovation. By connecting these complementary actors, BIOCHAR4SBR creates a living cross-border network centred on biochar — where learning about soil, carbon and circular practices naturally develops cooperation capacity, strengthens governance and fosters durable partnerships. The project builds multi-level capacity, from individual skills to institutional procedures, enhancing the region’s ability to collaborate effectively on environmental and social challenges.
